    Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss remarked: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”.

    In a recent development, another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so vital to this club over the last seven years.

    It has been revealed that martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

    In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

    If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

    The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

    Industry observers note that odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

    Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

    Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

    Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

    "Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T.

    After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

    Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

    "I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W.

    On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a upcoming chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

    He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

    His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he noted.

    It has been revealed that “The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”.

    It has been revealed that arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s fresh manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

    In a recent development, riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

    The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

    It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

    "I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w.

    New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

    Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

    Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF.

    Industry observers note that as Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh glitch.

    Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

    🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA.

    To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

    The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

    Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

    “Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”.

    Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

    Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy.

    Sources indicate that good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a upcoming season. A classic Arteta-ism.

    The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without newly introduced £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

    Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

    “In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta mentioned. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”.

    Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

    It has been revealed that “We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”.

    It has been revealed that this is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Roku Channel's new Christmas movie, Second Chance Holiday, premiered last Thursday, starring an actress in her first leading role: Ayesha Curry. The wife of Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has 20 acting credits on IMDB, but has never headlined a movie before, and with that new stature has come criticism.

    Arenas claimed that Curry speaks to other men via direct messages on social media because "she needs the attention because he doesn't give her the attention because he's focused," alluding to previous comments Curry made about having "zero male attention.".

    Former NFL running back LeSean McCoy also cited that conversation in criticizing Curry. "This is crazy. You got one of the greatest players of all time as your husband," McCoy stated on Speakeasy. "I've seen a while ago where she keeps saying how she wants more attention, and how girls throw themselves at him and she still just wants to feel like she's wanted… now you want us to see kissing a dude?… This is crazy.".

    On Wednesday, Stephen Curry addressed the comments with a video on Instagram.

    According to recent reports, "Nick, Gil, Emmanuel and anybody else who feels the need to jump in and give an opinion on something you don't really know about, something that kind of speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they're allowed and what they're not allowed to do," Curry mentioned. "Given the ignorance around how acting works, obviously I tried to laugh this one off but something needs to be said. Anytime Ayesha Curry demonstrates up in your headline, kindly suggest that you just give the happy hands, the congratulations, and maybe the apology can be as loud as when y'all leading y'all shows with this topic.".

    Both Young, a former teammate of Curry's with the Warriors, and Arenas apologized Wednesday. "You my dog. I love you. If I stated anything, I apologize like a man. I'm sorry," Young said.

    "I'm sorry if he's offended; I didn't mean it like that. I was just saying, he's such a perfect dude," Arenas added, saying that Curry had never drawn controversy himself, but if someone in the family had, it was Ayesha.

    NBA superstars are used to negativity from pundits, but commentary about their family is another matter. What Ayesha Curry does as an actress in a movie says nothing about her family or her husband's place in the basketball world. It's rare that Stephen Curry would address comments like this, but aside from the offense he and his family took, he was at least able to use it as a promotional opportunity.

    "Appreciate the free pub, thank you for giving a nice shout-out to Second Chance Holiday," he stated at the end of his video.

    Rossi descrive così le priorità del presidente quando iniziò a lavorare alla Lazio: «Io ho avuto un presidente che non sapeva neanche se il pallone era rotondo o quadrato, quindi il suo obiettivo quando sono arrivato era risanare il bilancio e non mi ha chiesto neanche come giocassi, 4-3-3, 4-4-2, 3-5-2, che giocatori volessi, anche perché non c'avevamo soldi, quindi dovevamo prendere i giocatori che potevano capitare per cui il suo problema era quanto guadagnassi».

    Alla domanda sul peso dell’ingaggio nella scelta dell’allenatore, Rossi risponde: «Se guadagnavo poco potevo essere un buon allenatore, se guadagnavo di più si rivolgeva da altre parti».

    It has been revealed that accanto al ricordo delle difficoltà economiche, Rossi esprime un giudizio netto sul lavoro societario di Lotito: «Ma devo dire che dal punto di vista societario ha fatto un lavoro incredibile alla Lazio perché ha risanato il bilancio. Noi eravamo una squadra che i giocatori-scommessa li dovevamo vendere per fare delle altre scommesse».

    L’ex allenatore distingue le capacità del presidente dal rapporto personale: «Lotito è sicuramente una persona molto capace, intelligente e come carattere magari se dovevo andare a cena preferivo andarci con altri presidenti e non con lui».

    #26953. Bob Boone, All-Star catcher, 1980 World Series champion and father of Yankees manager, dies at 78

    📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (766 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Bob Boone, All-Star catcher, 1980 World Series champion and father of Yankees manager, dies at 78

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, bob Boone, a four-time All-Star catcher and the middle member of a three-generation baseball family, has died.
    • According to recent reports, my dad- He was my mentor, my coach, my rock.
    • "Bob Boone had an enduring impact on the field as a 19-year MLB veteran, a seven-time Gold Glove Award-winning catcher, a four-time All-Star and 1980 World Champion with the Philadelphia Phillies," the MLB Players Association said in a statement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, bob Boone, a four-time All-Star catcher and the middle member of a three-generation baseball family, has died. He was 78. His son, Bret Boone, made the announcement on Tuesday. No cause of death was given.

    According to recent reports, my dad- He was my mentor, my coach, my rock. He taught me how to be a pro and more importantly, how to be a man. He was one of the highest integrity people I’ve ever known and I’m going to miss him dearly. Baseball lost a great one yesterday. R.I.P dad, I love you❤️ pic.twitter.com/4NtYAwXIv3.

    "Bob Boone had an enduring impact on the field as a 19-year MLB veteran, a seven-time Gold Glove Award-winning catcher, a four-time All-Star and 1980 World Champion with the Philadelphia Phillies," the MLB Players Association said in a statement. "He embraced a leadership role in the Players Association early in his career, and earned a reputation as a strong and principled voice in the advancement of player rights in the 1970s and '80s ... As we honor Bob's legacy and mourn his passing, we extend our heartfelt condolences to his wife, Sue, sons Aaron, Bret and Matt, his extended family, and his many fans and admirers throughout the game.".

    According to recent reports, the Boones were baseball's first three-generation family. Bob's father, Ray Boone, played for six teams from 1948-60, and his sons Aaron and Bret both had long careers spanning the 1990s and 2000s. Bob's other son, Matt, played in the minor leagues.

    It has been revealed that "I'm just so grateful that I had a dad that took us to work with him all the time," Aaron, now manager of the Newly introduced York Yankees, said in 2023 (via MLB.com). "He came up at the end of '72, and I was born in the spring of '73. He played until my senior year in high school and literally I was at the ballpark -- my brothers and I, in unis, shagging (fly balls) and doing everything you could possibly imagine. It was a great way to grow up.".

    Born in San Diego, Bob Boone made his MLB debut with the Phillies in 1972 and took over as the club's starting catcher in 1973. He hit 10 home runs and finished third in the National League Rookie of the Year voting. That started a 17-year run as one of the game's best and most durable catchers. Boone started at least 130 games behind the plate eight times in his career and 110 games 14 times.

    With the Phillies in 1980, Boone went 7 for 17 (.412) with four walks and zero strikeouts in Philadelphia's six-game World Series win over the Kansas City Royals.

    Recent findings suggest that A seven-time Gold Glove winner, including four straight during his age-38 to -41 seasons, Boone had his most productive years with the Phillies from 1976-79. He hit .282/.351/.414 those four seasons and averaged nine home runs, which was excellent output given the offensive standard at the catcher position during that era. Boone went to four All-Star Games and received MVP votes twice.

    "Bob was an incredible player, teammate and family man," the Phillies mentioned in a statement. "He embodied everything we believe exemplary athletes should represent, both on and off the field. We were proud to have him as part of the Phillies family during one of the most historic runs in team history. His impact on our organization, his teammates, and everyone who had the privilege of knowing him will never be forgotten.".

    Sources indicate that boone ranks second with 2,161 games at catcher during the Modern Era (since 1900), behind only Hall of Famer Ivan Rodriguez (2,377). He is 15th among primary catchers with 1,838 hits and 21st with 2,508 total bases. Boone played parts of 19 massive league seasons with the Phillies (1972-81), California Angels (1982-88), and Royals (1989-90).

    The Orlando SunRays, a potential expansion franchise, hired Boone to be their manager soon after he retired as a player, though the expansion franchises were instead awarded to Denver and Miami in 1991. Boone later managed the Royals from 1995-97 and the Cincinnati Reds (2001-03). He managed his son, Aaron, those years with the Reds.

    In 2005, Boone joined the Washington Nationals as their director of player development and had a hand in building the core that won the franchise's first World Series title in 2019. He remained with the Nationals until 2021. Boone spent five years on the Hall of Fame ballot from 1996 to 2000 but was not voted into Cooperstown.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This is an important week on the baseball calendar.
    • Also, the GM Meetings are this week in Las Vegas.
    • We've already ranked the top 50 free agents and the top 25 trade candidates.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This is an important week on the baseball calendar. First and foremost, it is awards week. Kevin McGonigle and Sal Stewart were named the Rookies of the Year on Monday. The Managers of the Year will be revealed Tuesday, Cy Youngs and Relievers of the Year will be announced Wednesday, and finally the MVPs will be announced Thursday.

    Also, the GM Meetings are this week in Las Vegas. The GM Meetings are not the Winter Meetings in terms of the sheer volume of rumors and transactions, but they do usually provide some news. There could be more than usual this year given the near certainty of a lockout on Dec. 1, which would also mean there are no Winter Meetings. This may be the only time everyone is in the same room this winter. The three weeks between now and Dec. 1 could be quite active.

    We've already ranked the top 50 free agents and the top 25 trade candidates.

    With that in mind, here are Tuesday's hot stove rumors.

    In a recent development, the Mets have a meeting scheduled with two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the clear top free agent avaiable this offseason, later this week, reports the New York Post. Skubal will meet with teams in California, presumably at the offices of agent Scott Boras. Owner Steve Cohen is expected to push for Skubal, according to SNY; president of baseball operations David Stearns has long been reluctant to sign big-money, long-term deals for pitchers, though pitchers of Skubal's caliber are rarely available. The Mets are also seeking first base help and bullpen reinforcements.

    Industry observers note that nolan McLean and Christian Scott are the only locks for Newly introduced York's 2027 rotation at the moment. Justin Hagenman, Sean Manaea, Kodai Senga, Zac Thornton, and Jonah Tong are next in line to make starts. Tylor Megill is expected back from Tommy John surgery early next year as well. The Mets have some depth but clearly need more impact.

    In a recent development, the Rangers signed Corey Seager to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season and it paid off quite handsomely with a World Series title in 2023 (Seager was the World Series MVP). With five years and roughly $155 million left on the deal, however, the Rangers appear ready to trade him.

    The Rangers "intend to explore moving Seager at the general managers' meetings," reports The Athletic.

    Recent findings suggest that seager, 32, was stellar from 2023 to 2025 in spite of a litany of injuries, averaging 6.2 WAR per season with a .294 average and 158 OPS+. He actually averaged 8.7 WAR per 162 games. Only the injuries kept him from making multiple serious MVP runs. Last season, though, was a step back. In 102 games, he hit .227/.312/.424 with 20 home runs, 51 RBI and 3.1 WAR.

    The injury history keeps getting more extensive, too, as he's dealt with injuries to his thumb, hamstring, hip, other hamstring and back in the last four years.

    With a lackluster, at best, shortstop class in free agency, now might be the perfect time for the Rangers to move on from Seager, assuming a deal can be worked out with the years and dollars left on his contract. Texas also has Sebastian Walcott, one of the top prospects in baseball, ready in the wings.

    In a recent development, the Blue Jays are among the teams with interest in free agent second baseman Brandon Lowe, according to Sportsnet. Ernie Clement, Toronto's primary second baseman in 2026, crashed hard in the second half and has always fit better as a super utility man who plays regularly at different positions. Josh Smith is the team's other second base option.

    It has been revealed that lowe would bring needed power to a team that finished dead last in home runs this past season and had just one player, Kazuma Okamoto (33), clear 15 home runs. Only four Blue Jays hit even 10 homers. Also, Toronto's lineup is mostly right-handed. Lowe would add power and also a lefty bat to provide balance. We ranked him as the 13th-best free agent available.

    Recent findings suggest that adding rotation help is a "top priority," White Sox GM Chris Getz said during an MLB Network Radio interview on Tuesday. "We're going to exhaust the starter market, both free agency -- we'll take a look -- along with trades. That is our top priority," Getz said. He also confirmed that Grant Taylor, the team's postseason closer, will move into the rotation. Hagen Smith will remain in the bullpen.

    In a recent development, the White Sox have solid enough rotation depth with Taylor joining Sean Burke, Luis Castillo, Anthony Kay, Davis Martin, David Sandlin, Noah Schultz, and perhaps Shane Smith and Drew Thorpe. There is room for improvement, though, particularly at the top. Chicago could use a bona fide ace, not that one is easy to acquire or abundantly available.

    Industry observers note that add the Padres to the list of teams that have shown interest in Skubal, reports MLB Network. San Diego has a major need in the rotation -- Joe Musgrove, who hasn't made a start since the 2024 postseason, and Randy Vásquez are their only rotation locks -- and a newly introduced ownership group that seems willing to spend in its first offseason.

    Skubal is far and away the offseason's best free agent. He is also a Scott Boras client, and, historically, top Boras clients take the largest contract offer regardless of team situation. That isn't to say the Padres are a bad situation. Not at all. They're a very good team that is in the postseason most years, plus they play in San Diego. Who doesn't love San Diego?

    The Padres are also connected to several Japanese players, according to The Athletic. That includes MLB free agents Seiya Suzuki and Shota Imanaga, as well as players coming over from Nippon Professional Baseball, like third baseman Teruaki Sato.

    According to recent reports, free agent lefty Adrian Morejon is drawing interest as a starting pitcher, but he prefers to remain in the bullpen, according to The Athletic. Even during the season, there were rumblings that Morejon would like to be given a chance to start in 2027. He came up through the minors as a starter and only remained in the bullpen because he was so dominant in a late-inning role.

    We ranked Morejon as the offseason's second-best free agent on the idea that he would move into the rotation. The belief within the game is that he has a chance to be an excellent starter, not just a back-end piece. Either way, Morejon is a very good pitcher, and at 28, he's also one of the youngest free agents available. He should have several peak years remaining.

    It has been revealed that although they are disinclined to pursue Tarik Skubal, the Cubs hope to add three established starting pitchers this offseason, reports The Athletic. Of the nine pitchers to make at least nine starts for Chicago in 2027, seven are free agents. Only Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery (per ESPN), and Edward Cabrera, who had a 5.96 ERA and was demoted to the bullpen, remain.

    Industry observers note that left-hander Justin Steele is expected back from UCL surgery next year, though he suffered a setback this summer and wasn't able to return as hoped in September. Others like Javier Assad and Jordan Wicks are depth options more than full-time rotation pieces. This free agent class offers plenty of second- and third-tier starters. That's where the Cubs are expected to shop.

    Unlike last offseason, the Mets are not interested in a major overhaul despite their disappointing year, reports MLB.com. The Mets went 74-88 and finished in last place in 2026. The only silver lining to the disappointing season was the ability to give a long runway to rookies like Carson Benge and Nolan McLean, both of whom finished in the top four of the Rookie of the Year voting.

    The Mets went 83-79 in 2025 and missed the postseason on the final day of the season. They made significant changes last winter, most notably jettisoning stalwarts Pete Alonso and Brandon Nimmo, then had a worse season in 2026. In September, president of baseball operations David Stearns admitted that much turnover created an "uncapped downside scenario," which is executive-speak for "there was too much risk.".

    Sources indicate that not surprisingly, the Braves are uninterested in moving former National League MVP Ronald Acuña Jr., according to MLB Network. It does feel like Atlanta's offense has gone stale and that they could move a core piece, but it won't be Acuña, nor is it likely to be Drake Baldwin, Michael Harris II, or Matt Olson. Ozzie Albies and Austin Riley are the more obvious players to move. Albies is entering the final season of his wildly team-friendly contract. Riley has six years remaining on his deal, which figures to make a move difficult.

    On Monday, Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow declined to commit to Trevor Story as his starting shortstop next season. "We still have a ton of confidence in Trevor, but any decisions like that are going to take place between Trevor and me far before I speak to anything publicly," Breslow told reporters, including the Boston Globe. Boston has one of the top prospects in the minors in shortstop Franklin Arias, who is very likely to make his debut early next year. Arias could push Story into a utility role or off the team entirely.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins had strong words Tuesday in reaction to Anthony Santander's anti-Muslim social media posts that he has since deleted.
    • Sources indicate that "There really aren't words to express my level of disappointment," Atkins said from the GM meetings on Tuesday, via Sportsnet.
    • Recent findings suggest that "I also talked to Anthony about his lack of awareness, realizing that he has a very large microphone, what that meant.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins had strong words Tuesday in reaction to Anthony Santander's anti-Muslim social media posts that he has since deleted.

    Sources indicate that "There really aren't words to express my level of disappointment," Atkins said from the GM meetings on Tuesday, via Sportsnet. "Anything exacerbating some level of hate, anti-Islamic, is just extremely concerning and extremely disappointing.

    Recent findings suggest that "I also talked to Anthony about his lack of awareness, realizing that he has a very large microphone, what that meant. We're working exceptionally hard internally to ensure, and we have been, that it's a safe environment, that baseball is for everyone. It's very important to us. It's a part of our organizational values and his behavior did not align with that.".

    Santander, a native Venezuelan, shared social media videos in the wake of the U.S. midterm elections last week, including one where a Christian pastor noted, "there is no such thing as kind Muslims." Another implied that Sharia law would be imposed in the U.S. following the election of Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate. Santander has since taken down the videos from his social media pages.

    In the aftermath, the team released the following statement:.

    "Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs.".

    It's unclear whether Santander prepares to address the matter publicly, but Atkins said he "told him that I thought he needed to and that he should.".

    According to recent reports, as far as personal conversations with Santander, Atkins said, "I expressed my level of concern. I believe he felt it. I know he feels badly. But I don't want to speak for him.".

    Santander was signed as an amateur free agent out of Venezuela in 2011 when he was 16. He signed a free agent deal with the Blue Jays prior to the 2025 season; injuries have held him to just 54 games in the past two seasons.

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    According to recent reports, that made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    According to recent reports, our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    In a recent development, steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an problem is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Things got heated between the Rockets and Warriors on Wednesday, with Marcus Smart getting ejected late in the third quarter for throwing a punch at the head area of Golden State's Charles Bassey.

    Smart and Bassey had gotten tangled up on the other end. After they disconnected and Bassey made his way back on defense, Smart chased after Bassey from behind, made contact, swung around to his front side, and threw the blow that is likely going to lead to a suspension.

    MARCUS SMART PUNCHES CHARLES BASSEY 😳 pic.twitter.com/MUsLlDHCz4.

    What did Bassey do, or say, that got Smart so riled up?

    "I just talked to [Smart]. He mentioned they got wrapped up, and [Smart]'s elbow that he hurt got bent up," Rockets coach Ime Udoka explained after the game. "So, [Smart] said something to him. Bassey said, 'What are you going to do?' And he did it.".

    You can see a better view of the play here.

    Smart was hit with a flagrant-2 foul, which carries an automatic ejection (the 13th of Smart's career). Smart didn't stick around long after he threw the punch.     • Industry observers note that chicago White Sox manager Will Venable and Brewers manager Pat Murphy were named the Managers of the Year in their respective leagues on Tuesday night as part of the BBWAA's awards week.
    • In a recent development, the annual awards, which also include Manager of the Year, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young and MVP, are voted on by 30 members of the Baseball Writers Association of America (that's two per MLB city in each league).
    • Murphy, manager of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, has been voted the National League Manager of the Year, the Baseball Writers Association of America declared on Tuesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that chicago White Sox manager Will Venable and Brewers manager Pat Murphy were named the Managers of the Year in their respective leagues on Tuesday night as part of the BBWAA's awards week. Murphy is the first manager to ever win the award in three consecutive seasons.

    In a recent development, the annual awards, which also include Manager of the Year, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young and MVP, are voted on by 30 members of the Baseball Writers Association of America (that's two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.

    Murphy, manager of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, has been voted the National League Manager of the Year, the Baseball Writers Association of America declared on Tuesday. He is the first person to win three consecutive Manager of the Year awards and the tenth person with three Manager of the Year wins in total.

    Industry observers note that ballots for the BBWAA's awards are submitted between the end of the regular season and the beginning of the postseason. They are regular-season awards and Milwaukee's World Series win did not factor into the voting.

    In a recent development, of course, Murphy did not need the World Series win to boost his Manager of the Year case. He guided the small-market Brewers to baseball's best record (103-59) and run differential (+214) during the regular season, and their fourth consecutive NL Central title. Their 103 wins are a franchise record and baseball's most since 2023.

    Murphy just completed his third season as Brewers manager and has three Manager of the Year wins to show for it. Bobby Cox (2004-05), Kevin Cash (2020-21), and Stephen Vogt (2024-25) are the only others with two consecutive Manager of the Year awards. Vogt was not an American League Manager of the Year finalist this season.

    Prior to Murphy's threepeat here, the Brewers had never had a Manager of the Year winner. He's won the award now three times in three years at the helm.

    Atlanta Braves manager Walt Weiss and Philadelphia Phillies manager Don Mattingly finished behind Murphy in the voting. Mattingly took over as an interim after the Phillies fired Rob Thomson on April 28. Philadelphia had baseball's fourth-best record after the managerial change. Weiss guided the Braves to the NL East title.

    Recent findings suggest that venable, who helped orchestrate a 24-win year-to-year improvement and guided the team to its first postseason berth since 2021, has been named the American League Manager of the Year, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced on Tuesday. He beat out Tampa Bay Rays manager Kevin Cash and Boston Red Sox manager Chad Tracy.

    Industry observers note that the White Sox went 84-78 in 2026 after going 60-102 in 2025 and a hideous 41-121 in 2024. Those 121 losses are the record in baseball's Modern Era (since 1900). Venable's White Sox are the first team in history to reach the postseason after losing at least 100 games in the previous two seasons (they also lost 101 games in 2023).

    The huge steps forward seem to be what secured the award for Venable. He took over in 2025 and the White Sox improved by 19 wins that season, only to turn around and improve by 24 more wins this past season. They were arguably the most surprising playoff team in 2026 and Venable gets his due here.

    Venable joins the following White Sox manager of the year winners:.

    According to recent reports, cash finishes as the runner-up in a very close vote. Venable got 15 of the 30 first-place votes while Cash got 12. Tracy finishes in third place, with Guardians manager Stephen Vogt fourth and Yankees' skipper Aaron Boone sitting fifth.

    Recent findings suggest that cash's Rays improved by 21 games to win an AL-best 98 and win the AL East after finishing in fourth place in 2025. Tracy took over the Red Sox after Alex Cora started 10-17 and was fired. Tracy went 77-58 and earned the second AL wild card.

    Two days after losing by 51 points to the Golden State Warriors, the Upcoming Orleans Pelicans managed an even more embarrassing loss on Wednesday when they were blown out 145-111 by the Brooklyn Nets, who were 2-8 entering the night.

    It has been revealed that fresh Orleans (4-8) began the season on a four-game losing streak before bouncing back to .500 with a four-game winning streak, but has now lost four straight again. The concerning part of their recent skid is that the Pelicans have grown increasingly uncompetitive.

    In a recent development, in that initial four-game losing streak to open the season, the Pelicans lost by a combined 23 points in the four games. In their last two games, they've lost by a combined 85 points, leaving Zion Williamson with just one word to describe his team's effort.

    Sources indicate that "Unacceptable," Williamson noted, via ESPN. "I don't even have a lot of words. Just unacceptable.".

    In a recent development, williamson called out the Pelicans' defensive effort during this latest losing streak, as they've allowed at least 138 points in three consecutive games. The seventh-year star then called for his team to look inward and be honest with themselves about whether they're doing everything they can to help the team win.

    "I said nobody likes to lose like this, but if we don't like to lose like this, we have to start with ourselves first," Williamson said. "Look in the mirror and say, did I do what I needed to do for my team? Not individually. Did I do what I needed to do for my team? And then we go from there.".

    Sources indicate that it's never a good sign when a team's star is questioning the collective's effort level and commitment to winning just 12 games into the season. This is when buy-in should be the easiest to get because a team's goals are still right in front of them, but the Pelicans are already showing signs that they will likely spend another season at the bottom of the Western Conference.

    That four-game winning streak -- which was somewhat schedule-aided with two games against the woeful Sacramento Kings and Utah Jazz -- feels like ages ago for the Pelicans. If they're going to turn things around, Williamson is right that it starts with accountability from the players, but with some key injuries to Trey Murphy III and Yves Missi, coupled with poor play, this season could get away from Latest Orleans quickly.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Houston Astros have chosen Brad Ausmus as their next manager, the team declared on Wednesday.

    It has been revealed that ausmus replaces Joe Espada, whose contract as Houston manager was not renewed after three seasons. Espada led the Astros to the playoffs in two of those seasons.

    Industry observers note that "I am very excited to be back in Houston," Ausmus mentioned in a statement. "The Astros and the city of Houston have been a huge part of my life, and I'm thrilled to create a new chapter as the team's manager. I'd like to thank [general manager Randy Flores] and the entire Astros organization for this opportunity, and I can't wait to get to work.".

    Ausmus, 57, had served as bench coach for the Fresh York Yankees since late 2023. Prior to that, he had two stints as a substantial-league manager. He first managed the Detroit Tigers from 2014-17, and over that span he guided the team to a 314-332 record and a division title in his first season. Ausmus also managed the Angels to a 72-90 record in 2019. Overall, Ausmus as a manager has a winning percentage of .478 in five seasons.

    Recent findings suggest that before his dugout career, Ausmus was a top defensive catcher for years. Ausmus's playing career spanned parts of 18 seasons in Major League Baseball, 10 of which came with the Astros. Along the way, Ausmus won three Gold Gloves behind the mask and earned an All-Star selection as a member of the Tigers in 1999.

    Recent findings suggest that "We are thrilled to welcome Brad back to the Astros organization," Flores stated in a statement. "Brad impressed us throughout the interview process, demonstrating the leadership, energy, and expertise critical to driving a winning culture both on and off the field. I am excited to work alongside Brad and happy to have him back in an Astros uniform.".

    Industry observers note that with Houston, Ausmus is the first major hire undertaken by Flores, who himself was named to his post earlier in the offseason. The Astros are coming off a division title and a postseason berth in 2026. However, they also finished 81-81 and had a negative run differential. It's an uncertain future, as the Astros have an aging roster in spots, a weak farm system, and multiple core contributors entering their walk years in 2027.

    According to recent reports, it remains to be seen whether owner Jim Crane will try to wring out another season of contention from the roster or lean into a rebuild. Whatever the course, Ausmus will help guide it in a city where he remains a highly popular figure.

    As of Houston's decision to hire Ausmus, the Los Angeles Angels are the only team with a current managerial vacancy.     Recent findings suggest that the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

    Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

    But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

    The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

    The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their significant-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

    There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

    Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

    Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

    In a recent development, “He is a top player, no doubt about it,” stated head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

    “He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

    Industry observers note that A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

    Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

    Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

    Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

    Sources indicate that tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

    He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

    Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

    Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

    Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

    This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

    Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

    Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

    Industry observers note that de Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more newly introduced faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

    Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

    But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

    Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that substantial-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his latest-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

    Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on latest players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

    Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

    Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

    His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

    “You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

    According to recent reports, “We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

    It has been revealed that “I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

    In a recent development, “Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

    “We can improve rapidly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] fresh players but we have to put something more.

    It has been revealed that “We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”.

    We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

    Industry observers note that it was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. Brentford is maybe one of the most vital teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

    According to recent reports, really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can promptly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

    Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

    It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

    Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

    Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the significant spenders.

    That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s upcoming leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

    The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

    De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

    Industry observers note that spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

    Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

    Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

    Asked about the Mali international, Andrews stated: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

    In a recent development, “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

    Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Golden State Warriors' fairytale start to the season got a dose of reality on Wednesday when Stephen Curry suffered an injury to his oblique in a loss to the Houston Rockets.

    Recent findings suggest that an MRI on Thursday confirmed an oblique abdominal tear and the team unveiled that Curry will be re-evaluated in two weeks. While two weeks is the best-case scenario, that being just the re-evaluation point means his absence could extend beyond that timetable -- as that also doesn't include any ramp-up process he would need to clear before returning to the floor.

    Sources indicate that the injury happened halfway through the first quarter. You can see Curry get tangled up with Alperen Sengun and grab at his side after they separate.

    Steph Curry got injured after Sengun grabbed and twisted his arm pic.twitter.com/4p20Rogpeu.

    Moments later, Curry hit his lone 3-pointer of the game and could once again be seen grabbing at his side after the shot.

    Sources indicate that stephen Curry headed to the locker room with an apparent right hip injury. pic.twitter.com/1zVrNz00bH.

    Industry observers note that curry exited the game at the next dead ball and didn't return. After the game, Warriors coach Steve Kerr stated concern about Curry's injury was "high.".

    In a recent development, "He remarked he tweaked something in his abdominal area," Kerr said. "He said he's never done it before. ... Concern is high, but I have no idea the extent of the injury.".

    In recent seasons, the range of recovery times for other notable NBA oblique injuries has varied.

    In a recent development, it's unclear how severe Curry's oblique tear is. These are all strains, which is code for a minor tear, but the worst-case scenario would be a more severe one. We saw this two years ago when the Orlando Magic lost both Franz Wagner and Paolo Banchero to oblique tears that kept Banchero out for 10 weeks and Wagner for more than a month.

    Any extended absence would be disastrous for the Warriors, who are not equipped to cover for any Curry injury. Curry has gotten off to a scorching start, entering Wednesday averaging 30.1 points per game on 50.3/45.7/98.7 shooting splits with Golden State winning eight straight games for the first time since the 2022 championship season.

    But this was always a fingers-crossed situation with an aging roster. Already down Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porziņģis, and with Brandon Williams and Gary Payton II also on the shelf and wing Will Richard playing through a ligament tear in his thumb, the Warriors have little, if any, margin for any more injuries.

    Industry observers note that this comes at a particularly tough time for the Warriors, who are entering their most difficult stretch of the season. On Friday, they'll visit the San Antonio Spurs before facing the Dallas Mavericks and Fresh Orleans Pelicans on a back-to-back.

    The Warriors have opened up at 8-4 with a top-three offense, but that can go south very promptly without Curry.

    Curry is the latest NBA star to face an extended injury absence in the first month of the 2026-27 season. Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren (Thunder), Anthony Edwards (Timberwolves), Tyrese Haliburton (Pacers), Kawhi Leonard (Raptors), Paolo Banchero (Magic), Jalen Duren (Pistons) and Kon Knueppel (Hornets) are among the players at the moment dealing with multi-week absences.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    LAS VEGAS — The Phillies are at a crossroads. A team that is still full of promise. A team that can compete with some of the best clubs in the league. A team that has World Series hopes. But also a team whose core consists of aging superstars.

    In a recent development, "We have a lot of high-end salary players, and they're not young, they're not old, but they're in that age bracket that you have to make a decision," Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowksi stated Tuesday during GM Meetings. "Maybe we have enough high-end players, and we need to complement them with other players overall. That's a decision we have to make.".

    In a recent development, with a likely lockout looming and the financial structure of baseball's future unclear, the Phillies have a projected payroll of $247 million for 2027. Roughly two-thirds, or approximately $164 million of that money, will go toward players who are 34 or older, including household names such as Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber, and Zack Wheeler.

    Industry observers note that all three had quality seasons in 2026, but it's fair to question whether this team has reached its ceiling. Wheeler is entering his age-37 season, while Harper and Schwarber are entering their age-34 seasons. That figure above doesn't account for Trea Turner, an aging shortstop who will turn 34 in June, or Aaron Nola, who also turns 34 that month. Turner and Nola will make a combined $51.8 million in 2027.

    It has been revealed that "Right now we need an outfielder," stated Dombrowski. "You're talking about an outfielder, you're talking about some right-handed hitting, a utility infielder, a bit more in the bullpen.".

    Can Dombrowski do it all? Especially in a market and a game that is defined by uncertainty this offseason?

    "I don't know," he said. "It might be hard because they all cost money, too.".

    According to recent reports, whether it's through free agency, trades, or both remains to be determined. If the Phillies do spend in free agency, Seiya Suzuki remains on the Phillies' shortlist of possible options.

    Despite the unpredictability surrounding the 2027 season and Philadelphia's financial commitments to aging players, Dombrowski acknowledged that owner John Middleton remains willing to spend if the right opportunity presents itself.

    Still, building from within provided a good amount of the tenor during Dombrowski's media availability. The Phillies' leader was adamant regarding infield prospect Aidan Miller, intimating that the 22-year-old is certainly a real possibility as a key contributor — even more so with the struggles of Turner at shortstop in 2026.

    According to recent reports, "I really am not going to ever anoint a young player a position," Dombrowski said. "I do think he has the capabilities, and it's just not me. Anybody that's seen him, and people from other organizations probably saying, 'Wow, you still have to earn the spot, but I think that, as it stands, that would be very helpful for us to have that consideration.' And frankly, I'm hoping he does. I'm not giving it to him. But I'm hoping that he does.".

    A fellow should-be NL East contender is connected to the best free agent on the market.

    Left-hander Tarik Skubal will reportedly meet with the Mets next week. The incumbent Dodgers, according to general manager Brandon Gomes, have also been in contact with Skubal. The expectation is that those two sides will meet at some point as well, Gomes mentioned at the GM Meetings Tuesday. While other teams, including the Padres are expected to make a run at Skubal, the Mets and Dodgers are currently viewed as the frontrunners.

    In a recent development, the Mets are coming off an abysmal season, finishing at the bottom of the National League East with a 74-88 record. Surely the club is in need of starting pitching, posting a 4.47 rotation ERA, the seventh-worst mark in baseball. David Stearns, the Mets president of baseball operations, elected not to comment on the Skubal sweepstakes, a customary practice this time of year, but spoke around the team's needs.

    Recent findings suggest that "Having a complete rotation is really notable, and that includes having pitchers who can successfully get you through a postseason and get you through a playoff series," Stearns said. "We've seen over and over again in the playoffs that that can be constructed in a variety of different ways, and so we're open to doing it in any way possible.".

    According to recent reports, skubal, certainly, would offer Latest York an anchor to its rotation. An ace that the Mets haven't seen since Jacob deGrom. But he isn't a sudden fix to all of the Mets' pitching woes. Unquestionably, talented depth also stands at the forefront of some of the team's needs.

    According to recent reports, the club traded Freddy Peralta to the Rays at the deadline after a bad first half with Newly introduced York. He turned a corner once he got with the Rays and helped lead them to a World Series. Also at the deadline, the club traded Clay Holmes, a converted starter, to the Cubs.

    Recent findings suggest that both pitchers are now free agents. Meanwhile, Kodai Senga and Sean Manaea, two veterans who have underperformed in recent years, are set to become free agents after the 2027 season (Senga has a $15 million option for 2028 that will likely be declined).

    Skubal is a logical fit in Queens, especially if Steve Cohen is ready to open his wallet.

    Sources indicate that "Every situation is unique," Stearns said. "It's been well-publicized, even since I've been here, we've engaged in extremely long-term negotiations for pitchers. We will do so again, but the situation matters. The specific circumstances matter. We do have to look at every individual pitcher on a case-by-case basis.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    CINCINNATI — Mauricio Pochettino went through Tuesday's U.S. match like every other during his two-year spell.

    Sources indicate that "It was a normal game," he remarked. "You are focused. You want to concentrate. You want to win. You want to help the players perform.".

    And then the end came — the end of a 2-0 victory over Haiti, the end of a two-leg CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal that completed an 8-0 aggregate wipeout, and the end of a 37-match tenure that saw advances in the program at large but also disappointment in not advancing deeper at the World Cup.

    When it was over at TQL Stadium, the finality of it all hit Pochettino hard. He's passionate about people and soccer. While his decision to sign with Manchester United was purely business, his emotions about leaving behind a tight group were genuine.

    Recent findings suggest that "When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things," he said. "Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.".

    There were hugs and tears, both on the field and in the locker room.

    It has been revealed that "It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us," he remarked. "When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are not robots.".

    Mauricio Pochettino and members of the team staff pose for a picture on the pitch after the victory over Haiti in a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal match at TQL Stadium.

    In a recent development, captain Tyler Adams observed, "He fell in love with the country. That's first and foremost, the most important thing. He didn't know exactly what to expect when he took the job. He fell in love with the people. He fell in love with the football, and he fell in love with our team. That's special.".

    Adams and the rest of the team sent Pochettino off in style with six consecutive victories, including four shutouts in a row.

    "We wanted to finish in a good way," Pochettino stated. "The way we play, that is what we dream of when we arrive. The team really enjoyed playing football, playing soccer.".

    Recent findings suggest that in the first half, Christian Pulisic scored on an audacious bicycle kick and teenager Julian Hall continued the torrid start to his international career by scoring for the fifth time in six matches. Weston McKennie set up both goals.

    "It was a pretty bad cross, to be honest. I had to save him," Pulisic joked about his longtime friend's assist. "I saw it and I had to go for it. It was cool; it was special.".

    Industry observers note that asked if he too had ever scored such a goal, McKennie remarked, "I've had side volleys, never bikes. I don't know if I'd survive the fall after that.".

    In a recent development, the postgame mood was light, fun and emotional; it was human. Pochettino had fostered a positive, engaging environment that took hold last year and carried through the World Cup over the summer and into this fall.

    "It's a little bit sad Mauricio is departing, but as a team, we're going to continue to stick together," Hall stated. "We're just waiting for what's ahead in the future.".

    Industry observers note that reflecting on his tenure, Pochettino remarked he wished he had had more time in the buildup to the World Cup. The way the players performed at the tournament, he said, should have been how they performed six months before it. From there, he said, the team would have hit full capacity at the World Cup.

    He did, though, have them playing well through his finale.

    "It's a good way to end," Pulisic remarked, "and send him off in a good manner like that.".

    Sources indicate that pochettino believes the U.S. is on the right path.

    Industry observers note that "I am sure this group of players will achieve big things in the future, I have no doubt," he remarked. "Experienced players with the talent that is coming, it's the perfect combination.".

    Recent findings suggest that the U.S. Soccer Federation has begun the process of identifying candidates to replace Pochettino, who, after the game, was off to the airport to fly to England and begin work with a storied Premier League club that's off to its worst start in 40 years.

    The next official U.S. matches will come at the Nations League final four in late March. By then, the USSF would like to have a coach in place.

    "I don't think someone's going to come in and completely change everything we have going on here," Pulisic said. "There's a lot of positives, and hopefully he can help steer us in the right direction.".

    What kind of coach is the star forward looking for?

    It has been revealed that "Someone who can just continue to build off this culture we have. We have a really good starting place — having a good identity, finding ourselves and what we're going to look like moving forward in the next [few] years and going into the next World Cup.".

    McKennie said he would like "someone that's ambitious, someone that's open-minded, someone that can gel with the group, has a good relationship with players, and believes in the youth as well.".

    Pochettino said he would be happy to provide advice, should the federation need it.

    "For sure, they are not going to ask me because they have the capacity," he remarked.

    Then, with a devilish grin, he added, "More than two years ago they signed [women's coach] Emma Hayes and Mauricio Pochettino. I think they have good eyes!".

    Corey Seager landing spots: Six possible destinations with Rangers veteran on the trading block

    📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (985 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A upcoming star-quality trade candidate recently barged onto the scene in Major League Baseball.
    • The Rangers signed Corey Seager to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season, and that splash signing played a leading role in the Rangers' 2023 World Series triumph.
    • Seager is going into his age-33 campaign in 2027, and he suffered a downturn at the plate this past season (while still remaining a plus at the plate and in the field).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A upcoming star-quality trade candidate recently barged onto the scene in Major League Baseball. The Texas Rangers are reportedly fielding and considering trade offers for veteran shortstop Corey Seager.

    The Rangers signed Corey Seager to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season, and that splash signing played a leading role in the Rangers' 2023 World Series triumph. Seager was named MVP of that World Series, and during the regular season he enjoyed perhaps the best campaign of his standout career. Now, though, with the Rangers facing an uncertain future, they may be looking to unload Seager and the five years and roughly $155 million left on his pact.

    It won't be simple. Seager is going into his age-33 campaign in 2027, and he suffered a downturn at the plate this past season (while still remaining a plus at the plate and in the field). As well, he's been injury-prone for much of his 12-year career. Over the last four years, he's averaged 111.5 games per season, and in recent times he's been limited by injuries to his thumb, hip, back, and both hamstrings. At his age and after such a long history of health issues, there's no reason to think that will change. Additionally, Seager can control the process. While his contract included a limited no-trade clause that allowed him to block trades to eight teams of his choosing, Seager has now earned "10 and 5" rights – i.e., he's spent at least 10 seasons in the majors and the last five with the same team – which means he has the right to block any trade.

    According to recent reports, all that mentioned, Seager is no doubt appealing to teams in contending mode and in need of upgrades on the left side of the infield. He still has strong quality-of-contact indicators at the plate, and he's still an asset with the glove. It's easy to dream on that career OPS+ of 135 from the shortstop position and the fact that he was at peak, at least when he was on the field, as recently as 2025. The Rangers are also presumably willing to pay down a chunk of his remaining commitment in order to make a trade more tenable. As for Seager's druthers, it's possible he'd like to play out his contract for a team better positioned to deliver to him a third career World Series ring.

    With all those considerations laid out, let's have a look at a handful of teams who may – or at least should – be kicking the tires on a Seager trade. We'll proceed in taut and suspenseful alphabetical order ….

    The Braves made it to the NLDS this past season and have made the playoffs in eight of the last nine years. For much of that time, though, they've struggled to find a reliable presence at shortstop. This past season, Atlanta shortstops combined to bat just .222/.280/.322, which is squarely in "unacceptable liability" territory. As well, the top two turn-takers at the position, Mauricio Dubón and Ha-Seong Kim, are both free agents.

    Boston still has Trevor Story under contract through next season with a club option for 2028. However, Story, who soon turns 34, appears to be very much in decline, and that's in addition to his troubles staying healthy. This past season, he had an OPS+ of just 75 and was barely above replacement level overall. The Sox have signaled they're open to an upgrade at the position, and Seager would certainly be that.

    It has been revealed that why not a headline-grabbing reunion in L.A.? Seager was a Dodgers lifer before he inked that big contract with Texas, and that level of familiarity – plus the Dodgers' ongoing excellence – could be alluring. The Dodgers could also use an upgrade in the middle infield. They could install Seager at short and shift Mookie Betts to second base, where he has significant experience. Or they could keep Betts at short, where he's adapted so very well, and let Seager transition to second – a marginally less taxing position that might even help him stay on the field. Tommy Edman, meanwhile, would transition back to a super-utility role. Either way, it's a compelling theoretical fit.

    The Yankees have previously shown trade interest in Seager, so it's no great leap to think they still might be eyeing him from afar. Young George Lombard Jr. is the shortstop of the present and future in the Bronx, so Seager would likely need to be willing to shift to third base if a Yankees trade is to come to pass. The Yanks have already signaled they're ready for an upgrade over Ryan McMahon, who's been frankly terrible at the plate since being acquired from the Rockies. The lefty-swinging Seager doubtless would enjoy that short porch in right at Yankee Stadium.

    It has been revealed that trea Turner is signed through 2033, but defensively he's become unplayable at the shortstop position. No surprise, then, that the Phillies are open to moving him, perhaps to the outfield, and finding someone else to man the critical position of short. Seager would be a needle-moving addition for lead operator Dave Dombrowski as he attempts to keep the Phils' contending window open for a bit longer. There's an argument that this would make the Philly lineup too left-handed, but the potential upgrade over what Turner provided them this past season makes it a worthwhile sacrifice.

    Recent findings suggest that the Jays had one of the worst offenses in all of baseball last season, and that lack of punch was the leading culprit in their tumble from the heights of 2025. Seager could be installed at short or second, and from there the Jays could shuffle infield incumbents Andrés Giménez and Ernie Clement. Indeed, Clement is perhaps at his most valuable when he's deployed as a heavily used multi-positional talent.
