    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • Industry observers note that kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • Industry observers note that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    Industry observers note that kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    Industry observers note that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    Recent findings suggest that it's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    We already know the Wild are substantial-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    Sources indicate that with Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't presently have on their roster.

    Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    In a recent development, allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

    Tech Report: Sam Darnold or Drew Lock? Breaking down the Seahawks' surprising QB debate

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Seattle Seahawks moved to 6-4 with their Sunday 21-13 victory over Fernando Mendoza and the Las Vegas Raiders.
    • In a recent development, should Mike Macdonald continue to roll with Lock under center and bench Sam Darnold?
    • Below, we will make the case for starting Lock moving forward, and the case for rolling with Darnold, with evidence obtained by Doug Clawson of CBS Sports Research.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Seattle Seahawks moved to 6-4 with their Sunday 21-13 victory over Fernando Mendoza and the Las Vegas Raiders. Drew Lock and Jaxon Smith-Njigba powered a strong second half, which included a 14-point third quarter to escape Sin City with the win, and now the Seahawks are going to need to have a conversation.

    In a recent development, should Mike Macdonald continue to roll with Lock under center and bench Sam Darnold? Lock has now made three starts this season, and won all three. If you want to count the Week 1 comeback against the Newly introduced England Patriots, where Lock took over on the second drive of the game, then he's accounted for four of Seattle's six wins. Lock is running the offense and taking care of the football, and it's working.

    Below, we will make the case for starting Lock moving forward, and the case for rolling with Darnold, with evidence obtained by Doug Clawson of CBS Sports Research.

    In a recent development, lock is a perfect 4-0 as the Seahawks' primary quarterback. Again, we'll use the term "primary" to include the season opener against the Patriots even though Darnold "started" that game. In all, Lock has completed 73.1% of his passes for 837 yards, seven touchdowns and zero turnovers.

    According to recent reports, lock ranks third in both EPA per dropback and yards per dropback this season (min. 75 attempts). The offense ranks eighth in EPA per play under Lock, and 28th with Darnold.

    Lock is also playing the style of football Seattle wants to play. What does that mean? It means he's accounted for zero turnovers and is getting the ball to JSN. Eight of Lock's 14 pass completions on Sunday went to Smith-Njigba, who finished with a season-high 171 yards and one touchdown. The Seahawks ran the ball 35 times and attempted 17 passes, and relied on an elite defense to take over the game. That's what Macdonald wants to do.

    The numbers prove it. Lock has been the more efficient quarterback this year, while Darnold leads the NFL with 29 turnovers over the last two seasons. He's turned the ball over seven times in the four losses this season, and they have been costly. Darnold threw zero touchdowns and two interceptions in the overtime loss to the Denver Broncos. He threw two interceptions in a three-point loss to the San Francisco 49ers, and two interceptions in the two-point loss to the Washington Commanders. Darnold actually hasn't finished a game this season without throwing an interception!

    It has been revealed that you can't argue with the record. Lock is 4-0 while Darnold is 2-4. If the season ended today, the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks wouldn't make the playoffs. You have to stick with what's working.

    Recent findings suggest that sure, Lock is 4-0, but have you seen who he's played? He beat a Patriots team that is clearly not the same Patriots team that made the Super Bowl last year. Drake Maye was seeing ghosts and threw three interceptions in Seattle's 13-10 win. Then, Lock beat the lowly Arizona Cardinals twice, and a Raiders team that was touting a rookie quarterback who was making his first career start. No. 1 overall pick quarterbacks are now 1-16-1 in their first career starts since 2004. It would have been shocking if Vegas won that game. Meanwhile, Darnold has faced off against Brock Purdy and the 49ers, Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears, and Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs.

    In a recent development, it's true that Darnold is turning the ball over too much right now, but he just became the fourth Super Bowl-winning quarterback in the last 35 postseasons to have zero turnovers in the playoffs. Darnold didn't have the most magical performance in the Super Bowl, but he was incredible in the NFC Championship Game vs. the Los Angeles Rams, throwing for 346 yards and three touchdowns with zero turnovers. He had to outduel NFL MVP Matthew Stafford.

    It has been revealed that we've seen Darnold play good football. We saw him play a part in a Super Bowl run just nine months ago. It hasn't been entirely smooth this year, but punting on Darnold for Lock right now would be an aggressive decision.

    Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin noted on NBC Sunday night that Macdonald and Darnold are "tied together for life" after the two helped engineer a successful climb to the NFL's mountaintop. Macdonald has a special level of respect for Darnold -- who has "money in coach Macdonald's emotional bank account," as Tomlin put it. It's worth having this debate because Lock is playing good football, but ultimately, Darnold is the Seahawks' starter.

    #26903. The lost years of Lamar Jackson -- and the greatness still within reach

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2354 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    The lost years of Lamar Jackson -- and the greatness still within reach

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2354 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Some years, Lamar Jackson's thumb hits another player and is fine.
    • Industry observers note that jackson's latest injury was almost too cruel to believe.
    • And then, on the Ravens' first play, Jackson hit his thumb on Greg Rousseau's arm.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Some years, Lamar Jackson's thumb hits another player and is fine. Some years, his ankle just gets hit rather than rolled up on. And those years, he has been -- and will be -- a player who can win an MVP and perhaps a Super Bowl.

    It has not been one of those years.

    Industry observers note that jackson's latest injury was almost too cruel to believe. After missing the previous three and a half games with a high ankle sprain, the two-time MVP was finally back. So, too, was the Ravens' hope. Jackson had looked phenomenal -- MVP-level phenomenal -- in fresh offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's system. Not only was he back, but he was back in a substantial spot: against fellow MVP Josh Allen in a crucial matchup vs. Buffalo on the first day of November, with Baltimore trying to end a two-game losing streak.

    And then, on the Ravens' first play, Jackson hit his thumb on Greg Rousseau's arm. Jackson looked down at his injured right thumb, trotted toward the sideline and then took a knee.

    "Oh boy," NFL on CBS analyst Ross Tucker noted.

    Medical personnel surrounded Jackson, draped a towel over his hand and brought him down the tunnel, off the field.

    Sources indicate that what more was there to say? Lamar Jackson, one of the defining players not just of the era but of NFL history, was hurt. Again. And it was serious. Again.

    According to recent reports, jackson officially landed on IR with a thumb injury that will require surgery. It is "potentially" season-ending, and with the Ravens 4-5 and losers of four straight, it's looking like a lost season in Baltimore. This is the fourth time in the last six years the 29-year-old has missed at least four games. It has robbed the Ravens of their Super Bowl aspirations. It has robbed the NFL of a superstar. And it has robbed Jackson, a Heisman Trophy winner and twice an NFL MVP, of even higher levels of all-time greatness.

    On the positive side, the thumb injury is the first ailment to land Jackson on IR. He has never had an ACL tear, an Achilles tear, etc. On the negative side, Jackson has racked up so many injuries of so many different kinds that it seems like something is constantly getting in the way, whether it's nagging at him or keeping him out of games. He even mentioned the ankle pain entering the Bills game last week was merely "bearable," not gone.

    Sources indicate that since the start of last season alone, Jackson has had hamstring, ankle, toe, knee, back, and thumb ailments. Not all of those kept him out, but they add up. He admitted he came back from last year's hamstring injury too early, impacting his play all season.

    And yes, for what it's worth, it's bad luck. If Jackson's hand hits Rousseau at any other angle, he might not hurt his thumb enough to need surgery. If a diving Jermaine Johnson II doesn't awkwardly trap Jackson's ankle to the turf in Week 3, Jackson might not miss the next three games. Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes have both had hundreds of similar plays and, with the exception of Mahomes' torn ACL last year, avoided injury for the most part. Sometimes, it's simply human anatomy, something Jackson cannot change.

    For as prolific a runner as Jackson is, he does an excellent job avoiding hits on those plays. None of his injuries have been on runs. It has just been a constant parade of misfortune. Unfortunately for Jackson and the Ravens, the NFL rolls on, whether you're lucky or not.

    According to recent reports, perhaps time and injuries have taken their toll and blocked our collective memory from how incredible Jackson has been. That would be truly unfortunate.

    In 2019, Jackson's second year of the league, he threw 36 touchdown passes and ran for 1,206 yards. In NFL history, there are ...

    There is ONE with both: Jackson in 2019.

    Recent findings suggest that in fact, only one other player ever has posted 1,200 rushing yards and merely double-digit passing touchdowns in a season: Spec Sanders of the New York Yankees (football version) in the All-America Football Conference in 1947. But he only threw 14 touchdowns. Jackson did things modern football has never known.

    Jackson became the youngest quarterback to win MVP and joined Tom Brady as the only unanimous MVPs in NFL history. There are many ways to measure individual season greatness, but Pro Football Reference's "Approximate Value" is as good as any. Jackson had an approximate value of 25 in 2019, tied for the second-best season on record; LaDanian Tomlinson's 2006 season, in which he scored an NFL-record 31 touchdowns, is the only one better.

    Industry observers note that jackson was healthy in 2020 and had another strong season, including a second straight 1,000-yard rushing effort. He has as many 1,000-yard rushing seasons as all other quarterbacks in NFL history combined (Michael Vick and Justin Fields both have one).

    Then the injuries started. In 2021, Jackson was on pace for another 1,000-yard rushing season, and the Ravens led the AFC North when Browns linebacker Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah dove at Jackson's ankles after Jackson released a pass. Jackson got carted off and didn't play in any of the final four games. The Ravens lost all four and missed the playoffs.

    The next year, Jackson sprained his PCL when his left knee got driven into the ground on a sack by the Broncos' Jonathan Cooper. He ended up missing six weeks -- the final five of the regular season and a wild card game, which Baltimore lost.

    This was a strange one. John Harbaugh initially wondered if Jackson could be back the next week and added "If not, it'll be sometime after that shortly." Then, Ravens officials were confident Jackson would return for the playoffs, per ESPN, leaving Jackson to essentially rule himself out -- and give his own medical update -- via social media.

    In 2023, though, Jackson was healthy and marvelous once again. Under new offensive coordinator Todd Monken, Jackson set career highs in completion percentage (67.2%), passing yards (3,678) and yards per attempt (8.0). He was still excellent on the ground with a team-high 821 yards. He won MVP and was one vote short of doing so unanimously.

    Sources indicate that he was somehow even better in 2024, with 4,172 passing yards and 8.8 yards per attempt. He threw 41 touchdowns and just four interceptions. He ran for 915 yards. He had already reached unprecedented levels. Now, he was reaching fresh ones, as the first player with:.

    His 10.25 touchdown-to-interception ratio was also the best ever in any 30-touchdown season.

    Somehow Jackson didn't win MVP. He was a first-team All-Pro, but MVP went to Allen, an extreme rarity. Jackson would have been the youngest three-time MVP in NFL history. That's how good the start was.

    From 2019 to 2024, Jackson ranked third in passer rating and touchdown-to-interception ratio and fourth in yards per attempt. He was also fourth in touchdown passes despite missing significant time in two seasons. He was also eighth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry.

    Industry observers note that he was the Shohei Ohtani of football. No one can be this good at two different aspects, right? Wrong. Jackson was truly exceptional, and he seemed to be getting better.

    He had nine touchdowns and zero interceptions on an absurd 9.6 yards per attempt through three weeks of 2025. Then came the hamstring injury, which started an avalanche of injuries. The hits haven't stopped coming since.

    If two things stand out as Jackson's career shortcomings, it's injuries and playoff performance. The two are somewhat intertwined. In 2021, Baltimore missed the playoffs. In 2022, Jackson missed the playoffs. Last year, his injuries derailed the Ravens, but they somehow got a Week 18 win-and-in game against the Steelers. Tyler Loop missed a game-winning field goal attempt. It's looking like he will not add to his postseason ledger this season, either.

    Recent findings suggest that had Jackson been healthy in even two of those four lost seasons, is he a Super Bowl champ? Or does he at least have more postseason wins?

    Jackson is one of nine quarterbacks to win multiple MVP awards since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger. Of those nine, Jackson has the second-fewest playoff wins (two) before his 30th birthday, only ahead of the famously late-blooming Steve Young.

    Wins, it is noted, are not a quarterback stat, and that can be true. Unfortunately for Jackson and the Ravens, both his play and his team's have declined in the postseason. The Ravens are 3-6 in the playoffs since drafting Jackson in 2018 (3-5 with Jackson as the starter).

    It has been revealed that jackson lost in his playoff debut in 2018, but the real disappointment came after his 2019 NFL season. With the Ravens as the AFC No. 1 seed, he had 365 yards and a touchdown passing and 143 yards rushing against the Titans, but he also had two interceptions,  lost a fumble, and failed on two fourth-and-short runs.

    Recent findings suggest that the next year, Jackson earned his first playoff win, getting a measure of revenge on the Titans in the wild card round. But one week later, Baltimore went quietly in a 17-3 loss to Buffalo, most remembered for Jackson throwing a terrible end-zone interception that Taron Johnson returned 101 yards for a touchdown.

    The INT that's tied for the longest pick-six in playoff history?This 101-yard return from Taron Johnson in the 2020 Divisional Round 🔥📺: #KCvsBUF — Sunday 6:30pm ET on CBS📱: Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Z9SsFryOEL.

    Jackson suffered a concussion on the final play of the third quarter and did not return.

    His next playoff game came after his 2023 MVP campaign. He was excellent in a win over the Texans, but in the AFC Championship, he lost a fumble and had another awful end-zone interception, this time in the fourth quarter. The Chiefs won 17-10, and Jackson's two turnovers loomed large.

    According to recent reports, in 2024, the Ravens, supercharged by the Derrick Henry addition, were on the precipice of a return to the AFC Championship Game before falling to the Bills, 27-25. Jackson again had turnover concerns -- a bad interception and an even worse fumble, the latter of which led the a Buffalo touchdown -- but that game is better remembered for a Mark Andrews fumble and, later, drop on the potential game-tying two-point attempt.

    Industry observers note that there have been tons of moments where supporting cast members have let Jackson down in crucial moments. Andrews' nightmare two seasons ago and Zay Flowers' fumble at the 1-yard line against the Chiefs certainly come to mind. There's a lack of game-changing plays from the defense: two turnovers forced in Jackson's seven postseason starts, and none in the past two playoff trips, when hopes were the highest. But it's undeniable that Jackson has been very poor in the playoffs, too.

    According to recent reports, >> Min. 3 playoff starts since 2018.

    Recent findings suggest that the final stat -- turnovers -- is truly staggering ... and costly. Jackson's turnovers have cost the Ravens an estimated 6.86 points per game in the playoffs, basically a touchdown. The only quarterbacks with a higher rate out of the 26-player sample are Drake Maye, Justin Herbert, and Trevor Lawrence.

    Unless there's a major turnaround, this stands to be the Jackson's fourth postseason-less season in the last six years. He can't fix a glaring hole in his resume if he can't even get there.

    The quick answer is "yes." It might just look a little different.

    The first order of business, assuming this season is over for all intents and purposes, will be Jackson's contract. Former NFL agent Joel Corry dove into that recently. Of note ...

    Baltimore should absolutely want to keep Jackson, even with the injury history. Through three games this year, he led the league in yards per attempt and was on pace for his highest missed-tackle rate and highest yards per rush of his career, all while not running as much as earlier in his career.

    They have also been truly unlucky with injuries. He was healthy in 2023 and 2024. Last year's hamstring and this year's ankle were unfortunate, but the thumb was a freak injury. Perhaps we should expect him to miss a few games every year from now on, but there's also a reasonable chance he doesn't.

    Industry observers note that jackson will be 30 next year, but 30 is not ancient. John Elway won his first Super Bowl at 37. Matthew Stafford got his first at 34. Drew Brees was 31. Peyton Manning was 30.

    Recent findings suggest that josh Allen is 30 and, like Jackson, hasn't been to a Super Bowl. Joe Burrow is about a month older than Jackson and hasn't won one.

    Sources indicate that A common budding misconception is that Jackson can't be a star as he gets older and he runs less and/or less effectively. But Jackson has proved to be a superb pocket quarterback. His development as a passer is as impressive as it gets. Since 2023, Jackson has the third-highest yards per attempt in the NFL on throws inside the pocket and released within three seconds -- aka without much improvisation going on.

    Sources indicate that jackson may never reach the heights he was on the path to after being on the precipice of becoming the youngest three-time MVP ever in 2024. That's the sad truth about a player playing hurt and/or missing significant chunks of three years of his prime. Would he have another MVP? Two? A Super Bowl ring? We'll never know, and that's tough to swallow.

    But there's a version of Jackson -- a little luckier, a little better in the playoffs, a lot better of a passer than he was his younger years -- that can still be a superstar for many years and get him back on a path that ends with him as an all-time great.

    Tech Report: NBA Rookie of the Year race: Three players at top, but don't count out AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson just yet

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1877 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • News broke on Thursday that Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson will miss the next four to six weeks after fracturing his right hand.
    • Wilson was off to a hot start during his rookie season with the Bulls.
    • Missing the next four to six weeks would keep Wilson out until at least mid to late December.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    News broke on Thursday that Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson will miss the next four to six weeks after fracturing his right hand. It marks the third separate hand injury Wilson has suffered during the last 11 months. He fractured his left hand and broke his right thumb during his freshman season at North Carolina, with the latter injury causing him to miss the end of the regular season.

    Wilson was off to a hot start during his rookie season with the Bulls. The No. 4 overall pick was averaging 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.8 steals in his first 10 games and was one of the few bright spots for the 1-9 Bulls.

    Missing the next four to six weeks would keep Wilson out until at least mid to late December. Although there is no 65-game minimum requirement to win Rookie of the Year as with other NBA awards, missing an extended period of time will likely see Wilson fall behind in what should be one of the most competitive races in recent memory.

    Sources indicate that entering Friday, there appears to be a clear-cut top five in this season's Rookie of the Year race. Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg, the No. 11 pick, is the current favorite (+115 at FanDuel). After Lendeborg, Grizzlies forward Cameron Boozer (+290) and Kings guard Darius Acuff Jr. (+320) have the shortest odds.

    The top two picks in the draft -- Wizards forward AJ Dybantsa and Jazz guard Darryn Peterson -- are tied for fourth (+1600) in the odds. Wilson is next at +4000, with a steep drop-off after that.

    Dybantsa missed the first four games of the season with an ankle sprain, while Peterson got off to a slower start than some of his peers but has looked fantastic for the shorthanded Jazz during the last week and a half.

    In a recent development, the current odds for Rookie of the Year (as of Nov. 13) are below.

    Less than a month into the NBA season, three players have separated themselves from the rest. Boozer opened the season as the favorite to win Rookie of the Year, with Wilson, Peterson and Dybantsa not far behind in the odds. However, two players outside of the top five picks in a loaded draft class are in position to crash the party. Here is a quick scouting report on what we have seen from Boozer, Acuff and Lendeborg and how they can continue to stay in the race.

    The things Boozer did well in college have carried over to the NBA. Since the 2010-11 season, no player in college basketball had a better box plus/minus (18.75) than Boozer. His freshman season at Duke was better than those of Cooper Flagg and Zach Edey, both of whom also won national player of the year honors. It speaks to how Boozer can make an impact on the floor when he isn't scoring. He has a great feel for the game and is already one of the best outlet passers in the league. He crashes the boards hard and is physical on both ends of the floor.

    Industry observers note that however, one (small) concern was also an issue at times at Duke: rim finishing. Boozer struggled against bigger defenders at times in college, and he's running into the same thing in the NBA, shooting just 46.6% at the rim on 58 attempts, per Synergy. That number has improved over the last few games, but it's something Boozer will have to improve.

    According to recent reports, lendeborg has been fantastic and is a major reason why the Warriors are off to an 8-4 start. The pressure will be even greater over the next several weeks while Stephen Curry is out with an injury. He routinely took advantage of mismatches at Michigan, and he's doing the same in the NBA. His all-around game has taken tremendous strides over the last 12 months and he's going to continue to get better.

    Of course, the one knock on Lendeborg in the draft was age. He was the oldest player selected in the first round and just turned 24, but he's a perfect fit for Golden State given its win-now timeline. What has been most impressive for Lendeborg is his shooting. He is knocking down 42.6% of his 3-point attempts while taking 5.7 per game. Last season at Michigan, Dusty May told him to shoot more 3-pointers. It paid dividends for his overall game.

    Recent findings suggest that he is the most polarizing rookie in this class, and he is being asked to do more than his peers on a nightly basis. Since having a rough shooting night in his NBA debut against the Clippers, his efficiency has been much better. People who don't watch the Kings (how can you blame them?) might not realize that the box score doesn't tell the full story. Yes, Acuff has attempted over 20 shots per game in each of his first 11 games, but he is also 13th in the league in potential assists (12), 12th in assist points created, and 10th in total assists (80). The game is really slowing down for Acuff in a good way.

    His passing was an underappreciated skill during his time at Arkansas. People will see the scoring numbers and immediately throw out a bad comparison for Acuff, but the truth is, Acuff is being asked to run the offense, be the primary scorer, and also facilitate. How many 19-year-olds in the NBA are being asked to do that? Right now, the answer is just him. Acuff will continue to put up numbers for a bad Kings team that is waiting for the trade deadline to deal some of the veterans on the roster.

    According to recent reports, ACUFF JR. JOINS LEBRON 👏In tonight's action, Darius Acuff Jr. (32 PTS, 10 AST) joined LeBron James (3x) as the only teenagers in NBA history to record 30+ points and 10+ assists in multiple games! pic.twitter.com/VmWshWmQZn.

    The debate surrounding the No. 1 pick was one of the biggest storylines in the lead-up to this year's draft. With Dybantsa going to Washington and Peterson to Utah, they ended up in similar situations on teams with established veterans that seemed ready to take the next step. But for the Jazz, it has been a nightmare season of injuries, with Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen out for extended periods.

    With everyone in the lineup, Peterson struggled to find a clear-cut role during his first few games. He finished in single digits in two of his first four games, which included taking just seven shots from the floor in his NBA debut. Coming out of high school, Peterson was best playing on-ball. However, when he got to Kansas, he played more off-ball. Part of that was due to cramping challenges that sidelined him for an extended period, but Peterson has shown he can play both roles well.

    darryn scored 26 tonight, a latest career high #TakeNote presented by @ZionsBank pic.twitter.com/NaCyoa8kQv.

    The last four games have been excellent for Peterson and showed why he was the projected top pick entering last college basketball season. He has scored over 20 points in those last four, including a 26-point outburst against the Timberwolves. Peterson's shooting from beyond the arc has also been impressive during that stretch.

    Industry observers note that with so many key veterans out for Utah at the moment, Peterson has been pushed into an expanded role. It's going to be that way for the next several weeks. With Utah's season already looking like a mess, the organization's top priority should be developing Peterson into a primary option. If the last week is any indication, Peterson could get back into a very competitive Rookie of the Year race.

    Thursday was a rough shooting night for Dybantsa during the most entertaining Wizards game of the entire season, which ended with a double-overtime loss at home to Detroit. Dybantsa shot just 2 of 10 and finished with five points -- the first time in his career he finished in single digits. However, Dybantsa did hit a clutch mid-range jumper to send the game to double overtime.

    Outside of Kyshawn George taking seven shots in 26 minutes due to foul trouble, Dybantsa attempted the second-fewest (10) shots among starters. Dybantsa also didn't get to the free-throw line, which was shocking because one of his greatest strengths is drawing fouls.

    Trae Young (23), Anthony Davis (21) and Alex Sarr (14) all attempted more shots against the Pistons. Dybantsa did contribute in other ways (eight rebounds and four assists), but that kind of game underlines why I'm hesitant to put Dybantsa in Tier 1 of the Rookie of the Year conversation. And trust me, it's not because of talent. Dybantsa is awesome.

    In a recent development, AJ DYBANTSA FORCES 2OT!IN THE CLUTCH THE #1 PICK COMES THROUGH. pic.twitter.com/lsqG6bGNXX.

    Industry observers note that the concern is that, with Davis and Young on the roster, the volume of shots for Dybantsa might not be there for him to win Rookie of the Year. Acuff is the primary option for the Kings. Lendeborg is now the de facto No. 1 option with Curry set to miss the next month. Peterson has been thrust into a larger role with veterans out. Boozer is putting up numbers on a nightly basis despite having a lower usage rate than Acuff, Wilson and Lendeborg.

    Dybantsa is the face and future of Washington's franchise. He should be featured as such. If he isn't, he will likely fall behind the top three players in the race for the majority of the season.

    According to recent reports, even outside of the top four names, several other rookies have performed well this season. Although they will likely be longshots to win Rookie of the Year, here are some sleepers and others worthy of recognition.

    It has been revealed that it's time for the Clippers to start Wagler. The impact he has on the game off the bench is impressive. If he is given more minutes, he will shine. The stat that stands out about Wagler is that he is shooting better from beyond the arc (35.4%) than inside the arc (29.7%). He is shooting 86% from the free-throw line, which is a positive indicator for future shooting success. He will be fine.

    Mara was a player I thought could make an immediate impact as a rookie because of his defense and offensive efficiency. Mara is shooting 60.3% from the field and is blocking 1.8 shots per game. Check and check.

    It has been revealed that the flashes from Brown are must-see TV. It's the same sentiment as during his time at Louisville. If you put together a highlight tape of Brown's best plays, you would think he's the best guard in the class. He has played in just seven games this season and hasn't started because of a minutes restriction.

    It has been revealed that flemings has been great in spots off the bench and even as a starter. He is one of the most efficient rookies in the class -- albeit on lower volume than his peers -- and is shooting 52.1% from the field, 42.9% from 3 and 72.7% from the charity stripe.

    #26901. Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1290 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1290 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The substantial prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal.
    • There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.
    • Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The substantial prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. We've seen and will continue to see predictions that he's going to land a deal of around 8-10 years and topping $400 million. The knee-jerk reaction to such prognostications in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

    Let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.

    Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

    It has been revealed that since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

    The recent track record here notes this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

    Industry observers note that there isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

    According to recent reports, he's stellar. Pretty much all the time.

    Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the big-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

    There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

    Recent findings suggest that we'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a new procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

    The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

    Skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

    I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

    Again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. If he signs an eight-year deal, it'll run through his age-37 season.

    For those so worried about the long-term finances of the team owner who ends up signing Skubal, are you sure you're really worried that he won't be productive through five, six, seven or even all eight years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

    Industry observers note that A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

    Recent findings suggest that yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

    Recent findings suggest that gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

    Stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

    In a recent development, justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

    Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

    In a recent development, david Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

    According to recent reports, corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

    According to recent reports, zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

    CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

    It has been revealed that max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

    Sources indicate that we can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

    By this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:.

    Are you sure a 10-year, $400 million deal for this guy would be a "risk?".

    I think we could argue that it would be a bargain.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, A lot was made about the Fresh England Patriots facing a historically easy schedule during their surprise run to Super Bowl LX in 2025. What flew more under the radar, however, was how remarkably healthy they were throughout that campaign. Between Week 1 and Super Bowl LX, New England placed just eight players on injured reserve. That's an astounding run of good health amid an NFL season, but water has found its level in 2026 in dramatic fashion.

    The Patriots have been hit hard by injuries through 10 weeks of their 2026 season, and Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany may have delivered the kill shot.

    At the tail end of the opening drive, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury that is reportedly feared to be season-ending. Specifically, there's concern the third-year quarterback may have fractured his ankle after taking a sack by pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson. Maye stayed in Germany for additional testing to see if surgery is required. He is already expected to miss a substantial period of time, possibly even the entire season.

    That would be the death blow for a New England team already marred by injuries throughout 2026.

    For instance, as noted by the Boston Herald, 16 of the Patriots' 22 Week 1 starters have either missed games or been knocked out of contests so far due to injury. That doesn't even include players like wideout Romeo Doubs, TreVeyon Henderson, and other rotational contributors.

    For a broader view of just how much of a bit the injury bug has taken, here's a look at some notable Patriots who've missed time so far this season due to injury (courtesy of Pro Football Reference).

    High ankle sprain, knee, hamstring.

    It has been revealed that in total, 28 different players have been listed as out on gameday or placed on injured reserve heading into the Week 10 game in Germany, not including the loss of Maye that happened during that game. This is an entirely different circumstance than the health the team enjoyed last season, and it's adding up. New England now lost three of their last four games, moving to 5-5 entering the Week 11 bye.

    Sources indicate that injuries reared their head almost instantly at the start of 2026. Most notably, A.J. Brown — the club's offseason prize acquired in a blockbuster trade with the Eagles — suffered a high ankle sprain in his Patriots debut. That landed him on injured reserve, keeping him out until Week 6. He missed two more games in Weeks 8 and 9, then left Sunday's contest early with a hamstring injury.

    The hits have kept coming for Mike Vrabel's team, and they aren't limited to players who've missed games we highlighted above. There are plenty of Patriots who have been limited by injury, but still been able to suit up. Safety Kevin Byard (chest), left tackle Will Campbell (knee), linebacker Christian Elliss (chest), tight end Hunter Henry (foot), right tackle Morgan Moses (foot), running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), defensive back Charles Woods (shoulder, hamstring), and safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) have all popped up on the injury report throughout the season.

    It has been revealed that these are foundational pieces to what Fresh England hoped would be a 2026 season that carried the momentum of last year's Super Bowl run and let them contend again. Instead, injuries — coupled with poor execution on the field — have turned a season once looked at with such promise upside down, especially in the wake of Maye's potential season-ender.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas.
    • Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.
    • We have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas. Though we haven't seen any major moves this offseason, we have seen an uptick in rumors in the past few days and that isn't a coincidence. Put a bunch of reporters and front-office execs in the same area for three or four days and chatter picks up, even if there isn't a ton of actual substance behind it.

    Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.

    We have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal. Phillips ranked No. 34 on our top 50 free agent list.

    Phillips, a 32-year-old right-hander, has been a setup man or closer for the Dodgers for the last several seasons. In returning from surgery last season, he appeared in 31 games, pitching to a 3.46 ERA and 1.07 WHIP with 33 strikeouts in 26 innings. The majority of his closing experience came in 2023 when he had 24 saves in 27 chances.

    The Braves' closer last season was Raisel Iglesias, but he's a free agent. Holdover Robert Suarez could take over those duties while Phillips, lefty Dylan Lee and youngster Didier Fuentes are also in the late-inning mix.

    Industry observers note that the Blue Jays went from one of the best offensive teams in 2025 to one of the worst in 2026. They'd love a substantial bounceback from Vladimir Guerrero Jr., among other positive movements, but they also look for outside help. Might that help come in the form of free agent infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr.?

    The Jays have met with representatives for Chisholm, reports Sportsnet.

    Chisholm, 28, hit .231/.312/.399 last season, but had a huge 2025 and any signing team would be hoping for the 2025 version of Chisholm.

    The Jays do have a capable incumbent second baseman in Ernie Clement, but either Clement or Chisholm can be used in the outfield and the Blue Jays certainly need outfield upgrades.

    The Phillies have been telling opposing teams that they are not "locked into anything" regarding their current outfield situation, according to The Athletic, so much so that All-Star outfielder Brandon Marsh is available in a trade.

    As things stand, with Bryce Harper moving back to first base, the Phillies would have Bryan De La Cruz in right, Justin Crawford in center and Marsh in left, but that all seems pretty fluid as they look to upgrade the ballclub and keep that window of contention open.

    Industry observers note that marsh, 28, had a stellar start last season, leading to his first-ever All-Star Game. Through July 1, he hit .319/.352/.530. The rest of the way, however, he slashed .177/.241/.241, dragging him down overall to a 90 OPS+ and 0.4 WAR on the season.

    The Mariners have shown interest in free agent left fielder Ian Happ, per MLB Network.

    Sources indicate that happ, 32, has spent his entire 10-year MLB career with the Cubs, who drafted him in the first round all the way back in 2015. He was pretty consistent from 2022-25, averaging 3.9 WAR with a .251/.347/.433 (118 OPS+) line and winning four Gold Gloves. Last season, though, he dipped to .218/.326/.412 (103 OPS+) with 2.7 WAR. He still topped 20 home runs for the fifth time in the last six years.

    The Mariners have a vacancy in left field with Randy Arozarena having hit free agency and a need to upgrade their offense.

    Yesterday's major news was the Yankees' interest in free agent first/third baseman Alec Bohm and The Athletic reports that we can now add the Mets to the list of suitors.

    Recent findings suggest that bohm hit .249/.315/.383 (87 OPS+) with 15 home runs, 88 RBI and -0.2 WAR last season. It might be surprising to see him garnering such interest on the open market, but there isn't much right-handed power out there and Bohm finished last season strong (.318/.402/.453 in his last 42 games). The Mets, meanwhile, are desperate for help at the cold corner after last year's disastrous Jorge Polanco experiment. Jared Young did provide a glimmer of hope at first base before suffering a concussion in September while colliding with a teammate on a play.

    Free agent starting pitcher Dustin May has a decent market right now, according to MLB Network, with at least the Cubs, White Sox, Padres and Astros having shown interest in the right-hander.

    May, 29, made 31 starts between the Cardinals and Brewers last season, going 7-9 with a 4.70 ERA in 145 ⅔ innings. He showed flashes of brilliance with the Cardinals and had a stretch from April 10 to June 15 during which he posted a 2.54 ERA in 12 starts, but in the end there was plenty of inconsistency and even bad, forcing him into a bullpen role in the playoffs for the champion Brewers.

    Free agent catcher Ryan Jeffers has been extended the qualifying offer from the Twins, meaning he has to decide by net Tuesday whether to accept the one-year, $23.15 million contract or hit free agency. There's nothing that says a team can't re-sign a player after he declines their qualifying offer, of course, and it sounds like that path is possible in this case.

    Recent findings suggest that jeffers will decline the QO and the Twins are interested in reaching a multi-year deal to bring him back, reports the Minnesota Star-Tribune. Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 with 14 home runs for Minnesota in 2026, a standout line for a catcher, though he missed several months with a broken hamate. The Twins do have several catchers in their farm system, including Vahn Lackey, the No. 3 pick in last year's draft, and Eduardo Tait, who headlined the trade return for Jhoan Duran.

    Much has been said and will continue to be said about the 2027 free agent class and how it looks relatively weak, especially on the position-player side, where the best players are the likes of Jazz Chisholm Jr., Seiya Suzuki, and the aforementioned Arozarena and Jeffers.

    As we know, the Rays love to find avenues where they can exploit market inefficiencies. Their latest move might be to hit the trade market with center fielder Jonny DeLuca in anticipation of moving Victor Mesa Jr. to center, according to The Athletic.

    Industry observers note that deLuca, 28, got more playing time than ever before in 2026, appearing in 112 games and getting 370 plate appearances. He hit .266/.300/.429 (101 OPS+) with 11 homers, 50 RBI, 17 steals and 1.7 WAR.

    Fresh off a playoff berth despite the lowest payroll in all of baseball at a paltry $75ish million, the Guardians are planning to increase payroll. Or so they say.

    In a recent development, "We'll go up," club president Chris Antonetti told The Athletic. "We have to.".

    The Guardians hosted six playoff games and made some money there, not to mention that they have a bunch of players hitting arbitration and surely they want to spend more to remain competitive. There's an added wrinkle here, too, which would be that the ownership side is really pushing hard for a salary cap when the upcoming CBA expires in a few weeks. With a cap comes a floor and we've seen MLB float proposals with salary floors in the $180 million range, or well more than double what the Guardians had last season.

    So, yeah, I'd say the Guardians "have to" increase payroll, one way or another.

    Hello football friends, and welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!

    I want to start things off here by letting everyone know that I've come up with a rock-solid fantasy football strategy that's going to win me every game for the rest of the season: I'm going to start any player who's facing the Cowboys defense.

    After watching them give up 46 points to the 49ers on Sunday, there's no way I'm not going to win my league championship. The best part is that the Cowboys play the Titans in Week 11 and almost every Titans player is still available in free agency.

    Now that I've shared my fantasy strategy, let's kick off the newsletter and get to the real stuff.

    Welcome to my favorite part of the Monday newsletter: where I hand out grades for all 32 teams. I spent Sunday night at Paycor Stadium watching the Bengals destroy the Steelers, so let's start our grades there today.

    As for the other grades that we've handed out so far in Week 10, you can check those out here.

    In a recent development, you can't have a week of NFL action without winners and losers, so here are some of them. It was an ugly week for the NFL teams in Texas, who both ended up on our Week 10 losers' list.

    Carter Bahns put together this week's list of winners and losers, and we'll check out his losers below.

    If you want to see Carter's list of winners (and a couple of other losers), be sure to click here.

    It has been revealed that everyone on the internet loves to overreact, and that's especially true when we're talking about the NFL. Zach Pereles looked at several things that happened during Week 10, so decide for yourself whether we're all overreacting.

    According to recent reports, statement: Patriots will miss the playoffs.Overreaction or reality: Reality. This game was a microcosm of the entire season. There were massive expectations around the Brown addition. He has fallen woefully short, first with a knee injury, then an ankle injury, and now a hamstring injury. With Romeo Doubs also on IR, the wide receiver corps looks nothing like New England envisioned. The defense also looks nothing like New England hoped. Simply put, this isn't a playoff team.

    Industry observers note that statement: Kirk Cousins trade just saved the Vikings' season.Overreaction or reality: Reality. The Vikings' 30-10 destruction of the Packers revealed, once again, just how good this defense is. Not just good - great. The type of defense you cannot waste. And the Vikings' trade for Kirk Cousins showed the Vikings won't waste it. Cousins went 21-for-31 for 207 yards, a pair of touchdowns, and an interception. It wasn't amazing by any stretch, and the Packers turning the ball over four times helped. But perhaps that's the point here. Minnesota doesn't need amazing quarterback play. It just needs not-awful play. All the Vikings needed was capable quarterback play. They got it from someone who only joined the team five days ago. Outstanding work all around.

    Statement: Falcons should bench Michael Penix Jr. Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. Michael Penix Jr. looked awful in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs. He was all over the place, completing just 23 of his 43 pass attempts. He threw an awful pick late. He looked completely flustered when he got pressured - and even before he got pressured. Penix's play has taken a nosedive since his three-touchdown Week 7 against the 49ers. He threw four interceptions in monsoon-like conditions against the Buccaneers in Week 8. Last week, he threw another bad pick against the Bengals. This week was another brutal outing. Unfortunately, the Falcons don't have a better option. Tua Tagovailoa has looked terrible in the few moments he's actually been available, and his penchant for turnovers, poor arm strength, and lack of mobility are near non-starters. It's pretty bleak in Atlanta, which will certainly have a upcoming quarterback next year.

    We're just over one month into the season, and the Pittsburgh Penguins are three games below .500 and 15th in the Eastern Conference. This slow start could create some very tough decisions for general manager Kyle Dubas.

    On the heels of a resurgence in 2025-26, the Penguins haven't quite been able to recapture that magic yet, and there's a good chance Father Time has something to do with that. The core of this team is one of the oldest in the NHL, and not even Sidney Crosby can remain an elite superstar forever.

    If the Penguins continue to occupy the bottom of the Eastern Conference, Dubas will face tough decisions. He has a handful of stars on expiring or soon-to-be-expiring contracts, and those players could be very attractive to other teams. Erik Karlsson seems like and obvious trade candidate. As does Rickard Rakell.

    But if there was a fire sale, would Dubas go as far as shipping out a franchise icon?

    According to recent reports, look, it's still very early, and there are reasons to believe a turnaround is coming. The Penguins' five-on-five numbers are far better than the results indicate, and Crosby is fully capable of shaking off a slow start and hitting another level.

    If things don't improve, though, things could get very interesting in Pittsburgh. As the Pens sink, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.

    Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

    📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5230 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning.
    • The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image.
    • All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

    The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

    All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

    In a recent development, A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

    In a recent development, joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

    Recent findings suggest that “It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca remarked, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

    Sources indicate that his team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

    Industry observers note that maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

    Industry observers note that momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

    Industry observers note that marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

    Marco Rose, their fresh manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he stated. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

    His team demonstrated an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

    It has been revealed that they could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his fresh manager.

    Industry observers note that "That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

    No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

    It has been revealed that city will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “fresh Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

    There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca stated “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

    Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a upcoming season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

    Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2.

    It has been revealed that the Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

    According to recent reports, emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

    BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez has won the 2026 American League MVP, the BBWAA announced Thursday night.
    • The Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing AL teams.
    • Recent findings suggest that alvarez, 29, bounced back from an injury-riddled disaster in 2025, during which he only played in 48 games.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez has won the 2026 American League MVP, the BBWAA announced Thursday night.

    The Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing AL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

    Recent findings suggest that alvarez, 29, bounced back from an injury-riddled disaster in 2025, during which he only played in 48 games. This time around, he avoided the IL and appeared in 158 games. He hit .316/.432/.601 (190 OPS+) with 34 doubles, a triple, 42 home runs, 106 RBI, 105 runs and 6.8 WAR. He made a late run at the Triple Crown, missing out by one home run and seven RBI. He did lead the majors in all three triple slash categories, though, leading in average by five points, on-base percentage by a whopping 42 points -- he led the majors in walks -- and 31 points in slugging percentage. Add the latter two and his OPS victory was 90 points -- 1.033 to second place's .943 (National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong).

    The only players in MLB history to lead the majors in all three triple slash categories:.

    Alvarez becomes just the third Astros player to win MVP after Jeff Bagwell in 1994 and Jose Altuve in 2017.

    Rays third baseman Junior Caminero finished in second. At age 22, he played all 162 games, leading the Rays to the best AL record. He hit .276/.360/.524 (144 OPS+) with 42 home runs, 101 RBI and 100 runs, posting a 5.7 WAR. He's already made history, too, as the Rays had previously never had a player finish in the top five of MVP voting.

    Sources indicate that royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. came in third. This is now his fourth straight season in the top seven and third straight season in the top four. He finished second in 2024. This season, he hit .281/.359/.441 (125 OPS+) with 33 doubles, 18 homers, 54 RBI, 94 runs, 45 steals and 6.7 WAR.

    #26891. Dejounte Murray landing spots: Three possible destinations after Pelicans guard requests trade
