    Dejounte Murray landing spots: Three possible destinations after Pelicans guard requests trade

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1201 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, we have our first trade request of the 2026-27 NBA season.
    • Murray has remained in the starting lineup for the Pelicans, but Newly introduced Orleans is 1-8 in the games he's played.
    • Meanwhile, Murray has made his displeasure public on several occasions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, we have our first trade request of the 2026-27 NBA season. If you had Dejounte Murray on your bingo card, congratulations. The 2022 All-Star landed with the Upcoming Orleans Pelicans before the 2024-25 season, but his tenure there has been a mess and he requested a trade on Friday. He played 31 games in his first season, shooting worse than he ever had before tearing his Achilles. He returned late last season and played well, but the beginning of this season has been a mess.

    Murray has remained in the starting lineup for the Pelicans, but Newly introduced Orleans is 1-8 in the games he's played. They've lost his minutes by over 14 points per 100 possessions, he's shot poorly from basically everywhere on the floor, and he hasn't been a consistently impactful defender since he played for the San Antonio Spurs.

    Meanwhile, Murray has made his displeasure public on several occasions.

    It has been revealed that at this stage, Murray's trade value is likely minimal. If a deal comes, it will likely involve a similarly bloated, multi-year contract attached to a player that a team is eager to move. Essentially, we're looking for "problem for problem" type of trades.

    Three destinations make some degree of immediate sense.

    The Suns are the first team to register known interest, according to Chris Haynes. Earlier this season, Haynes reported that the team's lack of a point guard had created frustration in the locker room. Phoenix started the season 1-5, but has since won four of its last five to somewhat right the ship.

    In a recent development, still, the Jalen Green experience has been a borderline disaster for Phoenix. The Suns have a staggering -15.7 net rating when Green plays and a +10.2 net rating when he sits. The former No. 2 overall pick was one of the primary pieces returned in the Kevin Durant trade, but his shooting has fallen off a cliff. He provides none of the playmaking that Devin Booker needs in a backcourt mate (which is part of why the Suns have fared so much better with Collin Gillespie on the floor in his place), and his defense is mostly nonexistent.

    Both Murray and Green have player options for next season, with Green set to make $36 million and $30 million owed to Murray. The notoriously stingy Pelicans might insist on some form of compensation for taking on that extra money, but the premise here would essentially be the "problem for problem" structure we suggested above. With Murray gone, Jeremiah Fears could be the unquestioned starting point guard for the Pelicans. Green would either come off the bench or slot next to him at shooting guard, while Murray would be closer to the point guard archetype that Booker prefers.

    Recent findings suggest that it's by no means a perfect fit. Murray's weakness as a 3-point shooter would be problematic as the Suns have lost quite a bit of shooting since last season, and the Pelicans frankly have too many talented, shoot-first players as is. But it's at least an attempt at addressing real challenges for both sides. The rebuilding Pelicans might at least like to take a look at a supremely gifted athlete, while the Suns would hope to get the point guard they feel they've lacked.

    Andrew Wiggins has really struggled to fit into the new, Giannis Antetokounmpo-centric version of the Heat. The former No. 1 overall pick is averaging less than nine points per game on some of the worst shooting numbers of his career. His usually steady defense has slipped a fair bit on a unit that has been enormously disappointing as a whole, and, offensively, Miami's lack of a genuine shot-creating guard has proven problematic early in the season.

    It has been revealed that the Heat need a more reliable shot-generator than Murray, but after spending most of their assets on Antetokounmpo, their options are somewhat limited. This sort of swap would essentially be a bet that going from one of the NBA's worst organizations to one of its best could rejuvenate a former All-Star. Fitting a point guard that shoots poorly from deep on a Giannis team would be pretty problematic, but Miami would presumably stagger the two of them to limit their minutes together.

    It has been revealed that such a swap would appeal to New Orleans for a few reasons. The first is contractual. Wiggins signed an unusual contract last offseason. He had a player option for the 2026-27 season, but rather than decline it and sign an entirely new deal, he picked it up and added a cheap two-year extension on the back end. He is making over $30 million this season but will dip to $16.3 million next season. That makes him an ideal trade target for a team that wants to save money. He can match salary with Murray in a trade now, but cost far less next year.

    Industry observers note that and then of course, there's the chance that Wiggins bounces back on a team that plays a bit more traditionally than Antetokounmpo-led teams can. Pelicans wings Trey Murphy III and Herbert Jones have been rumor mill fixtures for years, and with Saddiq Bey in place and a potentially rejuvenated Wiggins incoming, New Orleans would potentially feel a bit more comfortable cashing one of those other forwards out for draft picks since they'd have replacements in the building.

    Murray is emphatically not the sort of player that the Hornets tend to target, especially at point guard. Charlotte wants to bomb 3-pointers. That is not now, nor has it ever been Murray's game. When Charlotte traded LaMelo Ball, it expected to be able to sustain a somewhat respectable offense with Coby White in his place and Kon Knueppel ascending. Well, Ball is starring in Minnesota and White and Knueppel have barely played.

    The Hornets knew they were taking a step back this season with the Ball trade. They probably didn't expect the NBA's worst offensive rating, highest turnover rate and lowest true shooting percentage. Bringing in Murray could at least provide them with a stabilizing force at point guard, someone who could raise the floor enough to properly evaluate everyone else on the team moving forward.

    The Hornets have a $40.8 million trade exception generated from moving Ball and almost $30 million in room below the tax line. They could nearly absorb Murray outright without sending out another contract, and they've shown a willingness to take on salary in exchange for draft capital. That would be the idea here.

    According to recent reports, the Hornets are not taking on Murray's player option for next season lightly. The Pelicans would have to make it worth their while with some form of first-round draft compensation. The Pelicans are probably hesitant to do so after all of the criticism they (justifiably) received for the Derik Queen trade, but Charlotte is probably the only team that can offer real financial relief for Murray at this point. If that's a priority, there might be a conversation here. If the Pelicans expect the Hornets to treat Murray as a real asset, the Hornets almost certainly pass.

    #26889. Joe Burrow isn't just chasing MVP, he's chasing the greatest passing season ever

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (856 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Joe Burrow isn't just chasing MVP, he's chasing the greatest passing season ever

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Two years ago, Joe Burrow resigned himself to the fact that, despite having an MVP-caliber season, he likely wouldn't win the award based on the Bengals' 9-8 record and absence from the playoffs.
    • "I'll win one one day," Burrow mentioned at the time.
    • According to recent reports, already the MVP favorite entering Sunday night's game against the Steelers, Burrow is now the clear front-runner.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Two years ago, Joe Burrow resigned himself to the fact that, despite having an MVP-caliber season, he likely wouldn't win the award based on the Bengals' 9-8 record and absence from the playoffs.

    "I'll win one one day," Burrow mentioned at the time.

    That time could very well be now.

    According to recent reports, already the MVP favorite entering Sunday night's game against the Steelers, Burrow is now the clear front-runner. Against a team that defeated the Bengals back in Week 3, Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns while completing nearly 80% of his passes. It could have been much more, but Bengals coach Zac Taylor called off the dogs and took Burrow out of the game midway through the fourth quarter of Cincinnati's eventual 38-18 win.

    According to recent reports, playing in the background of Burrow's performance were MVP chants from Bengals fans, which Taylor acknowledged hearing throughout the game. Taylor, as you'd expect, agrees with that sentiment.

    "I mean it would be impossible to say that anyone is playing better," Taylor noted. "I'm not watching every game ... but I bet the people that aren't talking about him aren't watching our games, because if you are, it's really hard to say that he is not the best player on planet Earth.".

    Burrow's performance not only strengthened his MVP case but also put him on a historic trajectory with eight games to play in the 2026 regular season.

    Burrow is one of only five quarterbacks in NFL history with over 30 total touchdowns through nine games, according to CBS Sports Research. The other four won league MVP: Tom Brady in 2007, Aaron Rodgers in 2011, Peyton Manning in 2013 and Patrick Mahomes in 2018.

    According to recent reports, burrow joined Manning on Sunday night as the only two quarterbacks with five consecutive games with at least four touchdowns. Over that span, Burrow has thrown 20 touchdowns (against just three interceptions) and ran for two more while completing 78% of his passes. The Bengals won each of those games while taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North.

    Burrow is on pace to become the third quarterback to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season. He is on pace to throw 51 touchdown passes, which would put him behind Manning's 55 during the 2013 season. Burrow's 5,279 yards would rank fourth behind Manning (5,477 in 2013), Drew Brees (5,476 in 2011) and Brady (5,316 in 2021).

    Recent findings suggest that while he's not on pace to break those records, Burrow is on track to create his own category for quarterback excellence by becoming the first quarterback to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season while also completing 70% of his passes. If he does that, he will have a strong argument when it comes to having the greatest passing season in league history.

    Industry observers note that burrow's success can be attributed to his growth as well as improvements across Cincinnati's entire roster. The Bengals' offensive line has improved, and the defense has greatly benefited from the offseason acquisitions of Dexter Lawrence, Boye Mafe and Bryan Cook. It goes without saying that the trio of running back Chase Brown and wideouts Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have helped, too.

    It has been revealed that now in his fourth season, Brown has established himself as one of the league's more versatile running backs. He had two touchdown catches on Sunday night and was second on the team with eight receptions.

    "We know what we have in Chase," Burrow said. "He's a significant-time playmaker for us. When people devote too many resources to stopping the guys on the outside, Chase can beat you in a lot of different ways.".

    That's now two TDs for Chase Brown and FOUR TDs for Joe Burrow 😎PITvsCIN on NBC/PeacockStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/svZHSPGVmC.

    Chase and Higgins are the league's best receiving duo and have been for some time. They're on pace to become the first pair of teammates to each post 1,500-yard receiving seasons in the same year.

    Higgins is on pace to record a career-high 1,556 receiving yards this season, while Chase (who actually trailed Higgins in receiving yards prior to Sunday night) is on pace to have 1,658 receiving yards this season after catching 11 passes for 231 yards against Pittsburgh.

    Joe Burrow throws it deep to Ja'Marr Chase for the first down 🚀PITvsCIN on NBC/PeacockStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o97edw3OV3.

    Looking ahead, the Bengals have only three remaining games against teams with winning records (Cleveland in Weeks 13 and 18, the Chiefs in Week 14). The Browns have given Burrow fits in the past, but Myles Garrett (now a Ram) was a substantial reason for that. Burrow has historically played well against the Chiefs.

    It has been revealed that as Burrow alluded to in his postgame press conference, it's only mid-November with a lot of football left to play. That may be true, but it is also true that Burrow has put himself -- and his team -- in position to have a memorable, and perhaps historic, season.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong won the National League MVP award for the 2026 season unanimously, the BBWAA revealed Thursday evening.

    The Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing NL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

    Though the results were unsurprising by the time the year wound down, going back to the start of the season, this marks a huge upset. Shohei Ohtani was the overwhelming favorite to win the award heading into the season and maintained favorite status through the All-Star break. A combination of his injuries and PCA's monster season turned the tide late.

    Appearing in all 162 games, Crow-Armstrong hit .280/.372/.570 (156 OPS+) with 31 doubles, eight triples, 45 home runs, 107 RBI, 119 runs, 41 steals and 9.8 WAR. He led the majors in WAR, runs, home runs and total bases while leading the NL in slugging, OPS and OPS+. He became the seventh player in MLB history to join the 40-40 club (40 home runs and 40 steals in the same season). Further, he led the majors in multiple advanced defensive metrics, putting together one of the great all-around seasons from a position player in recent memory.

    PCA joins the following list of Cubs to win MVP:.

    Ohtani, the four-time MVP, finishes in second. At the plate, Ohtani hit .275/.377/.512 with 26 doubles, four triples, 30 home runs, 81 RBI, 89 runs, 11 steals and 3.2 WAR. On the mound, he was 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and 95 strikeouts in 85 ⅔ innings with 3.2 WAR.

    The nationally underrated Brewers second baseman Brice Turang finishes in third. He still hasn't made an All-Star Game, though he did start 2026 as a member of Team USA in the World Baseball Classic. In the regular season, Turang hit .268/.366/.450 (124 OPS+) with 37 doubles, three triples, 21 home runs, 100 RBI, 102 runs and 7.3 WAR, rating out as one of the best defenders in baseball.

    • Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that the Broncos backing out of the deal sets a bad precedent, and that this is a "loophole" the NFL needs to investigate.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that at the trade deadline last Tuesday, a rare inter-division deal was agreed to between the Los Angeles Chargers and Denver Broncos. The Broncos agreed to send the Chargers a fourth-round pick and a future fifth-round pick in exchange for linebacker Daiyan Henley, but the deal fell apart.

    The trade was nixed after Denver reportedly found an issue with Henley's knee during his physical. ESPN reported that the Broncos then approached the Chargers and attempted to renegotiate the compensation. Denver still wanted to acquire the linebacker, but just not at the price George Paton and Sean Payton initially agreed to.

    Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that the Broncos backing out of the deal sets a bad precedent, and that this is a "loophole" the NFL needs to investigate.

    Recent findings suggest that "That's why it's a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that," Harbaugh said. "It's a medical grade. It's a pass/fail for a medical trade. They told us they weren't going to pass him if there was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon. They would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a 'fill in the blank.' I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is.".

    Recent findings suggest that the Broncos were on a bye in Week 10, so we had to wait until Monday to hear their side of the story. Payton was indeed asked about the trade falling through, but didn't offer many details.

    According to recent reports, "I'm not going to get into the specifics. He's prospect we thought of — and still do — very highly of. It just didn't work out," Payton said, via The Athletic. "I'll leave it at that.".

    What did Payton think about Harbaugh's comments regarding a "loophole?".

    "Listen, I thought I saw it all," he mentioned, via Mile High Sports. "There's no loophole. It's just part of the trade process, every step of the way.".

    According to recent reports, whatever the Broncos found in Henley's knee hasn't affected him yet. He hasn't missed a game due to injury in each of the last two seasons. In eight games played this season, Henley has recorded 51 tackles, half a sack, two passes defensed and an interception. The Broncos and Chargers will see each other again in the regular-season finale when Week 18 rolls around.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.
    • Crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.

    Crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors. He hit .280/.372/.570 with stellar defense, led the league in home runs (tied with Kyle Schwarber) and massively upgraded his on-base skills. Now, just a few months shy of his 25th birthday, he has an MVP to his name.

    So what's next? To answer that, we'll look backwards.

    Sources indicate that since integration, only eight center fielders have posted at least 8.0 WAR in a season age-25 or younger: Willie Mays, Mickey Mantle, Willie Davis, César Cedeño, Ken Griffey Jr., Andruw Jones, Mike Trout and PCA. The only ones to top PCA's 9.8 were Mays, Mantle and Trout. If we went back to pre-integration, Tris Speaker and Ty Cobb were the only others who bested PCA here.

    What road map will PCA's career follow?

    Willie Davis was an inconsistent hitter through his age-23 season but had flashed a nice power-speed combo. Sound familiar? That gaudy 8.4 WAR total in 1964, though, was driven largely by monster defensive metrics. Davis hit .294/.316/.413 (110 OPS+) with 23 doubles, seven triples, 12 home runs, 77 RBI, 91 runs and 42 steals. There's little doubt that PCA's 2026 season dwarfed this one overall, and Davis was far behind Mays (11.0) for the league lead in WAR.

    Recent findings suggest that for the rest of his career, Davis averaged 3.1 WAR per season, and though he had good years, he never reached 6.0 WAR again. The WAR figure was, again, mostly driven by defense. He had several good offensive seasons, but his only 20-homer season came in 1962 when he was 22, two years prior to his career year.

    Recent findings suggest that davis' career probably looks a lot like PCA's apparent upside before his home run barrage in the first half of 2025. He racked up over 60 career WAR with a decent batting average, excellent defense and excellent baserunning.

    With PCA reaching 30-30 last year and 40-40 this year, though, the bar has been raised.

    Sources indicate that césar Cedeño followed up his 8.0 WAR season with a 7.4 season at age 22 and 5.8 at age 23. He was very good through age 29 and, in fact, the most statistically similar player through both ages 27 and 28 was Hall of Famer Carl Yastrzemski. Things fell apart after that. As a quick and easy way to illustrate it, Cedeño amassed 49.4 WAR through his age-29 season and only 3.6 in his final six years.

    Recent findings suggest that it's easier to remember that Andruw Jones' career unfolded in similar fashion because we witnessed it not too long ago and then discussed his Hall of Fame candidacy during his nine turns on the ballot before he finally made it in. In Jones' 12 Braves' season, he racked up 368 home runs, 1,117 RBI and 61 WAR while generally being considered the best defensive center fielder in baseball. Once he left, in time for his age-31 season, Jones accrued just 1.7 WAR in his last five seasons.

    Through Jones' age-28 season, the most statistically similar players are Bryce Harper and Frank Robinson.

    To compare these two to Crow-Armstrong, the argument would be that he'll continue to look like one of the best players in baseball -- even if taking steps backward from being the very best in the 2026 regular season -- before falling apart once he's around 30 years old.

    Sources indicate that certainly possible, but given the adjustments he's already not only been willing to make at the plate, but eager to make, I'm just not seeing him all of a sudden hitting a wall. Sure, at some point he'll start losing speed and that'll affect his defensive range and baserunning, but why would the plate skills deteriorate all of a sudden?

    Then again, few saw it coming with Jones.

    All three of these players were on the path to having an argument as the best player in history before injuries derailed them in their 30s and left them as mere "all-time greats.".

    In a recent development, through Mickey Mantle's age-30 season, he had 90.7 WAR. He averaged 121 games per year in his final six seasons, putting up 19.5 WAR. Through  Ken Griffey Jr.'s age-30 season, he had 76.2 WAR. He played 10 more seasons, but only amassed 7.6 more WAR. Through Mike Trout's age-27 season, he had 72.1 WAR (his top statistical similars were Mantle, Robinson and Griffey). We'll skip 2020 for obvious reasons, but since then he's averaged 90 games and 3.0 WAR per season.

    Sources indicate that even with the drop-offs, it would be surprising to see Crow-Armstrong reach this level because it's surprising to see any player reach this lofty standard. In career WAR among center fielders, Mantle is fourth, Trout is fifth and Griffey is sixth. They trail only Cobb, Speaker and the guy we're going to discuss next. Joe DiMaggio is seventh.

    Despite the lofty standard PCA set for himself in 2026, coming close to Willie Mays' career would be jaw-droppingly shocking, and that is absolutely not intended as a slight.

    In a recent development, mays has an argument as the greatest player in baseball history and he put himself in that discussion by being good at everything and doing it all with great longevity. From his age-23 to -35 seasons, he led the majors in WAR eight times, leading the NL an additional two times. His worst seasons in that timeframe were 7.6 and 7.8 WAR. In that span, he also led the league in runs twice, hits once, triples three times, home runs three times, stolen bases four times, average once, on-base percentage once, slugging percentage five times and OPS five times.

    Recent findings suggest that mays even posted 5.2 WAR at age 39 and 6.3 at age 40. He led the NL with a .425 OBP when he was 40 years old! He hit .345/.411/.667 at age 23.

    Mays' 156.2 career WAR ranks third among position players all-time behind two guys you might have heard of: Barry Bonds (162.8) and Babe Ruth (162.3).

    I feel pretty strongly Pete Crow-Armstrong isn't headed for a run at this career and that's just fine.

    According to recent reports, the realistic long-term range for the 2026 National League MVP seems somewhere between Cedeño and Mantle. It's a wide variance of outcomes between those two, obviously, as well it should be when the player we discuss is only 24 years old. For his name to be mentioned among these at all is a testament to the year Crow-Armstrong just put together.

    #26881. Breaking: Sophomore bounce-back or letdown? Will Campbell quietly improving, Ashton Jeanty among 2025 first-round busts

    Breaking: Sophomore bounce-back or letdown? Will Campbell quietly improving, Ashton Jeanty among 2025 first-round busts

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2817 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Some positions take longer to evaluate than others, but a year and a half is enough of a sample size to determine whether or not most of the top 2025 NFL Draft picks are on track to live up to expectations.
    • Recent findings suggest that for those who opened their careers with quiet rookie seasons, it is imperative to turn things around in 2026 and solidify or expand upon their roles before it is too late.
    • Contract extensions are not far off in the distance for last year's top-producing early draft picks, while those who continue to disappoint may find themselves reaching free agency before they reach their option year unless they correct their course.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Some positions take longer to evaluate than others, but a year and a half is enough of a sample size to determine whether or not most of the top 2025 NFL Draft picks are on track to live up to expectations. Some, like Green Bay Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden, have already arrived as stars. Others, including running backs Ashton Jeanty and Omarion Hampton, regressed during the first 10 weeks of their sophomore season. And the jury is still out on some.

    Recent findings suggest that for those who opened their careers with quiet rookie seasons, it is imperative to turn things around in 2026 and solidify or expand upon their roles before it is too late. Consecutive underwhelming campaigns at the start of a career turn projected stars into busts.

    Contract extensions are not far off in the distance for last year's top-producing early draft picks, while those who continue to disappoint may find themselves reaching free agency before they reach their option year unless they correct their course.

    Below are 10 players who underwhelmed as rookies and where they stand just over halfway through their second NFL seasons.

    Sources indicate that the season-long passing numbers and team record still leave a lot to be desired, but Cam Ward might be turning a corner. In his last two games, he posted a personal-best 304 passing yards against the Cincinnati Bengals and the third-best completion rate (71.8%) of his career against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Impressively, those performances came without standout rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate in the lineup.

    Ward's totals are always inflated by the Tennessee Titans' negative game scripts and, thus, their reliance on the pass, but notably, he is beginning to use his high volume more efficiently than in the first year and a half of his career. Ward is completing more passes, getting the ball out quicker, and taking fewer sacks in the process.

    According to recent reports, this all comes as head coach Robert Saleh said that the team has decided to make "a shift philosophically" on how to let Ward handle the offense. "Philosophically, the change was, how are we going to evaluate if he's capable of being the franchise QB if we don't give him the opportunity to prove it," Saleh said during his Monday media availability. "Over the last three weeks, he has done that.".

    It has been revealed that this could be a small blip, or it could be the first sign that Ward is the long-term answer at quarterback for the Titans. He would be far from the only signal-caller to require a long onramp into stardom. For instance, Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence is now among the most renowned passers in football, and his first 25 starts were as much of a slog as Ward's.

    Tennessee has a decision to make in the 2027 draft: use another early pick on a quarterback or commit to Ward. If he keeps playing as he did in Weeks 9 and 10, it should earn a call in his favor.

    Recent findings suggest that A torn LCL in late October 2025 robbed the football world of Travis Hunter's rookie year just when it was starting to take off. Back at full strength in 2026, the two-way player recaptured the momentum he built in the final games of his debut season and built on it, flourishing into the star the Jaguars expected when they traded up to draft him.

    Hunter's offensive snap count (47) indicates he is a defense-first player, but he is not entirely absent from the receiving initiative and has a touchdown to his name. In Week 6, Hunter became the first player since 2002 and just the fifth player since the merger to record a touchdown reception and an interception in the same game, according to Stathead. The Jaguars allowing him to hone in on his defensive role, however, has led to a complete breakout on that side of the ball.

    The Jaguars' busy trade deadline means two stars will join Hunter in the lineup, but he may already be on level footing with Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III in terms of the playmaking he brings. His PFF defensive grade ranks 11th league-wide at cornerback, and the factors behind that evaluation are astounding: he has allowed a passer rating of just 52.8 across 35 targets and has hauled in the first three interceptions of his career. That figure leads all Jaguars defensive backs and is 10th in the league among all defensive backs with at least 20 targets, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. The athleticism he displayed on his latest takeaway was uncanny for a cornerback.

    It has been revealed that travis Hunter dives for the interception! 🔥JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RKvGzhsi9H.

    Will Campbell just completed his worst game of the season. The six pressures, 18.2% pressure rate, and two sacks he allowed in the Newly introduced England Patriots' loss to the Detroit Lions were all season highs. Even worse, one of those sacks was the one that injured Drake Maye's ankle. It was a stain on what has otherwise quietly been a better year than the disastrous rookie campaign he turned in last fall.

    Even before the costly performance in Munich, Campbell was not exactly considered a star on the left side of the Patriots offensive line. But he is still more reliable than he was in 2025. Fresh England will take any improvement it can squeeze out of the former No. 4 pick. The quick pressures and blatant one-on-one sacks that marred Campbell's injury-impacted rookie year have mostly subsided. He also improved on his pressure rate and sacks allowed (down from 11.2% and 8.5 last year to 7.0% and 2.5 through 10 games, according to Next Gen Stats).

    Sunday's game against Detroit also ballooned those numbers: through the first nine weeks, his 5.9% pressure rate allowed led the team and was fourth among all tackles with at least 100 pass blocks, per Next Gen Stats.

    In a recent development, his mistakes remain devastating, but they are fewer and further between. There is growth here.

    Jeanty was initially projected as a can't-miss running back prospect after his Heisman Trophy finalist senior campaign at Boise State, but he hasn't translated his dominant ball-carrying ability to the NFL. His 41% rushing success rate as a rookie was as underwhelming as the 975 yards and five touchdowns he ran for in the Las Vegas Raiders' disaster of a season, and even though the team has taken a sizable step forward in 2026, Jeanty's production on the ground has regressed by a meaningful margin.

    In a recent development, the skill set Jeanty brought from college made him an ideal fit for an every-down role, but coach Klint Kubiak instead placed him in a timeshare in the rushing department and has gotten more out of him as a receiver than a runner. Jeanty ceded playing time to rookie Mike Washington Jr. and even saw a soft benching in Week 8—which Kubiak said was unrelated to the poor-taste comments he made about the New York Jets defense, but it certainly seemed that way.

    The split between Jeanty and Washington wouldn't be uncalled for if the former were a mid-round pick. But this is last year's No. 6 overall selection. The Raiders are not completely free of fault. The team averages a league-low 1.5 yards before contact per rushing attempt, the third-lowest mark of any team since Pro Football Reference began tracking the stat in 2018. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, the Raiders' 34 tackles for loss on called runs and 58 stuffed runs both lead the league through Week 10 (with the Ravens and Chargers still to play at the time of writing). However, it is evident Las Vegas is not getting their investment's worth from a player who was supposed to be a no-doubt bellcow back.

    It has been revealed that the San Francisco 49ers are consistently great at identifying defensive line talent, so when they made Mykel Williams the third player off the board at that position, the assumption was that he would rapidly become the next stellar lineman to emerge from this franchise. He earned plenty of opportunities as a rookie to jumpstart that trajectory and started in all nine of his appearances but suffered a season-ending torn ACL and has not made his way back into the starting lineup since then.

    Now more than midway through his second season, Williams has only played in 14 career games and owns only 2.5 sacks. He was never going to unseat Nick Bosa as the team's top pass rusher, but not even being his primary running mate on the edge (instead leaving that role for Keion White) is disappointing. Williams has yet to play more than half of all defensive snaps in the five games he has appeared in this season, something he never failed to do in his rookie campaign. Even with his eight pressures on the season, putting him at a commendable 9.6% pressure rate in his limited role, his average time to pressure of 3.69 is tied for 15th-longest in the league among the 191 defensive linemen with at least 50 pass rush snaps this year. Only one of Williams' eight pressures have come within 2.5 seconds of the ball being snapped, per Next Gen Stats.

    Sources indicate that without him stepping up to bolster the defensive line, the 49ers had to make a splash at the trade deadline and acquired DeForest Buckner to elevate the group. Since joining San Francisco, the 32-year-old Buckner has nearly caught up to Williams in snap count (84 to 126) and has just as many quick pressures through two games (1) as Williams has all season.

    There was an opportunity for Cincinnati Bengals edge rusher Shemar Stewart to level up into a regular starter when Trey Hendrickson left in free agency. Instead of building upon the five starts he made a year ago, the former No. 17 pick has actually seen his role dramatically decrease in 2026. Stewart has just 52 defensive snaps all season and has become expendable enough to get listed as a healthy scratch multiple times in the first 10 weeks.

    It has been revealed that outside of a Week 2 game in which Stewart registered a sack in the five snaps he played, the rest of his reps have been proverbial wind sprints. Zero pressures, zero sacks, and just one tackle assist credited to Stewart's name over his last five games played.

    The Bengals just don't have a need for Stuart in this revamped defense, a damning thing to say about a 17th overall pick in his second year. Offseason acquisition Boye Mafe slid into the job that was there for Stewart's taking, and Cedric Johnson has been the more productive of the two edge rushers on the second line of the depth chart. Even second-round rookie Cashius Howell has made a bigger impact, with a sack and 12 pressures already this season. The fact Cincinnati felt the need to both spend big free-agent money and high-end draft capital on the edge position was a bad sign already, but the evidence halfway through the 2026 campaign has been even worse.

    Stewart was always going to be somewhat of a project, because he was more renowned at Texas A&M for his tools rather than his production. He shined at the NFL Draft Combine with 40-yard dash, vertical jump, and broad jump results that placed him in the 90th percentile or better for edge rushers all time. But as in college, those raw attributes have not translated to on-field performance at the professional level.

    Industry observers note that while Justin Herbert has rightfully been the face of the Los Angeles Chargers' shocking offensive disappointment, Hampton is just as much of an underperformer as anyone on the unit. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's history of featuring extremely productive running backs in do-it-all roles -- just like all of his other hallmarks -- simply has not translated to L.A., and Hampton is a second-year bust because of that reality.

    Hampton's sample size is now nearly equal to his rookie year when he played just nine games because of an ankle fracture, and his per-game and per-touch production is dramatically worse. He sustained a downturn in each of the following categories.

    It is difficult to perform well when everything around him is broken, but Hampton is hardly holding up his end of the deal, either. The -46 rushing yards over expected he tallied in his first eight games ranked 123rd among 132 running backs. The Chargers are disastrous in a lot of areas right now, but the holes for Hampton are there. Los Angeles ranks ninth in ESPN's run block win rate metric. Six of the top-10 teams in that metric also rank top-10 in rushing EPA per play,.

    Golden totaled 361 receiving yards as a rookie. It took him only five weeks to outdo that total in his breakout sophomore season.

    Opportunities were always going to be there for Golden following the exodus of receivers from the Packers offense in the offseason, so the question was whether Golden was ready to capitalize on them. He sure is. The former No. 23 overall pick — who famously became the Packers' first first-round wide receiver in 23 years — is the fifth-leading receiver in the NFL with 853 yards.

    In a recent development, it's not just the explosion in production, but the reliance that Love has placed on him. Golden is just one of three receivers who have already broken 100 targets through Week 10. The only other two are CeeDee Lamb and Jaxon Smith-Njigba, consistently considered some of the league's top pass-catchers. This isn't to put Golden in conversation with two All-Pro receivers, but it demonstrates the sky-high confidence Jordan Love has in going to the second-year wideout.

    It has been revealed that golden has emerged as one half of a stellar duo with Christian Watson, both of whom rank in the top seven in receiving yards per game. He is a premier downfield threat who unlocked newly introduced deep-passing elements of an explosive offense that two weeks ago racked up a season-high 45 points.

    In a recent development, green Bay seems to have hit a home run with its rare swing at a first-round receiver and might, as a result, own one of the NFL's best one-two punches at the position now and in the years to come. Golden and Watson join Cincinnati's Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins as the only receiving pair with at least 800 yards and five touchdowns through the first 10 weeks of the season.

    In a recent development, the Detroit Lions defense takes more heat than it receives praise, and rightfully so given its deep struggles. But with the unit allowing no more than two touchdowns in any of its last four games and playing a major role in the team constructing a five-game win streak, the tide is turning, and Tyleik Williams is a massive part of that.

    Sources indicate that the Lions' defensive woes stem mostly from the secondary. Up front, the group is actually quite stout against the run. In fact, it ranks fifth in yards allowed per game and 10th in defensive rushing EPA per play. Williams is the anchor around which that run-stopping system operates.

    Recent findings suggest that last year, Williams was a rotational element on the defensive line. Now he is a fixture, helping a Lions defense that ranked in the bottom 10 last year in rush EPA per play allowed climb into the top 10 through the first half of the season. He eats space and plugs gaps to let the linebackers behind him shine, and he's prolific at bringing down running backs, too. In fact, only Malcolm Rodriguez, Derrick Barnes and Jack Campbell own more run stops among Lions defenders.

    What's more, Williams is a sure tackler. In addition to his run-stopping prowess, ball carriers have trouble breaking through his arms. He is one of just 10 defensive linemen in the entire NFL with at least 100 snaps against the run who has not missed a tackle this year, according to Next Gen Stats.

    A lack of any interceptions and a total of only two passes defended on the season make Maxwell Hairston a modest factor of the Buffalo Bills secondary at face value. But a deeper dive into his coverage explains how he has outperformed his up-and-down rookie season even without the takeaways and breakups.

    Take these metrics into consideration, all via Next Gen Stats:.

    Davison Igbinosun took Hairston's starting job after four games. That is more a testament to Igbinosun than a knock against Hairston. Ultimately, he looks poised to settle into a role where he covers smaller and speedier receivers while Igbinosun locks down the taller and more physical wideouts.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the annual GM Meetings came and went this week with only one significant transaction: Evan Phillips signed with the Braves. Phillips, our 34th-ranked free agent, received a three-year deal worth $35 million. He'll replace Raisel Iglesias in Atlanta's bullpen and pair with Robert Suarez at the end of the game. The Braves could still re-sign Iglesias too, I suppose.

    Sources indicate that otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors -- A LOT of rumors -- and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the crucial offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Friday's hot stove happenings.

    The Rangers are among the teams with interest in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports The Athletic. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers, though he does not stand out defensively, and could land at first base or in the corner outfield in MLB. Texas could stand to upgrade at first base and could always slot Sato in at DH as well.

    We ranked Sato as the fourth-best free agent available and the best free agent position player. The reigning Triple Crown winner in Japan hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs in 2026. Sato, 28 in March, has some similarities to Munetaka Murakami as a lefty with major power and swing-and-miss concerns, though Sato is a much more aggressive hitter and won't walk as much as Murakami.

    Recent findings suggest that with Miguel Rojas retired, the Dodgers are looking to add a right-handed hitting infielder, according to The Athletic. Mookie Betts and Max Muncy are entrenched on the left side of the infield. Tommy Edman, a switch-hitter, is penciled in at second base, with fellow switch-hitter Alex Freeland next in line as depth. Freeland has not hit much in his limited MLB time, however.

    It has been revealed that this is not a great free agent class overall, but it does feature several utility infielders who hit right-handed. Among them are Mauricio Dubón, Ha-Seong Kim, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, and Edmundo Sosa. Glovemen Oswald Peraza (Angels) and Jared Triolo (Pirates) are potential trade targets. Rojas was a very productive role player for Los Angeles. He won't be so easy to replace.

    The Padres are receiving calls about catchers Luis Campusano and Freddy Fermin, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. Top prospect Ethan Salas was called up in September and became the youngest catcher to appear in the postseason in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series. Salas is the future behind the plate, making Campusano or Fermin (or perhaps both) expendable.

    Recent findings suggest that campusano and Fermin are very different players. Campusano is a bat-first catcher who might be worth keeping given his age (28) and the fact that the Padres could slot him at DH. That mentioned, those same qualities make him appealing to other teams. Fermin, 31, is a terrific defender who hasn't hit much the last few years. The Padres need pitching and could deal a catcher or two for an arm or two.

    According to recent reports, samsung Lions outfielder Ja-Wook Koo has hired a upcoming agent and is looking to make the jump to MLB, reports MLB.com. Koo, a 10-time All-Star and this year's Korean Series MVP, has been among the best hitters in the Korea Baseball Organization the last few years. The 33-year-old hit .371/.458/.581 with 15 homers and nearly as many walks (66) as strikeouts (71) in 2026.

    Koo's age and the fact he's a left-handed hitter in a market inundated with left-handed hitting outfielders will work against him in free agency. He has a great track record in Korea, though, including a history of high contact rates, which could make him a cheaper and more appealing target than MLB free agents like Michael Conforto, Trent Grisham, Cedric Mullins, and Daulton Varsho.

    Recent findings suggest that I don't do a lot of NHL content in this space, even though I bet it often, because it's still fairly low on the national totem pole in terms of attention when football is in season. But I'm irked at the New Jersey Devils for ruining what would have been the most "villainous" homecoming by any player this NHL season when Connor Hellebuyck returns to Winnipeg on Tuesday.     Even with the three-time Vezina Trophy winner not playing, Jets fans will be out for blood, and I think we can find some good betting value in the game because of it.     Sources indicate that fans can try NHL betting on the best sports betting apps and get bonuses. The SportsLine Projection Model also has picks on games like Devils-Jets from its 10,000 simulations, and our experts also offer insights on games every day.

    FanDuel SGP price: +101  (subject to change).

    The relationship between the Jets and their best-ever player in Hellebuyck, who was also the primary goalie for gold medal-winning Team USA in the Winter Olympics, had been strained for a while. Then it broke over the summer when he publicly demanded a trade and stayed away from the club until he got it. Hellebuyck is in the third year of a seven-year contract extension with an $8.5 million average annual value and said it was about family and not money.

    The 2024-25 Hart Trophy winner preferred Florida, but the sides couldn't agree on that deal. On Oct. 23 the Jets sent him to Upcoming Jersey for Dawson Mercer, Alexander Command, Nick Bjugstad, goalie Nico Daws, a 2029 second-round pick and a 2027 seventh-round pick. That date was important, as it was the day Hellebuyck's suspension by Winnipeg was set to end and he was expected to report. He waived his no-movement clause to facilitate the trade.

    Things might have gotten ugly without a deal, but Hellebuyck became simply the latest prominent American NHL player to push for a move from a Canadian club, following the likes of Brady Tkachuk and Quinn Hughes.

    #26877. Tech Report: Could Tarik Skubal take a short-term, high-AAV contract? Breaking down pros and cons

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Could Tarik Skubal take a short-term, high-AAV contract? Breaking down pros and cons

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m.
    • In a recent development, skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly.
    • Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Barring a surprise agreement, the owners are almost certain to lock out the players at that time. Skubal is expected to sign before then.

    In a recent development, skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly. There's a real chance Skubal signs a contract worth more than $400 million in the next two weeks or so. Excluding Shohei Ohtani, who is technically a pitcher but is really a two-way player, here are the largest pitching contracts in history:.

    In a recent development, 1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M.

    2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M.

    Sources indicate that 3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.

    Sources indicate that 3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M.

    Recent findings suggest that 4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M.

    Sources indicate that something like, say, eight years at $50 million a year would give Skubal a $400 million contract that obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee and average annual value. Several massive-market clubs are mentioned to be pursuing Skubal (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), who is a special free agent as an in-his-prime ace. Conditions are ripe for a record deal.

    There is also a chance Skubal goes the Valdez route, or the Bo Bichette/Kyle Tucker route, and signs a short-term contract with a high annual salary. It might only be a small chance, but there is a chance. The Athletic reports the Dodgers prefer such an arrangement with Skubal. ESPN states Skubal has no interest in such a deal, though minds can always be changed.

    With that in mind, here are the pros and cons of a high-dollar, short-term contract for Skubal. Keep in mind that such a contract is usually a three- or four-year deal with opt outs, not a straight one- or two-year contract, and Skubal wouldn't necessarily have to use the opt outs to re-enter free agency. He could leverage them into a latest contract to stay with his team.

    1. Maximize earnings. Plain and simple, a short-term contract would give Skubal a chance to max out his earnings by making free agency available to him again as soon as next offseason. Go out, have a typical Skubal season in 2027, and perhaps market forces push the demand even higher than it is right now. Remember that, along with a salary cap, there could be a salary floor in the future. Small-market contenders like, say, the Guardians or Rays could throw many millions at Skubal to reach the floor in the future.

    2. Chance to set more records. This ties back to the last point. Skubal already set a newly introduced salary record for an arbitration-eligible player ($32 million in 2026) and he's positioned to set a new standard for pitcher contracts this offseason. Go back into free agency in a year or two, and Skubal (and Boras) could have a chance to break his own pitcher contract record. The record itself won't be a driving factor in that decision (the money will ultimately decide things), but it would be a nice feather in his cap.

    According to recent reports, 3. Freedom to change teams. Sometimes things don't work out. I don't think Juan Soto expected to miss the postseason in the first two years of his record 15-year, $765 million contract with the Mets. It's entirely possible Skubal could find his next situation not to his liking for whatever reason. Maybe the team doesn't contend, maybe he clashes with the coaching staff, maybe he doesn't like the local breakfast taco options. There could be a million different reasons it doesn't work. A short-term, high-dollar deal would give Skubal an escape hatch and allow him to head elsewhere if things go sideways.

    It has been revealed that 1. Injury and performance risk. All things considered, Skubal is a pretty safe bet on a long-term contract, though he is a pitcher, and pitchers get hurt. It's what they do. Skubal has had three elbow surgeries, including Tommy John surgery in 2017 and a minor procedure this May. If he gets hurt again, or his performance slips for whatever reason, then he could wind up costing himself in the significant picture because he won't be able to opt out and sign a larger deal. A short-term, high-dollar contract will pay him handsomely. He won't struggle to put bread on the table. But injury/performance risk means Skubal could ultimately leave money on the table.

    Sources indicate that 2. Potential salary cap. It is possible the next CBA will include a salary cap, which could limit Skubal's market and earning potential should he go back out into free agency in a year or two (or three). It's not just the cap itself either. MLB has proposed contract limits as part of the salary cap: five years at 15% of the cap for players who change teams, or six years at 16% of the cap for players who remain with their current team. Even if MLB doesn't get a salary cap and instead the competitive balance tax system remains in place with stiffer penalties, that could cost Skubal in the future. This offseason might be his last chance to sign in a truly free market.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

    Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

    Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

    Really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

    They were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

    Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt.

    Industry observers note that “I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle noted quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”.

    Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

    Industry observers note that no wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

    According to recent reports, one of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

    How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address promptly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

    Sources indicate that off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

    It has been revealed that an electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F.

    As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

    “We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”.

    It has been revealed that what could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

    According to recent reports, this, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

    It has been revealed that cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v.

    In a recent development, but parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

    In a recent development, "Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK.

    “We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola remarked. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

    “You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”.

    Why they didn’t follow the initiative that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

    In a recent development, those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

    “We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola said. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”.

    Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander has issued a statement regarding his recent anti-Muslim social media posts that he has since deleted.
    • "After taking time to reflect on my recent social media posts and speaking with people I trust and respect, I recognize that I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared on my platform.
    • "I realize that this content caused hurt and I sincerely apologize.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander has issued a statement regarding his recent anti-Muslim social media posts that he has since deleted. Santander's statement, which he posted to Instagram and follows a public condemnation of the posts by Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins, reads as follows:.

    "After taking time to reflect on my recent social media posts and speaking with people I trust and respect, I recognize that I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared on my platform.

    "I realize that this content caused hurt and I sincerely apologize. I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared, recognizing the responsibility that comes with having a public voice.

    Industry observers note that "As a man of faith, it is my belief that every person deserves to be treated with dignity and respect, regardless of their religion, background, or beliefs. After hearing feedback from those I hurt, I realize that the content I shared fell short of my own convictions.

    "I would like to affirm my respect for the Muslim community and for the dignity and freedom of people of every faith and background.

    "From this experience, I have learned to ensure that none of my communications promote hate or give the impression that I support hatred, discrimination, or violence against anyone.".

    The club had earlier released a statement on the incident that read:.

    It has been revealed that "Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs.".

    Santander, a Venezuela native, shared social media videos following the recent U.S. midterm elections, including one in which a Christian pastor mentioned, "There is no such thing as kind Muslims." Another suggested that Sharia law would be imposed in the U.S. following the election of Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate representing the state of Michigan.

    Atkins told reporters Tuesday that Santander's behavior "did not align" with organizational values and there were no words "to express my level of disappointment.".

    "I talked to Anthony about his lack of awareness, realizing that he has a very large microphone, what that meant," Atkins said. "We're working exceptionally hard internally to ensure, and we have been, that it's a safe environment, that baseball is for everyone. It's very key to us. It's a part of our organizational values and his behavior did not align with that.".

    Santander, 32, joined the Blue Jays prior to the 2025 season on a five-year, $92.5 million free-agent contract. He struggled badly across 54 games in 2025 and missed the entire 2026 season with injury.

    Yaxel Lendeborg, Warriors get a taste of life without Stephen Curry: 'It felt helpless out there'

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Warriors went into survival mode the minute it was revealed that Stephen Curry would miss at least the next two weeks, and perhaps more, with an oblique tear.
    • The Warriors would have been heavy underdogs in this game even had Curry played.
    • There are a few core things that need to happen for the Warriors to stay competitive while Curry is out, and it starts with Yaxel Lendeborg assuming full-time alpha status and producing like an All-Star with the defense now primarily focused on him.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Warriors went into survival mode the minute it was revealed that Stephen Curry would miss at least the next two weeks, and perhaps more, with an oblique tear. And in their first test, Curry's absence was felt in a major way as the Spurs put a 38-point beating on them on Friday night.

    This was never going to end well. The Warriors would have been heavy underdogs in this game even had Curry played. But the Warriors were hoping to at least stay in the fight for a little while. Instead, they were the Michael Spinks to San Antonio's Mike Tyson as the Spurs scored the first 18 points of the game and never looked back.

    There are a few core things that need to happen for the Warriors to stay competitive while Curry is out, and it starts with Yaxel Lendeborg assuming full-time alpha status and producing like an All-Star with the defense now primarily focused on him.

    According to recent reports, it's a lot to ask of a rookie, but he's set the bar so high to start his career that he's proven capable. He's putting up north of 20 points per game on super efficient shooting through his first 12 games.

    Could he possibly do it again against the Spurs? The answer was an emphatic no. Lendeborg had three points on 1-of-13 shooting, and afterward he was beating himself up worse than the Spurs did.

    It has been revealed that "We just got the s--t beat out of us," Lendeborg noted. "I was flustered the entire game. I couldn't make a damn layup. I don't even know, man. ... I'm not going to move past this. Everybody is saying throw it out the window. I can't throw a damn thing out the window. We just lost by like a hundred. I'm f--ked up mentally right now.

    It has been revealed that "It was an awful performance by me," Lendeborg continued. "I let everybody on this team down. I'm not gonna forget this ever. I don't remember the last time I got beat [like this] the whole entire game, with no hope at all. It felt helpless out there.".

    Helpless. It's a strong word, but appropriate on this night. Welcome to life without the greatest shooter and one of the greatest scorers to ever live commanding all the defensive attention and still putting up 30 a night.

    Lendeborg's unfiltered commentary is refreshingly raw. He says exactly what is on his mind, and certainly you'd rather have a player be hard on himself after a performance like this than a guy who doesn't care. But it was, in the end, one game against probably the best team with the best player in the world.

    It has been revealed that lendeborg will be fine. If you're thinking he got exposed in this game, save it. This dude is for real. He'll discard this and get right for New Orleans on Monday, because at 8-5 the Warriors are still in good shape. They can't let this spiral and suddenly the next few weeks are undoing all the good work they did to start the season.

    Steve Kerr started small against Victor Wembanyama, inserting De'Anthony Melton and Will Richard into the first five with Draymond Green at center. Bold move. The only way that can work is to run and gun, and Brandin Podziemski needed to be at the forefront of that attack. He wasn't.

    Podziemski, who has been terrific to start the season, averaging nearly 17 points per game and hitting 2.8 3-pointers a night at a 40% clip, finished with eight points on 2-of-10 shooting in San Antonio. Do the math, and Podziemski and Lendeborg, the Warriors' top two offensive options in Curry's absence, combined to miss 20 of 23 shots.

    There's some reason for hope with this duo as this Curry-less stretch continues. This season, they have led the Warriors to a +2.6 net rating in their minutes without Curry, via Databallr. It's a very different story doing it without Curry for a few minutes while he rests on the bench, versus doing it for full games. But there's no time for learning curves here. This duo probably needs to score 40 points and create closer to 60 without Curry.

    Recent findings suggest that the Warriors need to win in New Orleans on Monday. The Pelicans are kind of a mess right now, and Golden State getting to 9-5 would go a long way toward at least allowing Curry to return to a .500 team. After facing the Pelicans, the Warriors play the Mavericks and Grizzlies on a back-to-back, and then the Celtics in their first game back home. It's a hard stretch.

    It has been revealed that after that, it's the Kings on Nov. 25, which will be the two-week mark of Curry's timeline. The Warriors will cross their fingers that he can come back after that game, and in that case, even if they only beat the Pelicans and Kings over this stretch, they would still be 10-8 upon Curry's return.

    According to recent reports, even if Curry ends up missing an extra week or so, two of the Warriors' three games following the Kings matchup come against the 3-8 Clippers (who they have already beaten without Curry) and the 1-12 Jazz. They can still come out of this OK.

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In the Week 10 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Los Angeles Chargers.
    • According to recent reports, los Angeles is in the midst of an epic disaster of a season, having started the year 0-8 and looking horrific on both sides of the ball.
    • In a recent development, will the Ravens bounce back, or will the Chargers finally get on the board?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In the Week 10 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Los Angeles Chargers. Baltimore is coming off a disastrous Thursday night loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, during which the offense looked inept with third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano under center while nursing an injury. The Ravens will now turn to the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett in hopes that he can reinvigorate the attack in the absence of both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley.

    According to recent reports, los Angeles is in the midst of an epic disaster of a season, having started the year 0-8 and looking horrific on both sides of the ball. The Chargers are once again beset by a cavalcade of injuries, but that is no excuse for just how poorly they have played. They're the only winless team in the league at the moment, so they'll be looking for their first victory of the season.

    In a recent development, will the Ravens bounce back, or will the Chargers finally get on the board? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.

    The Chargers are 26th in the NFL in total yards and 32nd (a.k.a., last) in points. They average a mere 4.7 yards per play, which is 29th in the league, and they have scored points on only 27.4% of their drives while turning it over a league-worst 18.9% of the time. They lead the NFL in pre-snap penalties per game. They don't do anything well, and they often put themselves behind the eight ball with inexcusable mistakes.

    Sources indicate that justin Herbert looks like a broken quarterback, completing just 61.3% of his passes at an average of 6.8 yards per attempt, with six touchdown passes against a league-worst 11 interceptions. His receiver corps has been brutal all season, dropping passes and seemingly miscommunicating with him on routes left and right. He once again won't have Ladd McConkey on Monday evening, either, which will leave the uninspiring trio of Quentin Johnston, Tre Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith as his top perimeter options.

    Sources indicate that los Angeles has been entirely unable to run the ball, with Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combining for 709 yards on 184 carries -- an average of 3.8 yards per tote. The offensive line has given them no room to run whatsoever, clearing the way for only 0.90 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media. The backs themselves have a slightly below-average avoided tackle rate, but they still check in considerably below average in yards after contact per carry.

    Other than all that, though, things are going really well!

    Industry observers note that that noted, the Ravens do provide the Chargers with an opportunity to at least move the ball. Baltimore is 25th in the league in scoring defense and 21st in yards allowed per play. The Ravens have shown themselves to be beatable mostly through the air, as they've allowed only 3.6 yards per carry this season. Herbert doesn't have his top receiving option available in this game, but if the offensive line can actually provide him with adequate time to throw (not a guarantee with this group, obviously), then perhaps he can throw the ball to the guys wearing his color shirts rather than the opposing team for a change.

    It's hard to know what to expect from Baltimore's offense given that the Ravens are now on their fourth starting quarterback. This time around, it is the one who has yet to play with his new team and arrived in town just a week and a half ago.

    According to recent reports, we know that Brissett has completed 63.3% of his passes for only 5.6 yards per attempt this season, with 10 touchdowns against seven interceptions. We also know that he was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew before being traded from Arizona to Baltimore. He's competent and can keep the offense moving at times, but he doesn't offer much in terms of ceiling.

    According to recent reports, we also know that Brissett likes to hyper-target his top options in the passing game. We saw that in Arizona with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, but we also saw it in other stops, like when he honed in on Amari Cooper during his year as the starter with the Cleveland Browns. The Ravens already focus the majority of their passing game on wide receiver Zay Flowers, and it wouldn't be surprising if Brissett peppered him with targets here.

    Flowers was having a monster season with Lamar Jackson and even Tyler Huntley under center, but he did nothing the last two weeks with Joe Fagnano in the lineup, essentially. He should get back to producing at a decent level here, provided that offensive coordinator Declan Doyle moves him around the formation rather than parking him in the slot, where the Chargers have been better in coverage than they have been on the outside.

    According to recent reports, still, the Ravens will likely look to center the offense on Derrick Henry, so that Brissett doesn't have to do a ton of heavy lifting. Henry hasn't been as efficient this season (3.9 yards per carry) as he was during his first two years with the Ravens (5.6 per carry), presumably in part because he hasn't had Jackson to draw defensive attention away from his runs up the middle.

    Recent findings suggest that henry does still have a 53.7% rushing success rate, but he hasn't broken the types of long runs we've been used to seeing from him because the wider rushing lanes are not available with defenses crowding the box. He's run into an eight-man box on 30.9% of his carries, according to Tru Media, the third-highest rate among the 26 players with at least 100 rushing attempts so far this season.

    The Chargers have actually been half-way decent against the run this year, allowing 4.1 yards per carry to opposing running backs, but they've been hit for explosives at an above-average rate. If they don't get Henry on the ground quickly, he could hit a crease and take it a long way. If that starts happening, it'll open things up for Brissett to work the play-action game, which could lead to massive plays for the likes of Flowers, Ja'Kobi Lane and perhaps even Mark Andrews.

    I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board.

    Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20.
