    #26845. Which team needs Tarik Skubal the most? Ranking the suitors for the best free agent available

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1177 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Which team needs Tarik Skubal the most? Ranking the suitors for the best free agent available

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1177 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that as we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec.
    • The decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No.
    • In a recent development, "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that as we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec. 1 lockout of the players by MLB owners, we might see an accelerated pace of activity soon. The most tantalizing possibility is that ace and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the undisputed top talent on the free agent market this winter, will sign before the sport shuts down for an indeterminate amount of time.

    The decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No. 1 free agent of the 2026-27 class, and it's not an especially close call. Here's part of our write-up:.

    In a recent development, "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He highlighted few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    Will he set the record for the biggest contract ever signed by a pitcher? Will Skubal fetch the highest average annual salary for a pitcher? Will he top $400 million? Those are all reasonable questions to ask. First, though, there's a question to be asked about the teams that are already pursuing him the most vigorously. That question is, which team needs him the most? We're restricting our discussion to the five teams that have been most reliably linked to Skubal so far this offseason. We're already hearing reports of surprise teams, and it's always possible a surprise late bidder will enter the fray and even win his signature, but for now, these five clubs are the favorites. This, then, is an ordering of those teams based on which desperately needs a talent like Skubal in order to reach their goals in 2027 and beyond. Let's get to it, in order from "needs him the most" to "needs him but not as urgently as the teams ahead of them" ….

    The Cubs are in contention mode and in need of roster improvements if they're going to run down the world champion Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central. The rotation is without question the most pressing need for Chicago. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, David Peterson, and deadline acquisition Clay Holmes are all free agents. Justin Steele hasn't taken the mound at the significant-league level since early in the 2025 season thanks to UCL surgery and a halting recovery process. While he's expected to be ready for 2027, he's not exactly a known quantity right now. Young upsider Cade Horton may not be back until midseason after undergoing Tommy John surgery, and Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery, may be on a similar timeline. So, yes, the Cubs need a lot of rotation help, and Skubal would give them the true frontline ace they'd lack even if everyone were healthy. Unfortunately for the Cubs fans, it sounds like the Ricketts aren't willing to be truly competitive for his services.

    In a recent development, coming off the grave disappointments of 2026, the Mets could certainly use a headline-grabbing addition to improve their chances in 2027 and inspire a surely disaffected fan base. Beyond that, the Mets need more starting pitching to accompany promising young Nolan McLean. Christian Scott seems like a lock, but he doesn't project as a frontliner. They have some depth options for the back end, but they need a true needle-mover like Skubal at the very front. That's especially the case in what figures to be a hotly competitive NL East in 2027. Thus far, David Stearns and owner Steve Cohen sound committed to making a good-faith run at Skubal.

    It has been revealed that the Padres have a lot of work to do if they're going to earn a fourth straight playoff appearance. Speaking of which, the rotation is crying out for help right about now. They lost Dylan Cease to free agency last winter, and this time Michael King may be bound elsewhere, too. The Pads declined their club option on Nick Pivetta, and while they hope to bring him back on more favorable terms, there's no guarantee they'll be able to do that. Yes, Joe Musgrove will be back, but how much can he give them and how effective will he be? They'll need even more help if Adrian Morejon, a lockdown bulk reliever and possible starter-conversion project, signs elsewhere. Skubal's made to order, and signing the top talent on the market would be a strong signal by fresh owners José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones that the team's recent tradition of spending and contending won't be fading away.

    The Dodgers self-evidently needed Skubal enough to acquire him from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the deadline and do so at significant cost. On paper, the Dodgers aren't as desperate for rotation help as the teams ahead of them on this list, but there's still a need. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is a certifiable ace, but behind him Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are established health and durability risks. Shohei Ohtani is something of an unknown, at least insofar as his pitching is concerned right now, and thus far Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan have not proved worthy of being relied upon. One can squint and see the Dodgers' current championship window closing in the reasonably near future, which means that's all the more reason to push the chips in now. Retaining the elite services of Skubal would greatly aid the cause in 2027.

    Sources indicate that eyeball a rotation that already includes Dylan Cease, José Soriano, and Trey Yesavage, and you might think it doesn't need much more. And maybe it doesn't. As a matter of principle, though, any team with contending aspirations should be interested in a top-shelf ace when he hits the market. The Jays, who in recent years have invested in the roster at commendable levels, are no doubt dreaming of a Skubal-Cease one-two punch that would be the envy of, oh, every other team in baseball. There's also depth to think about. In particular, Cody Ponce is a bit of an unknown coming off knee surgery that ended his 2026 season in the middle of his first start. Addressing the offense probably should be more of a priority for the Jays this winter, but, again, it's Tarik Skubal, and the likes of Tarik Skubal make any team better.

    Tech Report: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.

    This was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek. Xabi Alonso’s team eventually won with a goal from each of his attacking triumvirate of Rogers, Palmer and João Pedro – and at times it will have been painful for the fresh Chelsea manager.

    It has been revealed that that was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team. Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham had their moments – and the best ones were granted to them by Sánchez. At a club that is such a restless trader of footballers, it feels remarkable that Sánchez has endured for so long.

    Recent findings suggest that alonso played down the significance of Sánchez’s errors, although he cannot seriously be considering sticking to his mantra of “relax and carry on”. That was, he mentioned, his response to the first-half Sánchez mistake that let in Josh King’s shot for Fulham’s first goal. Sánchez could have done a lot better with Gonzalo García’s goal after the break.

    Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE.

    Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN.

    Chelsea have a lot of faith that Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian on the bench for this game, will be their first-choice goalkeeper eventually. The situation seems rather more urgent and with Penders likely to feature against Luton Town on Thursday night in the Carabao Cup it would appear a big decision is looming for Alonso.

    It has been revealed that in terms of the Palmer-Rogers axis, this was very promising, although there was no doubting the senior figure in this. Palmer’s ball set João Pedro free in the first minute, the Brazilian lifting a well-judged nudge over Bernd Leno.

    "A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB.

    It was Palmer who was crucial to the second for Rogers, made by Maxence Lacroix on his debut. Palmer stroked in the third on 49 minutes with the easy confidence of a man in form.

    Recent findings suggest that A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v.

    It has been revealed that "Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq.

    Recent findings suggest that “I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”.

    Sources indicate that palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”.

    If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

    Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

    Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will rapidly become familiar.

    There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

    It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

    It has been revealed that sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

    “We concede goals in the first minute, the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half and there are not worse moments to concede. But we highlighted character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. If you lose against a team like Chelsea they [should] have to do a little bit more. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.

    “We are on our way and we will keep improving. The first thing I want to see is a competitive team. We were tonight, we tried our best and tried to play our football against a team like Chelsea, which is not easy. I believe in them and I believe in young players. I think they have the energy and ambition I want and they fit in the way I play. Josh King is absolutely amazing. I am really happy with him. Gonzalo [Garcia] scored and Cesar [Palacios] did well. I think they need a bit more time but they are doing great and making an impact already.”.

    "We need to help them, not to rely everything on them" Xabi Alonso speaking about Chelsea's 'special' front three 🔵 pic.twitter.com/JnSBoNexF4.

    "Arsenal DON'T win the league if they have Ramsdale and not Raya" 🧤@Carra23 and @GNev2 think that upgrading the goalkeeper position could be the 'last piece' for Chelsea 🧩 pic.twitter.com/UBzMCFmxpp.

    "You can see in his eyes, he's ready to prove people wrong""Best player on the pitch by a mile" 👏Morgan Rogers reacts to his debut and the performance of Cole Palmer pic.twitter.com/M7JKk1MQ8U.

    "How ready are you?""Did you not watch the game?" 😅Cole Palmer says he is 'hungry' and ready to get back to his best! pic.twitter.com/xpg5zJl9k0.

    Recent findings suggest that “There were things to really like. On paper, that front three [for Chelsea] is sensational. It really is. It looked it in the game. I think Joao Pedro is fantastic. [Morgan] Rogers’ first game, what a start. But when you think of him, [Cole] Palmer and Pedro; that is as good as anything in the Premier League right now.

    Recent findings suggest that “But I do think concerns defensively. They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper concern out because it is going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight.”.

    “The attacking play, Cole Palmer was sensational. If you talk about Cole Palmer getting back to his best you have got a £120m-£125m player there. [Morgan] Rogers getting a goal. Those two being electric with Joao Pedro up front. The front three were brilliant tonight. One of the best things I have seen this weekend.

    Industry observers note that “They have added an experience player at centre-back, centre midfield and centre forward. I do not know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do. The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement [Robert] Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It is a problem.”.

    The final whistle is blown at Craven Cottage and Chelsea hold on to win 3-2 to give Xabi Alonso a win in his first game in charge. Alvaro Arbeloa’s first game as Fulham boss ends in defeat. An absorbing west London derby.

    Garcia throws himself to the ground as Sessegnon sends in a cross but that is never going to be a penalty.

    Will there be one more chance for Fulham to try and find an equaliser? Time is running out for the hosts.

    According to recent reports, pedro has the ball in the back of the Fulham net but Quenda was offside in the build-up. A quick VAR check proves so.

    There will be four added minutes.

    Recent findings suggest that surely there is another goal in this one? It is a surprise there has not been since Garcia got a goal back for Fulham.

    The latest booking of the game goes the way of Castagne, who cynically trips Colwill.

    Industry observers note that sessegnon is played in down the left channel and flicks it past Acheampong inside the Chelsea penalty area. Sessegnon gets his shot away from a narrow angle and it is straight at Sanchez.

    Industry observers note that palmer looks like he might have cramp in his calf and is going to be replaced by Estevao. Quenda also comes on for Chelsea, coming on for Rogers.

    Fulham make an attacking alteration as Muniz replaces Robinson.

    That is a huge, huge chance for Fulham to equalise. Robinson is played in behind the Chelsea defence with a long ball in behind and Sanchez is in no-man’s land out of his goal. Robinson just has to lift it over Sanchez from the edge of the box but his effort goes wide. Fulham should be on level terms.

    Recent findings suggest that fulham fans think they are about to be awarded a free-kick right outside the box but instead the free-kick goes the other way. It was a clear dive from Bassey, who is rightly booked for simulation.

    James is the third Chelsea player into the book for cynically pulling King back. James then has the cheek to wag his finger at King, as if it was not a foul, yet it was a clear booking. James had to be careful there as some referees may not have taken too kindly to that.

    Double change for Fulham as Kevin and Sessegnon are brought on.

    That would have been a great goal from King. He has already scored once and is inches away from his second. He receives a pass on the turn from Robinson and drives towards the Chelsea box. He then cuts inside onto his right, beating Lacroix with ease, and nearly beats Sanchez at his near post but his shot goes inches wide.

    This is a very open, end-to-end game and you would fully expect more goals in this one. I would be very surprised if this one ended 3-2. Both defences are looking leaky.

    Fulham are going to make their substitution of the night as Charles comes on for his debut having signed from Southampton, replacing Bobb.

    Enzo is being booed a lot by the home fans every time he touches the ball.

    Chelsea are the first to turn to their bench. Enzo is coming on and is met by a lot of boos, mostly though from the home fans as the majority of the travelling Chelsea fans are applauding him. Chavarria is also on to make his Chelsea debut. Hato and Lavia head off.

    In a recent development, there is a latest rule being implemented. Hato takes far too long over a throw-in and Fulham are therefore awarded the throw-in instead.

    Sources indicate that when Palmer put Chelsea 3-1 up, the visitors looked in control of this match. Fast forward five minutes and the momentum has completely switched around. What an absorbing opening Monday night of the season!

    In a recent development, the Fulham debutant gives them life and this game is not over. Castagne is found making a run in behind and cuts back inside onto his left inside the Chelsea penalty area. His shot is straight at Sanchez, who can only parry it straight into the path of Garcia, who heads into the ground and the ball bounces over Sanchez into the Chelsea net. Another poor piece of goalkeeping from Sanchez.

    Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN.

    All members of Chelsea’s starting front three have got on the scoresheet tonight and Palmer also has an assist to his name.

    Chelsea come close to a fourth as Hato squares it for Rogers inside the Fulham box but Robinson nips in just in front to clear.

    Sources indicate that he came close to scoring moments ago and now he does get on the scoresheet. Pedro gets onto the end of a flicked-on header by Rogers near halfway and drives into the Fulham half. As he gets to the Fulham penalty area, he waits for the overlapping run of Palmer and times the pass just right. Palmer, from a narrow angle, puts it between Leno’s legs and into the far corner.

    "Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq.

    Palmer does brilliantly down Chelsea’s right to skip past a number of defenders and moves into the Fulham penalty area. He opens up his body and curls one towards the far corner. He is adamant that there is a deflection but a goal kick is given. Replays show Palmer may have had a point.

    We are back under way at Craven Cottage.

    Nottingham Forest are ramping up their pursuit of Chelsea’s Liam Delap as Oliver Glasner eyes two major signings before the window closes.

    Forest are in talks with Chelsea over a potential loan deal for the forward after he was made available at Stamford Bridge and not included in their opening-day squad against Fulham.

    Negotiations are ongoing, but Delap fits the profile of striker Forest are prioritising and is a long-term target for both the club and Glasner from his spell at Crystal Palace.

    An absorbing first half at Craven Cottage is brought to a close and Chelsea take a 2-1 lead into the break. Pedro put them ahead inside the first minute before King equalised for Fulham. However Rogers, on his Chelsea debut, put the visitors back in front not long before half-time.

    There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

    Recent findings suggest that palmer, who has run the show for Chelsea in this first half, is inches away from putting the visitors 3-1 up. Both sides have been guilty of giving the ball away in dangerous areas and Fulham do so on this occasion. Palmer then curls an effort from the edge of the box but his shot goes just wide of the far post.

    Recent findings suggest that the British record transfer puts Chelsea back in front on his official debut. It stems from great play from centre-back Lacroix, who finds himself in an advanced position and receives a pass from Palmer on the right side of the box. Lacroix cuts it across to Rogers, who makes no mistake from 12 yards out. Assist and goal both coming from fresh signings.

    A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v.

    Fulham fail to clear a cross from James into their box and Hato’s header falls at the feet of Lavia, whose shot from close range is saved by Leno.

    Is Colwill lucky to still be on the pitch? The ball is played in behind the Chelsea defence and Colwill appeared to throw his arm across King but no foul is given. That could so easily have been given as a free-kick and a second yellow card.

    Sources indicate that rogers drives towards the Fulham box and cuts inside onto his right foot. His effort is blocked by Cuenca before James’ first-time shot is straight at Leno.

    It has been revealed that chelsea are inches from going back in front. It stems from great work from Palmer, who drives down Chelsea’s right. His cross from the right side of the box picks out Pedro near the penalty spot. The Brazilian volleys it first time but his effort goes just wide.

    Fulham are on top at the moment and Chelsea are lucky shaky as they are under the cosh inside their own box. King is playing really well, finding pockets of space down Fulham’s right and looking a real threat.

    Fulham are back on level terms but it is really poor goalkeeping from Sanchez. King, who had just threatened down Fulham’s right, receives a pass from Castagne on the right touchline and takes a touch into the Chelsea box. King then fires his shot away at the near post and gets plenty of power on it but there is no way Sanchez should be beaten. He is beaten and Fulham equalise. Good strike from King but terrible keeping from Sanchez.

    Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE.

    Recent findings suggest that chelsea haven’t spent all that money on Rogers for his defending, but Alonso won’t have liked the way he let Josh King to run past him to collect the ball and smash Fulham level. Rogers switched off there.

    King does brilliantly to drive down Fulham’s right and flashes a dangerous ball across the six-yard box but none of his teammates are on hand to meet the cross.

    Fulham are flirting with danger in and around their box and are a touch fortunate not to concede a second goal.

    Down the other end, King is urged to shoot from outside the box and he obliges. It looks like it should be a fairly routine save for Sanchez but the Chelsea keeper looks uncomfortable and pushes it behind for a corner. The delivery comes to the near post and King, who lays it off the edge of the box. It comes to Palacios, who cannot guide his effort on target.

    Chelsea started this game well but have lost control and are asking for trouble. The latest example sees Sanchez take too long to clear and he accidentally allows the ball to go out before clearing to gift Fulham a corner. Bobb’s delivery is headed away at the near post by James.

    According to recent reports, that is strong one-vs-one defending from Bassey. Palmer lifts the ball over the top to pick out the run of Pedro, who is dispossessed inside the Fulham box by Bassey.

    Industry observers note that moments later, Lavia flies into a reckless challenge on Bassey and is booked. Lavia looks stunned at that decision but he is perhaps on the fortunate side that VAR did not advise the referee to have a further look at that on the screen. Lavia was out of control and could have easily been in more trouble. Two Chelsea players already into the book and were a little bit lucky.

    Palmer had just one Premier League assist to his name throughout last season and has already matched that tally tonight on the opening weekend.

    It has been revealed that colwill is in trouble. Could Chelsea go down to 10 men early? He loses possession poorly inside his own half and then resorts to hacking Bobb down with a nasty challenge. Was Colwill the last man and could Bobb have gone racing in on goal? Colwill is booked and is perhaps a touch fortunate, although what saved him is that you perhaps could not definitively say that it was a denial of a goal-scoring opportunity.

    How do Alvaro Arbeloa and his Fulham side react now they are a goal down early?

    With their first attack of the Xabi Alonso era, Chelsea hit the front inside the opening minute of this west London derby. Lacroix’s header from halfway finds Palmer, who plays it into the path of Pedro. The Brazilian, fresh from signing a fresh deal at the club, takes it in his stride and, from inside the Fulham penalty area, lifts it over Leno and into the far corner. A fine finish from Pedro and Alonso has the perfect start.

    We are under way at Craven Cottage in the final game on this opening weekend of the newly introduced Premier League season.

    Sources indicate that the most interesting piece of Chelsea team news is that there is no Enzo Fernandez in the starting line-up, despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo. Instead, Romeo Lavia will partner Reece James in the centre of midfield, with Caicedo presumably injured. There is still an expectation that Manchester City will bid for Fernandez before the transfer window shuts, but the Argentine is on the substitutes’ bench. As expected, there is no place in the Chelsea squad for Nico Jackson and Liam Delap, both of whom have not travelled and are expected to leave Stamford Bridge. Aston Villa remain favourites to land Jackson, although Atletico Madrid have been showing an interest. Nottingham Forest are leading the race for Delap.

    Alvaro Arbeloa hands full debuts to Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, who have both joined from Real Madrid. Shea Charles is on the bench ahead of his potential Fulham debut.

    Fulham: Leno; Castagne, Cuenca, Bassey, Robinson, King, Berge, Iwobi; Bobb, Garcia, Palacios.Substitutes: Lecomte, De Gougerolles, Tete, Reed, Charles, Sessegnon, Kevin, Smith Rowe, Muniz.

    It has been revealed that morgan Rogers and Maxence Lacroix make their full Chelsea debuts this evening. Fellow newly introduced signings Danny Welbeck, Valentin Barco, Pep Chavarria and Geovany Quenda are on the bench, as is Enzo Fernandez, who has been linked with a move away. Moises Caicedo is not in the matchday squad.

    Chelsea: Sanchez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Gusto, Lavia, James, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Chavarria, Barco, Enzo, Neto, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck, Quenda.

    No more excuses. No more jam tomorrow. It is time for Chelsea to fight for the Premier League title this season. Anything else should be deemed a disappointment.

    This is Chelsea version 3.0 under BlueCo, who bought the club four years ago. First there was Todd Boehly’s trolley dash, then came Behdad Eghbali’s youth club. This summer the focus has been on being Premier League-ready.

    Sources indicate that off the pitch, the timing might be right for Boehly to be discussing the sale of his shares to Eghbali’s Clearlake Capital. But on it, Chelsea look better equipped to re-enter the title conversation than at any point in the BlueCo era.

    Saturday:Hull 2 Manchester United 0Everton 2 Crystal Palace 0Ipswich 2 Sunderland 1Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 1Brentford 3 Tottenham 0.

    Sunday:Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0Newcastle 2 Liverpool 2.

    Let's get it.#CFC | #FULCHE pic.twitter.com/G2M8LknNgV.

    Monday Night Fulham. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Oxuni9yiez.

    Recent findings suggest that two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the latest Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

    “I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa said. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”.

    It has been revealed that arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

    Industry observers note that chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

    It has been revealed that “We feel ready,” Alonso said. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”.

    Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

    “Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”.

    Industry observers note that these sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

    NBA Rookie Rankings: Yaxel Lendeborg debuts at No. 1, Darryn Peterson making up ground in tight race

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This season's NBA Rookie of the Year race has the potential to be one of the closest in league history.
    • It has been revealed that that's why Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson faces an uphill climb to win the honor after fracturing his right hand earlier this month.
    • During the first month of the season, three players have separated themselves at the top: Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer, and Darius Acuff Jr.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This season's NBA Rookie of the Year race has the potential to be one of the closest in league history. While there is no 65-game requirement to win the award — unlike MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and All-NBA honors — playing as many games as possible will be paramount this season in order to claim Rookie of the Year.

    It has been revealed that that's why Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson faces an uphill climb to win the honor after fracturing his right hand earlier this month. Wilson is set to miss the next 3-5 weeks and will likely lose serious ground to others in his class. He at the moment has the sixth-best odds (+4000) on FanDuel Sportsbook to win Rookie of the Year.

    During the first month of the season, three players have separated themselves at the top: Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer, and Darius Acuff Jr. While it's not a guarantee one of those players wins it, if the season ended today, those would be the top vote-getters.

    Darryn Peterson and AJ Dybantsa — the first two picks of the 2026 NBA Draft — have some ground to make up during the next four months to get back in the mix.

    With the regular season almost a quarter of the way complete, let's dive into our first Rookie of the Year rankings. All odds via FanDuel.

    With Steph Curry out, Lendeborg has continued to step up. The oldest player drafted in the first round is coming off a lackluster showing against the Spurs in the NBA Cup, but before that he had three straight games of 23+ points. He is shooting 48.6% from the field and 41.4% from 3. Lendeborg didn't start shooting 3s on a consistent basis until he got to Michigan last season, so knocking down that percentage on 5.4 attempts per night is a positive sign. Fourteen games into the season, Lendeborg is the favorite.

    Boozer's raw stats aren't as good as Lendeborg's or even Acuff's, but his impact goes well beyond the box score. His feel for the game is elite for a 19-year-old. Boozer keeps getting better and better as a processor as he continues to log more minutes. The Grizzlies have been one of the league's surprising teams this season. Boozer deserves a ton of credit for that. He wins everywhere he goes, whether at the high school, college, or professional level.

    Acuff just turned 20 last week. In 13 games as a teenager, he averaged 25.5 points per game and became the first teenager in NBA history to score at least 275 points and dish out 80 assists in his first 11 games. Acuff is a special offensive talent who is being asked to do more than any rookie in his class. Sacramento is a very bad basketball team, but Acuff makes the Kings somewhat fun to watch. That's a huge credit to him.

    Industry observers note that the Jazz have been decimated by injuries this season and are at the moment riding a 12-game losing streak. The one bright side amidst some very bad basketball is how good Peterson has been during that stretch. Peterson had a five-game stretch in which he scored 20 points in each game and shot the ball well from 3. Peterson is the future of Utah's franchise, so getting him as many reps as possible on and off the ball should be the priority.

    Industry observers note that dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick, is averaging 14 shot attempts per game during his first 10 appearances as a pro. He should be taking even more shots. The way the Wizards are using him is confusing at times. Dybantsa is in somewhat of a weird situation because of the Wizards' roster. Washington handed Trae Young a huge contract this offseason that is already aging poorly. Dybantsa should be the focus of the offense. He should be touching the ball and shooting it even more than he is already. I have been impressed with Dybantsa's defense this season.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I have made it 24 years without watching a single episode of "The Bachelor,"  but that streak might soon be coming to an end because an NFL quarterback has been chosen to star in the show.
    • According to recent reports, commanders quarterback Sam Hartman is this year's bachelor, and the only reason I'm mentioning that is that I'm not quite mentally ready to start talking about Week 11 yet.
    • There are seven games in the early window, and none of them will feature two teams with winning records facing off.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I have made it 24 years without watching a single episode of "The Bachelor,"  but that streak might soon be coming to an end because an NFL quarterback has been chosen to star in the show.

    According to recent reports, commanders quarterback Sam Hartman is this year's bachelor, and the only reason I'm mentioning that is that I'm not quite mentally ready to start talking about Week 11 yet. I just looked at the Week 11 schedule and what the NFL is giving us during the 1 p.m. window might be the worst slate of games ever.

    There are seven games in the early window, and none of them will feature two teams with winning records facing off. Let's take a look at this schedule:.

    I would rather watch old episodes of "The Bachelor" than any of these games. That being noted, I might watch the Cowboys game just to see if Jerry Jones fires everyone after his defense gives up 47 points to the Titans.

    Recent findings suggest that so will that actually happen? Let's get to the picks and find out.

    It has been revealed that for the second straight week, we have a team coming off a game in Europe facing a team coming off a bye. Last week, things worked out pretty well for the Bengals, but that feels like an anomaly. This game will mark just the seventh time in NFL history that a team coming off an international game has had to play a team coming off a bye, and uh, I have some bad news for everyone in Detroit: The team coming off the international game has gone 1-5, with the only win coming by a possessed Bengals team in Week 10 that got to host a Sunday night game at home for the first time in three years. There was no way the Bengals were losing.

    Industry observers note that however, I am worried about the Lions. For one, they just lost Aidan Hutchinson for the season to a torn ACL, and thanks to the injury, there's a 50% chance that Dan Campbell is going to ban his entire team from celebrating anything ever again.

    Aidan Hutchinson suffered an injury on this play and went to the locker room.(📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/ysx9NLmNHF.

    It has been revealed that not only did they just lose their best defensive player, but it gets worse, because they now have to face the top rushing offense in the NFL. The Bucs are averaging 163.9 yards per game on the ground, which is 10 yards more than the next closest team. Tampa Bay has more rushing yards this season than the Bengals and Packers COMBINED.

    I do not know if Baker Mayfield (foot) is going to play, but I'm not sure it matters, because the QB in Tampa only has one job and that's to hand the ball off. If Baker can't play, Jalon Daniels will, and if he can't play for some reason, the Bucs could probably just hold a fan raffle for the job.

    Industry observers note that bucs: Can you hand the ball off? Fan: Yes. Bucs: OK, the job is yours.

    There have only been three games this season where an NFL team has run the ball at least 49 times and the Buccaneers have two of them. With the Buccaneers coming off the bye, that means they're going to be well-rested and it also means that offensive coordinator Zac Robinson has had plenty of time to tear out every page from his playbook that has a passing play on it. The Bucs might run it 71 times on Sunday.

    The good news for the Lions is that they've been one of the best teams in the NFL at stopping the run. They're giving up just 90.4 yards per game, which is the fifth-best number in the NFL, but that was with Hutchinson on the field. This week, they obviously won't have him.

    It has been revealed that the Lions are flying back from Germany; they just lost their best defensive player, and they have to face a Bucs team coming off a bye. Oh, and did I mention that NFL teams are a combined 13-3 coming off their bye this year? Because NFL teams are a combined 13-3 coming off their bye this year. And two of those three losses were by the Titans and Chargers, so I'm not even sure those count.

    Not only do the Bucs have the best rushing attack in the NFL, but they also have the best run defense in the league, so this could be a long day for Jahmyr Gibbs. This game comes down to whether you trust Jared Goff to dice up Tampa Bay's defense, and, well, I'm the guy who made Goff my preseason prediction to win MVP this year, so I'm riding with Goff and the Lions here.

    PICK: Lions 23-20 over Buccaneers.

    It has been revealed that if there's any game in Week 11 that feels like a disaster waiting to happen, it's definitely this one. With the Jets and Chargers on the same field, I won't be surprised if the government declares SoFi Stadium a federal disaster area.

    Recent findings suggest that there's been no bigger disaster in the NFL this year than the Chargers. They hired Mike McDaniel to fix their offense and he somehow might have made it worse. When McDaniel was in Miami, one reason his offense worked so well is that he had two superstar receivers in Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle. He doesn't have anything near that in L.A., but he does not seem to realize that. McDaniel keeps doing things his own way, and as a result, the Chargers' offense is so bad it's almost painful to watch.

    Recent findings suggest that it's getting to the point where I feel like the Chargers' best offensive strategy would be to just not have an offense at all. I have no idea how that would work, but I have to think it would be an upgrade over what they're doing now. This team is averaging UNDER 180 passing yards per game, which shouldn't be possible when you have Justin Herbert as your QB.

    Not to be outdone, the Jets have also been a disaster. Here's a quick synopsis of how things have gone for the Jets. Back on Feb. 24, Aaron Glenn remarked he would call plays on defense because it's one of his superpowers.

    "To me, play calling is my superpower"Aaron Glenn on his decision to call plays on defense pic.twitter.com/FvHFYW97pK.

    As it turns out, though, he might have been wrong, and play-calling might actually be his kryptonite.

    Recent findings suggest that aaron Glenn gave up play calling vs the #Bills — that’s really major of him. Called it his “super power” this offseason. He wants to call the game. To step back and be willing to give it to someone else, for the betterment of the team, isn’t something a lot of coaches are willing… https://t.co/ivYq4cnBca.

    Aaron Glenn saw Josh Allen coming up on the schedule in Week 10 and stated "No thanks, I'm good. You're now in charge of calling play on defense, Brian.".

    Industry observers note that so we have the Jets' broken defense going up against a Chargers offense that can't move the ball on anyone. I mentioned this game feels like a disaster waiting to happen and that disaster might happen after the game. If the Jets lose here, the temperature on Aaron Glenn's hot seat will get so hot that I don't think the Fahrenheit scale can actually measure it. We might have to switch over to Celsius.

    The Chargers stunned the Ravens on Monday night by rushing for a season-high 160 yards. Running the ball is literally the only thing the Chargers can do on offense, which might work in their favor here because the Jets can't stop the run.

    The Chargers went into Week 10 with ZERO wins, so I feel crazy even thinking this, but this team might actually win two games in a row.

    Never in my life did I think I would live long enough to see a Jaguars-Giants game get flexed into the 4:25 p.m. late afternoon slot, but that's exactly what happened here. This game was originally scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. ET, but the NFL decided to move it to 4:25 p.m. ET, and we're celebrating that fact here at CBS Sports by sending "The NFL Today" crew to MetLife Stadium.

    The NFL Today is headed to MetLife! 🔥The show will be LIVE outside the stadium ahead of @Jaguars vs @Giants this Sunday 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Bv2zAZ1htI.

    If you're going to be at the game, please come dressed as your favorite CBS Sports studio analyst.

    Sources indicate that the Giants have been a huge surprise this season, and that's mostly thanks to John Harbaugh, who is my early vote for coach of the year. Harbaugh has been forced to start THREE different quarterbacks this season, but he still has the Giants at 5-3-1 and on top of the NFC East.

    The biggest surprise is that the Giants have somehow made J.J. McCarthy look good. I was led to believe by the Vikings that McCarthy was a washed-up bust, but apparently they just didn't know how to use him. McCarthy is the chopsticks of NFL quarterbacks. I hate chopsticks because I'm incompetent and don't know how to use them, just like the Vikings didn't know how to use McCarthy. On the other hand, my wife is such an expert with chopsticks that if every utensil on earth disappeared tomorrow and we only had chopsticks left, she would be fine, just like the Giants will be fine with McCarthy running the show.

    McCarthy played well enough to win in Week 10 against the Commanders, and the Giants might have won if they had a kicker who could make field goals from the right hash.

    According to recent reports, all 6 of Dominic Zvada’s missed kicks this season have come from the right hash, including his 33-yard miss last night.The Giants have lined up on the left hash for every extra point, where Zvada is a perfect 16/16. https://t.co/D9YzxVSYyx pic.twitter.com/UHJa8av5EK.

    Zvada's inability to hit a kick from the right hash is like Zoolander not being able to turn left, except worse.

    Industry observers note that I watched zoolander today (kind of like idiocracy) and the main character DEREK zoolander. Cannot turn left. Where have i heard of a derek related to the direction left. pic.twitter.com/e8cUEOU8Ct.

    Although I think the Giants will keep this game close, this will be the first week that the Jaguars finally unveil their fresh defense. They made three trades before the deadline, acquiring DT Davon Godchaux, DT Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III. The Jags decided to keep Davis and Bates on the bench in Week 10 so they would each get a "bye" week this year. Those two will make their debut on Sunday, and I have a feeling the new-look Jags' defense is going to cause some problems for the Giants.

    PICK: Jaguars 30-23 over Giants.

    Sources indicate that for the first time in four years, the NFL is playing a game in Mexico City. I went to Mexico City once, and I was totally blown away by the food. I mean, they had a Chili's and Burger King UNDER THE SAME ROOF.

    In a recent development, if you're looking for food in Mexico City, I highly recommend this place. Only place I know of where you can get the world's two best restaurants under one roof TOGETHER pic.twitter.com/G58xvmA5DS.

    Someone needs to make that happen in the United States. Mexico is light years ahead of us when it comes to combining fast food with fast casual dining under one roof.

    It has been revealed that OK, I need to stop talking about Chili's and start focusing on what could be the best chess match of the 2026 season: Kyle Shanahan vs. Brian Flores.

    Sources indicate that through the first 10 weeks, the 49ers have had one of the best offenses in the NFL this year: They rank first in yards per game (399.8) and second in points per game (31.2). No one has really been able to stop them. The 49ers are so good that the Cowboys' defense basically gave up on trying to stop them in Week 10.

    As for the Vikings, they have one of the best defenses in the NFL. They've given up the fewest points per game (14) and the second-fewest yards per game (273.3). One major reason they're so successful is that they've gotten really good at destroying the opposing quarterback. The Vikings have racked up 37 sacks this year, which leads the NFL, and Flores loves to blitz on nearly every single play.

    The problem with that strategy is that Brock Purdy is basically the one quarterback you do NOT want to blitz.

    Leaders in EPA per drop back vs the blitz…DO NOT blitz these guys pic.twitter.com/Vn67jHblTm.

    Purdy thinks fast and gets rid of the football swiftly. It's like he was designed in a lab to beat the blitz, but Flores is almost certainly aware of this, which means we'll probably see him cook up something special for the 49ers quarterback on Sunday. And now that we're talking about cooking, I'm thinking of Chili's again. I might need to take a lunch break.

    Sources indicate that I actually think the X-factor in this game is going to be the altitude. Mexico City sits at an elevation of nearly 7,400 feet, which is more than 2,000 feet higher than Denver. When you're playing at an altitude this high, it's not easy to get acclimated, which is why the 49ers will be spending the entire week in Colorado Springs, a city that has an altitude of just over 6,000 feet.

    Recent findings suggest that #49ers are set to travel to Colorado Springs tonight to begin altitude acclimation. They’ll have a normal practice week before traveling to Mexico City on Saturday to play the Vikings on Sunday night.

    According to recent reports, on the other hand, the Vikings will be practicing at their normal practice facility, which has an altitude of 945 feet. Advantage, 49ers.

    This feels like a game where the altitude starts to get to the Vikings in the second half and that's when the 49ers will take over.

    This is the final international game of the 2026 season, and I feel like the NFL should add some spice to the last international game each year by having the government revoke the losing team's passports. I'm not sure if that's legal, but I would definitely watch a reality show that consisted only of NFL players trying to get back home after having their passports revoked in a foreign country. It would be more entertaining than "The Bachelor.".

    Dan Quinn is probably going to be having nightmares all week and that's because he has to figure out a way to stop Joe Burrow, which is something that no one else has been able figure how to do this year.

    At this point, you've probably seen plenty of Burrow highlights this year, but if you're wondering just how dominant he's been, let me break it down for you:.

    To put his yardage number in perspective, no other QB is even averaging 285 yards per game. He has five more TD passes than the next closest player and his completion percentage is so high that he might actually break the NFL single-season record of 74.4%, which was set by Drew Brees in 2019.

    Burrow is playing at an insanely high level, and now, he gets to face a Commanders defense that has given up the most passing yards per game in the NFC this year and second-most in the NFL (244.8). Burrow against this defense would be like inviting Joey Chestnut to your family's Thanksgiving and telling him to eat whatever he wants. You know you're going to get a Hall of Fame performance.

    Recent findings suggest that sam Darnold threw for 379 yards against this Commanders defense. Jameis Winston threw for 326 yards against this defense. J.J. McCarthy threw for 293 yards against this defense. I think what I'm trying to say here is that the NFL might want to invite Norm Van Brocklin's family to this game, because Burrow might take down his all-time single-game passing record of 554 yards.

    Although I feel like Burrow is going to have a major game, I think the Commanders' offense could also have some success. This is a home primetime game; Washington will be desperate, and Jayden Daniels has been playing well over the past few weeks.

    The last time these two teams played back in 2024, there wasn't a single punt in the game. That might happen again on Monday night because Zac Taylor doesn't sound like a guy who aims on punting this week.

    Asked what he didn't like about last night's blowout win against the Steelers, #Bengals coach Zac Taylor said, "We punted.".

    I'm going to say Burrow continues his MVP campaign by leading the Bengals to a shootout win in Washington.

    PICK: Bengals 34-27 over Commanders.

    Best pick: Commanders over Giants. Last week, I predicted that the Commanders would score exactly 24 in a win over the Giants, and guess what happened? The Commanders scored exactly 24 points in a win over the Giants. As soon as Sam Hartman got picked to be the next bachelor, I knew there was no way the Commanders were going to lose. Washington decided to distract the Giants by posting thirst traps of Hartman on social media and it clearly worked.

    The next Bachelor 🌹#BachelorNation x #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/xjcyF6Ys6q.

    Hartman is going to go down as the greatest practice squad signing in NFL history.

    Worst pick: Texans over Browns. At the rate things are going, I might have to eliminate the "worst pick" section because I'm not getting any picks wrong. Over the past two weeks, I've gone 25-4 straight-up. The hilarious part is that I'm 0-2 when it comes to picking Browns' games and 25-2 in all other games. I think what I'm trying to say here is that I might have to take a week off from picking Browns games, so there will be no Browns pick this week.

    Finally, if you guys have ever wondered which teams I'm actually good at picking, I'm going to start sharing that information every week from now through the end of the season. Here's a quick look at my best and worst teams when it comes to picks this year.

    The upstart Chicago White Sox have added one of the game's hardest-throwing pitchers to their rotation. Chicago and righty Dustin May have agreed to a three-year contract worth $52.5 million, reports FanSided. The team has not yet confirmed the signing.

    According to recent reports, may, 29, split this past season between the St. Louis Cardinals and World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He threw a career-high 145 ⅔ innings with a 4.70 ERA, though the underlying numbers (3.63 FIP and 4.50 expected ERA) were more respectable. May's 96.9 mph average fastball velocity was 15th highest among the 141 pitchers with at least 100 innings in 2026.

    It has been revealed that rotation help was a priority for a White Sox team that reached the postseason for the first time since 2021, but used openers and bullpen games regularly throughout the season. Only twice in seven postseason games did Chicago use a traditional starting pitcher. Here is the team's updated rotation depth chart:.

    It has been revealed that castillo struggled badly (30 runs in 31 innings) after coming over from the Seattle Mariners at the trade deadline, and finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder problem. His $22.75 million salary could land him in the rotation on Opening Day, though the White Sox have enough options to replace him should Castillo remain ineffective.

    We ranked May as the offseason's 25th-best free agent, and the 11th-best starting pitcher. Here's a snippet of the write-up:.

    According to recent reports, may turned only 29 in September and he's topped 130 innings in back-to-back years after throwing 101 innings total around injuries, including UCL surgery, from 2021-24. Even after the injuries, May still lives in the mid-to-upper-90s with his sinker, and pitch data models are fond of his sweeper and curveball. It is not the best sign, though, that the Brewers, who know pitching as well as any team, couldn't fully unlock May after making him their massive deadline rotation addition. Still, the combination of age and high-octane stuff makes him a nice upside play ...

    May made two starts and three relief appearances during Milwaukee's postseason run. If the White Sox opt to use bullpen games again next year, he is familiar and capable in that role. The signing pushes Chicago's projected 2027 payroll up to $120 million, per FanGraphs, well above the team's $102 million figure this past season.

    The White Sox went 84-78 in 2026 and became the first team in baseball history to reach the postseason after back-to-back 100-loss seasons. They lost 100 games in each of the three previous seasons, going 61-101 in 2023, 41-121 in 2024, and 60-102 in 2025.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Philadelphia 76ers are off to a fantastic start to the 2026-27 season at 12-3, good for first in the Eastern Conference, and perhaps most encouraging for the Sixers is that they're winning without looking like a team playing at its absolute peak.
    • After a huge offseason adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, the Sixers still look like a team figuring out how best to work together, but when it comes time in the fourth quarter to find a way to win, they manage to get the job done.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Philadelphia 76ers are off to a fantastic start to the 2026-27 season at 12-3, good for first in the Eastern Conference, and perhaps most encouraging for the Sixers is that they're winning without looking like a team playing at its absolute peak.

    After a huge offseason adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, the Sixers still look like a team figuring out how best to work together, but when it comes time in the fourth quarter to find a way to win, they manage to get the job done. Tyrese Maxey is leading the way with Brown quickly finding his rhythm, but James and Joel Embiid in particular still seem to be feeling it out early in the season.

    James, who has never averaged less than 20.9 points per game in his previous 23 seasons, is averaging just 15.1 points per game and his 44.3/22.5/71.7 shooting splits are all career lows or close to it. As James figures things out, ESPN reported that a Sixers source claimed James "asked coaches to be patient with him as he expects to find his rhythm and get his conditioning in line by December as he ramps up.".

    That report hit social media and caught James' attention, with the 41-year-old star denying ever saying that.

    Recent findings suggest that ESPN didn't report a direct quote from James, and it's very possible the Sixers source offered an anecdote that paraphrased James and used the word patience when James never did. That then ended up on a social media graphic and prompted James to shoot it down.

    In a recent development, what's fascinating here is it's not a scathing report or even anything particularly juicy. James is struggling with his shot early in the year and seems to be figuring out exactly where he fits in the offense alongside Maxey, Brown and Embiid as a scorer. He's still doing plenty of things well -- including leading the team with 6.9 assists per game and just took over third all-time in assists in NBA history -- and the Sixers are still winning even with James ice cold with his jumper, which history suggests will turn around at some point.

    Patience would be prudent from the Sixers with James, whether he wants to use that word or not, and it seems like a matter of when, not if, he gets shots to start falling and the Philly offense becomes even more dynamic.

    #26838. Six lessons learned from Week 10: Brock Purdy belongs in MVP race, John Harbaugh makes more poor decisions

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1813 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Six lessons learned from Week 10: Brock Purdy belongs in MVP race, John Harbaugh makes more poor decisions

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1813 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • And on the 65th day of the NFL season, everyone finally had a win.
    • The Browns, who watched all of their closest competitors for the final AFC wild card berth fall by the wayside.
    • Over in the NFC, there's a brutal battle.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    And on the 65th day of the NFL season, everyone finally had a win. The Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens wasn't the prettiest football, but the Chargers will find it as beautiful as any. A long flight home after a win feels a little shorter, and in a season that can't end soon enough, Jim Harbaugh and co., at least for one day, have something to smile about.

    Also smiling? The Browns, who watched all of their closest competitors for the final AFC wild card berth fall by the wayside. The only teams within two games -- the Patriots, Raiders and Ravens -- all lost in Week 10 while playing a quarterback who wasn't the Week 1 starter. Add in that the Browns got a crucial win over the Texans, and the AFC playoff picture looks pretty clear.

    Over in the NFC, there's a brutal battle. There are nine teams with winning records. The 6-4 Packers hold the No. 7 seed right now, but after a blowout loss to the Vikings, Green Bay finds the Seahawks and Rams -- also 6-4 -- right there. Lots can and will change, but the next time we see the Rams and the Packers facing off on Thanksgiving Eve, it will be arguably the most notable game of the year to date.

    As the NFC playoff hopefuls scratch and claw, though, they're all looking up at one team, led by one very, very good quarterback.

    Recent findings suggest that so much of Brock Purdy's success gets dismissed as him being a cog in the Kyle Shanahan system. And maybe there were times, earlier in his career, when that was closer to the truth.

    It is no longer remotely close to the truth. Yes, Shanahan set up some easy release valves for Purdy in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys, like getting Christian McCaffrey matched up against Von Miller for the game-winning touchdown (I wrote about Shanahan deserving Coach of the Year on Sunday), but Purdy was truly magnificent. And he has been pretty much all year.

    In a recent development, one play exemplifying this was McCaffrey's first touchdown, when Purdy bought time and, at the last second, found McCaffrey. McCaffrey had been blocking in pass protection just a moment earlier.

    BROCK TO CMC OH MYSFvsDAL on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/JoKDvzWC3K.

    The quick feet in the pocket. The full-sprint escape. The pump fake. The stop. The vision. The throw. This is elite quarterbacking.

    Purdy had several impressive plays like this one, including a 23-yard completion to Keenan Allen on third-and-12 after getting turned around 180 degrees while escaping a sack. This is what has separated Purdy from previous Shanahan quarterbacks: the creativity and out-of-structure playmaking. Purdy's 0.15 EPA per dropback on throws that take 3.5 seconds or more to come out is second, only to Joe Burrow.

    Speaking of Burrow, Purdy won't win MVP, it seems, because Burrow is on a historic heater. He's now a -115 favorite, per DraftKings. Josh Allen is second at +350, followed by Purdy at +425.

    But what Purdy, who has never finished above fourth in MVP voting, is doing with an ever-changing carousel of wide receivers is MVP-level stuff. The film matches the numbers, too.

    Next up? The Vikings -- a huge chance for Purdy to boost his MVP stock. Speaking of Minnesota ...

    We're not just talking about "it looks better," which it absolutely does. We're talking about how Kirk Cousins changes how it looks, as in simply watching the unit moves before the action even happens.

    Under-center, play-action snaps per game.

    Average time to throw (seconds).

    Industry observers note that this is why Minnesota got Cousins in the first place. He does everything Kevin O'Connell wants. He's happy to go under center, hit his back foot and let it rip. He doesn't quite rip it as hard as he once did, but the comfort in the system is evident. In fact, one of his most impressive snaps was him getting through audibles to set up a successful screen pass on third and 12.

    Sources indicate that excellent work from Kirk Cousins pre-snap.All game, the Vikings were trying to take advantage of the numbers game with screen passes. They got a 4x2 advantage, and pulled the OL to keep the numbers on the outside pic.twitter.com/rXVHc17XDh.

    Remember, this is five days after he was traded!

    Recent findings suggest that the Vikings look very different with Cousins, but Cousins looks very different from the last time he was with the Vikings, too. This was the same field on which he tore his Achilles in 2023, when he was playing some of the best football of his career. He had a rough two seasons in Atlanta and a resurgent half-season in Las Vegas. His movement (he even had two scrambles!) looks so much better than it did in 2024 and 2025. Hearing him after the game was a really cool moment, proving that he not only looks at home, but is, in a broader sense, home.

    An emotional Kirk Cousins, in his return to the Vikings at Lambeau Field: “I tore my Achilles here and it’s been a tough three years…” pic.twitter.com/8PhbEVs7Oq.

    The Bengals have long had great wide receivers in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, and we know how good a healthy Burrow is. But after Sunday night's dismantling of the Steelers, we need to talk about how good this offensive line is, too.

    Cincinnati's offensive line stonewalled what's supposed to be a strong Pittsburgh pass rush. Burrow was pressured on just 20.5% of his dropbacks, his lowest rate in over two years. T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith combined for 63 pass-rush snaps ... and ZERO pressures. It's the first time ever both players have been shut out in the same game.

    Recent findings suggest that it's a distant memory now, but the Bengals came into this year wanting to do more under-center stuff to help the run game and the offensive line. But the running game hasn't materialized, and the offensive line simply doesn't need the help of under-center and/or play-action concepts.

    According to recent reports, the Bengals are fifth in PFF's pass-blocking grade this year. They were 26th last year and 29th the year before that. What a huge jump, and in a great year to have one, too.

    Going back to where the week started. The Giants bungled a chance to get closer to putting this division away. Yes, give the Commanders credit where credit is due, but John Harbaugh was a huge part of Newly introduced York's collapse.

    There are two conservative choices Harbaugh made late in the fourth quarter that stand out. The first was fourth-and-1 at the Giants' own 11-yard line with 3:26 left.

    It has been revealed that yes, their OWN 11-yard line. And, yes, they should've gone for it. This is reminiscent of the Lions going for it in nearly the exact same scenario in Week 7, which I wrote about back then. As Dan Campbell explained, he 1) thought his team would convert and 2) knew if it didn't, it would almost certainly get the ball back with a decent chunk of time left. The Lions failed, but Green Bay missed a kick, and the Lions ran the clock out.

    The same applied here, and Jameis Winston has been really good at quarterback sneaks, too, the previous play notwithstanding.

    Instead, Winston barked out his now-infamous "Who let the dogs out?" cadence, and the Giants took a delay-of-game penalty and punted. According to Ben Baldwin's fourth-down decision bot, 101 out of 101 models favored the Giants going for it.

    If you listen to nothing else today, at least listen to Jameis Winston's hard count here lmao 😂 pic.twitter.com/F1nr26EN3W.

    In a recent development, after a Jayden Daniels interception, the Giants again played it safe with three straight runs, including a designed J.J. McCarthy run on third and 3. Sonny Styles sniffed it out for a 2-yard loss; the Commanders had been all over McCarthy's designed runs. Models were split on the fourth-and-5 decision; the Giants punted again, and to make matters worse, Jordan Stout shanked the punt 12 yards. Daniels led the game-winning touchdown drive, and Washington now has life.

    Overall, Harbaugh's conservative decisions -- he had another one in the fourth quarter and one in the first quarter, too -- cost Fresh York about 11.4% win probability, per Baldwin's bot. That's rough. If New York doesn't make the postseason, Winton's silly cadence will re-emerge for all the wrong reasons.

    Fernando Mendoza's first career was the top headline for what ended up being a 21-13 Raiders loss to the Seahawks, but Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald, special teams coordinator Jay Harbaugh and wide receiver Tory Horton teamed up for one of the smartest plays you'll see.

    The effort by the Seahawks special teams to prevent the touchback and keep the clock running 👏SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YF6eTRh4gs.

    Industry observers note that '"Nine yards, 11 inches (into the end zone) -- literally, if there's any way to return the ball, return the ball,'" Harbaugh told his kickoff-return team. 'Burning the two-minute (warning on the kickoff return) is so impactful at that time.'".

    Harbaugh even reminded his unit of that right before it went onto the field, and then Horton defied gravity to do exactly what Harbaugh had asked.

    I love how Macdonald celebrated with Horton. The term "player's coach" is overrated and overused, but Macdonald clearly gets it. So, too does his staff and his team. And for those wondering about "illegal batting," it would have been a 10-yard penalty and a re-kick, which would have occurred within two minutes. Las Vegas obviously declined.

    Recent findings suggest that we've seen so many clock mismanagements, especially on special teams, this season. Getting little details like this right is a sign of a coaching staff and team that's 100% bought in. We'd expect nothing less from the reigning champs.

    Recent findings suggest that there have been 21 games decided by 15+ points over the past three weeks. In the seven weeks before that, there were only 26.

    According to recent reports, we're starting to see the effects of the massive wave of quarterback injuries. The Patriots and Jets both lost their starters during Week 10, and the Cardinals are now on their third quarterback of the year. They accounted for three of the seven losses by 15+ this week. (Steelers, Titans, Packers and Falcons, you have no excuses).

    Sources indicate that this might be the way it is going forward, too. The Colts and the Dolphins played one another in Week 10, but they project as two of the league's worst teams, and they play the Texans and the Bills, respectively, in Week 11. The Cardinals face the Chiefs. Unfortunately, there are just a lot of teams playing out the string already.
