    #26836. MLB rumors: Mets meet with Tarik Skubal, Red Sox getting calls for multiple players, plus Cubs, Red Sox, more

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (899 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    MLB rumors: Mets meet with Tarik Skubal, Red Sox getting calls for multiple players, plus Cubs, Red Sox, more

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the annual GM Meetings came and went last week with two significant transactions.
    • According to recent reports, otherwise, we're still waiting on the winter's first true blockbuster, and the clock is ticking with a lockout expected upon the collective bargaining agreement's expiration at 11:59 p.m.
    • Teams are calling the Rangers about left-hander MacKenzie Gore, who is a year away from free agency, according to The Athletic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the annual GM Meetings came and went last week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some desperately needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.

    According to recent reports, otherwise, we're still waiting on the winter's first true blockbuster, and the clock is ticking with a lockout expected upon the collective bargaining agreement's expiration at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the vital offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Tuesday's hot stove happenings.

    Teams are calling the Rangers about left-hander MacKenzie Gore, who is a year away from free agency, according to The Athletic. There is some reluctance to trade for players with only one year of control because games could be lost to a work stoppage next year, but pitching is so in-demand that at least some clubs are exploring a deal for Gore.

    Recent findings suggest that now 27, Gore is one of only six pitchers to make at least 30 starts in each of the last three years. His under-the-hood numbers (3.87 FIP and 4.19 expected ERA) were much better than his 4.58 actual ERA, plus he has long been considered to have untapped upside. Gore will give you innings, at minimum, and there's a chance his best days are ahead of him.

    The Red Sox are exploring the trade market for righties Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, and Johan Oviedo, according to WEEI. They are also believed to be preparing to trade Jarren Duran, reports MassLive.com. Duran is a potential non-tender candidate if the Red Sox are unable to find a trade partner prior to Friday's deadline. The Mariners and Phillies are among the teams that are "poking around.".

    Crawford, Houck, and Ovideo all missed significant time with injuries in 2026 (Crawford has not appeared in an MLB game since 2024) and are far down Boston's rotation depth chart. Duran has been pushed out of the everyday lineup by the recent Jake Bauers signing. Exploring trades for these four players in a seller's market is a sensible approach.

    Industry observers note that the Mets had an in-person meeting with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Monday, reports the Latest York Post. Owner Steve Cohen and president of baseball operations David Stearns were among those in attendance, according to SNY. Skubal and agent Scott Boras will meet with the Blue Jays, Dodgers, Padres, and potentially two other teams in the coming days.

    Skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Boras clients. Nolan McLean and Christian Scott give the Mets two promising young arms to build around, but they need to improve the rotation around them, and Skubal would give the club a no-doubt ace to lead the pitching staff.

    Industry observers note that the pitching-needy Cubs have shown interest in free agent lefty Trevor Rogers, reports The Athletic. Chicago needs multiple starters this offseason and has cast a wide net in their search. Justin Steele (UCL) and Ben Brown (neck), ostensibly the Cubs' No. 1 and 2 starters, are both recovering from surgeries, and Brown is expected to miss the start of 2027.

    In a recent development, we ranked Rogers as the third-best free agent available this offseason because he is very good as is, and because he'll make analytical models hum with the quality of his arsenal and strike-throwing. Nine pitchers made at least nine starts for the Cubs in 2026 and only two -- Javier Assad and Edward Cabrera -- presently remain under contract/team control.

    The AL East rival Orioles and Yankees are among the teams with interest in free agent slugger Randy Arozarena, according to the Baltimore Banner and Latest York Post. The O's also have some interest in re-signing Luis Robert Jr. Other than Dylan Beavers and maybe Tyler O'Neill, Baltimore's outfield is wide open right now. They have DH at-bats available too.

    It is likely the Yankees checked in on Arozarena out of due diligence more than serious interest. His righty bat would help their lefty-heavy lineup, though he would be a clunky roster fit as a corner outfielder who really needs to DH on a team that already has plenty of corner outfielders who really need to DH. If Arozarena's market is slow to develop, perhaps New York would pounce.

    Teams around the league believe the Rockies are more open to trading All-Star catcher Hunter Goodman now than they were at the trade deadline, reports MLB Network. Colorado is stated to have set a very high asking price for Goodman, who in 2026 became just the tenth primary catcher with a 40-homer season. He hit more homers on the road (25) than at Coors Field (16) too.

    Recent findings suggest that ryan Jeffers and Carson Kelly represent viable free agent alternatives to Goodman as right-handed offense-first catchers, though Goodman is several years younger than both and will have a lower salary the next three years through arbitration. Teams will likely feel more confident in Goodman holding his production for another few years than Jeffers and Kelly.

    #26832. NFL coaching hot-seat rankings: Cowboys' Brian Schottenheimer feeling even more heat

    NFL coaching hot-seat rankings: Cowboys' Brian Schottenheimer feeling even more heat

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2294 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that from 2018 through 2025, October featured at least one coach firing each season.
    • The closer teams get to the end of the schedule, the more likely it is that someone will lose their job.
    • According to recent reports, schottenheimer's seat is hotter now than ever before.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that from 2018 through 2025, October featured at least one coach firing each season. That streak ended in 2026. Even the most embattled coaches made it to the campaign's third month. Heading into Week 11, the only major firing of the year has come at the executive level, with the Indianapolis Colts moving on from general manager Chris Ballard earlier in the season. But it is only a matter of time.

    The closer teams get to the end of the schedule, the more likely it is that someone will lose their job. A cursory look at the standings sheds light on which teams are most likely to see changes in leadership, but not all losing records are created equal. For instance, the Las Vegas Raiders ought to feel optimistic about their future under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak, while the Dallas Cowboys are in a state of disarray with Brian Schottenheimer continually failing to field a competitive defense.

    According to recent reports, schottenheimer's seat is hotter now than ever before. His team just squandered an opportunity to inch closer to a playoff berth in one of the worst defensive performances in a home game in franchise history.

    Sources indicate that dallas' leader is far from alone on the hot seat. Here are the 10 coaches under the most pressure.

    According to recent reports, A team that opened the year at 0-4 and is in an absolute fight to stay alive in the playoff race cannot afford to squander a 17-0 lead. Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Browns was about as disappointing of a defeat as any for the Houston Texans this season, and there have been some heartbreakers along the way, so that is saying something.

    According to recent reports, ryans took over the defensive play-calling duties after the first month of the year, and while the Texans are 3-2 with him orchestrating the unit again, the operation is far from fixed. Over the last three weeks, the defense gave up 27 points to a Deshaun Watson-led Browns team, 22 points to the Los Angeles Chargers and the worst offense in football and 27 points in a loss to J.J. McCarthy and the New York Giants. These are not exactly the most well-oiled operations that are moving the ball against Houston.

    Industry observers note that in the month since New Orleans Saints owner Gayle Benson voiced her frustration with the team and called out coach Kellen Moore by name, the squad is 2-2 with a divisional loss to the Carolina Panthers. Going .500 over four games might be enough to win the NFC South in another down year for the division, but is it really a strong enough product to justify running things back in 2026? It probably will be if the Saints clinch a postseason berth.

    Industry observers note that the final five weeks of the regular season feature all NFC South games and an extremely winnable home date with the Arizona Cardinals, so there is the potential for a strong finish to the year and a run to the division title. But things will probably get worse before they get better. Back-to-back road games against the Chicago Bears and Cincinnati Bengals, and the matchup against the Green Bay Packers that follows, could be disasters for a defense that ranks tied for 24th in points allowed.

    Industry observers note that if Benson were to make an in-season move, a three-game losing streak to those opponents might prompt it. But if not, how the Saints fare against their rivals in the final month will likely determine Moore's fate.

    It has been revealed that cam Ward just turned in two of the best performances of his career, so at least the Tennessee Titans have that going for them. Sustained improvement from the former No. 1 pick quarterback is the main goal for the Titans at this stage of the season now that they are locked into the NFL's basement at 1-8 and have traded away their top defensive assets. Getting the absolute most out of Ward the rest of the way has to be Robert Saleh's top priority, because he probably will not have much else to show for himself.

    One-and-done coaches used to be a relative rarity in this league, but there has been one in each of the last five hiring cycles, and Saleh is the most likely candidate to add to that streak. If he can continue to squeeze promising games out of Ward and the other young weapons, including Carnell Tate (once he returns to the lineup), Saleh will have something to sell to the front office. If not, the Titans might be back in the market for another quarterback come draft time, and they will have to decide whether Saleh is the right person to oversee his development.

    According to recent reports, either the bye week came at an ideal time for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to recharge their defense and ground game for the stretch run, or it will halt their momentum. Todd Bowles had better hope the former rings true, because he will continue to lean on those elements to save his job. There is a chance Baker Mayfield will be unavailable in Week 11 against the Detroit Lions, but it might not even matter at this point for the league's least productive passing offense. The Buccaneers will go as far as their rushing attack takes them.

    In a recent development, bowles has the benefit of playing in the worst division in football. An 0-4 start and a 3-6 record at the bye would be crushing for most teams' playoff hopes, yet here are the Bucs -- just one game out of first place in the NFC South and with a win over the leaders under their belt.

    It is hard to trust a team that relies so heavily on forcing turnovers to string together wins, because takeaways are so unpredictable. The minute their fortunes turn and they stop turning teams over four times a game, this could go back downhill for the Buccaneers.

    It has been revealed that there were no end-of-game snafus from Dan Quinn in Week 10, and what do you know; the Washington Commanders won a one-possession game. If he can stay out of his own way, he has the talent on his side with Jayden Daniels and a still-productive Stefon Diggs to win games like the 24-21 battle with the Newly introduced York Giants. Instead of clock management gaffes and head-scratching play calls, the Commanders dialed up a game-winning touchdown pass with 57 seconds left in a contest that put them right back in the NFC East conversation.

    Success has been fleeting for the Commanders this year, though. They have yet to win consecutive games and remain a game and a half under .500. As soon as they lose again -- an that could happen on "Monday Night Football" against the scalding-hot Bengals -- Quinn will be back under the microscope.

    And as far as contending for the division and a playoff spot goes, Quinn has already used all but one of his opportunities against NFC East foes. He has to take care of business and hope for some help in the way of Giants and Cowboys losses in order to get into first place. And if he cannot do it this year when the division is wide open, will he ever?

    Sources indicate that the first look at the post-trade-deadline Philadelphia Eagles comes in Week 11, when they host the Pittsburgh Steelers for an in-state rivalry game. A lost season could go even further down the drain in that spot, and the Eagles will likely be considerable underdogs the following week when they hit the road to face a Dallas Cowboys team that already beat them by 17. The next best opportunity for a win does not come until December, and the Eagles could be 2-9 by then. Now that they have committed to a rebuild, the question is less about whether this year is salvageable and more about how bad it will look when it is all remarked and done.

    Sources indicate that nick Sirianni earned all kinds of goodwill with his championship season in 2024, two trips to the Super Bowl and five consecutive playoff berths, but he also fell short of expectations last year and is at the helm for what may go down as the franchise's worst season of the century. In a "what have you done for me lately" league, the recent downturn may outweigh the heights of the Sirianni era when it comes time to decide whether he deserves to come back in 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that he finally did it. Jim Harbaugh won a game in 2026. The threat of becoming the first 0-17 coach in NFL history is gone, but the stain of a brutal year will stick around on his otherwise prolific resume unless he is able to capture lightning in a bottle and rattle off a handful more wins between Week 11 and Week 18. Judging by the fact that it took a matchup against a Baltimore Ravens team that started its fourth different quarterback of the year -- one who had only been in town for less than a week -- to get victory No. 1 on the books, a sustained win streak is probably not in the cards for the Los Angeles Chargers.

    In a recent development, even though the run game got out of the mud and Omarion Hampton reemerged as a productive lead back in the win, the offense remains a massive problem and one that will probably continue to plague the franchise so long as Mike McDaniel is calling plays. Harbaugh retained him through the bye week and got a win out of that decision, so the offensive coordinator seems unlikely to go anywhere in the immediate future. A bigger question is whether the front office would give Harbaugh the chance to make an assistant change or if management would prefer to move on from Harbaugh himself.

    Offense will never be a problem for Brian Schottenheimer, but the defensive woes that plagued his first season and a half with the Cowboys just keep getting worse. At some point, Jerry Jones has to decide he cannot put up with the inexplicable lapses on that side of the ball, right? Some of that is his own doing and the result of his personnel moves, but a great deal of it falls on Schottenheimer and his assistants. It reached a upcoming low in Week 10 -- one that might expedite the process of moving on from Schottenheimer and staff.

    Sources indicate that the porous unit wasted yet another gem from Dak Prescott, George Pickens and the offense by surrendering 46 points in the 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. The scoring total marked the fourth-worst performance by the Cowboys defense in a home game in franchise history, and the 584 yards they gave up were the most ever at home. Christian McCaffrey gashed the defense for receiving touchdowns of 74 and 66 yards. Deebo Samuel made the Cowboys look foolish on a 70-yard scoring run on a reverse.

    In a recent development, the defense is undisciplined and uninspired and the main reason why Dallas is not in line to reach the playoffs. Sunday was a prime opportunity to capitalize on the Latest York Giants' latest loss and move within a game and a half of first place in the NFC East. Instead, the gap between the Cowboys and the top of the division looks insurmountable with the way this team keeps playing. That is an utter disappointment.

    Sources indicate that how poetic was it that mere days after the Indianapolis Colts completed their trade deadline fire sale, the remaining players in the locker room banded together for their first win since Oct. 4? Credit to Shane Steichen for motivating them enough to defeat the Miami Dolphins, because everything the front office did in firing general manager Chris Ballard and shipping many of the team's best players out of town indicated that they are punting on this season and looking ahead to the future.

    It has been revealed that there is little reason to think this is more than just a one-week boost, though. Steichen is still a lame-duck coach now that his GM is gone, and he has fewer tools to work with than he did during the 2-7 start to the year. A difficult road ahead spells trouble. Do not forget, too, that the win they just pulled off came at home by a mere two points against a lowly Dolphins team that was without its starting quarterback. Two months from now, the Colts might look back at that win as their last of the season.

    According to recent reports, defensive play-calling is Aaron Glenn's self-proclaimed superpower. He touted the Upcoming York Jets' potential on that side of the ball when he took over the duties at the start of the year. But after just half the season, his powers ran out. Glenn said on Monday that he ceded the play-calling role to defensive coordinator Brian Duker in last week's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

    In essence, Glenn benched himself. It was a deserved move considering the Jets have the ninth-worst defense in EPA per play allowed and entered Week 10 having surrendered at least 26 points in each of their previous four games -- all of them losses. But if a coach with a so-called superpower cannot fix the defense, then why would a change in play-callers get the job done? It is a desperation move for a coach running out of answers and, frankly, running out of time.

    • Bauers, 31, broke out with the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers this past season, authoring a .266/.389/.484 batting line with 26 home runs that more than doubled his previous career high (12).

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Boston Red Sox have made the offseason's first major free agent signing. The Red Sox and first baseman Jake Bauers have agreed to a four-year contract worth a reported $58 million, the team announced on Tuesday.

    Bauers, 31, broke out with the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers this past season, authoring a .266/.389/.484 batting line with 26 home runs that more than doubled his previous career high (12). He was named the NLCS MVP during Milwaukee's title run thanks to a 4 for 14 (.286) effort. Bauers drove in seven runs in the four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers.

    It has been revealed that the Red Sox desperately needed a power bat and certainly added one with Bauers. Their 163 home runs this past season were the fifth fewest in baseball and three players -- Wilyer Abreu, Willson Contreras and Jarren Duran -- accounted for 71 of those 163 home runs. Boston's lineup figures to look something like this with Bauers now added:.

    Sources indicate that that leaves Duran without a full-time position and makes a trade or even a non-tender more likely. Franklin Arias, one of the very best prospects in the minors, could debut early next season and wrestle the shortstop job away from Story. POBO Craig Breslow recently noted Story is not locked in as the team's starting shortstop.

    It has been revealed that we ranked Bauers as the 12th-best free agent available this offseason, and the seventh-best position player free agent. Here's our write-up:.

    It has been revealed that rake Bauers (finally) lived up to the nickname this year and carried it over into the postseason, particularly during the NLCS. Long an exit velocity and hard-hit rate darling, Bauers fully tapped into his power in 2026 thanks to a more open stance and moving back in the box and further off the plate. That allowed him to see the ball better and get his bat into the hitting position on time more consistently. I'm not 100% sold on those adjustments solving his career-long concerns with lefties, though at least there is a tangible reason to believe in his great left-on-left performance this season. Bauers can be an adventure in the field (he has played outfield in the past) and he just turned 31. A few teams will look for the next Jake Bauers rather than pay the actual Jake Bauers.

    The Brewers tendered Bauers the $23.15 million qualifying offer and will receive a 2027 compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million. Because they paid the competitive balance tax, the Red Sox will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in bonus pool money for the 2027 international signing period, to sign Bauers.

    Milwaukee could turn to Tyler Black and Andrew Vaughn at first base next season. Andrew Fischer, the No. 20 overall pick in the 2025 draft, slugged 48 home runs in the minors this summer and reached Double-A. He is the long-term solution at first base but is likely a year away from the big leagues. The Brewers could bring in a stopgap first baseman if they're not sold on Black.

    In a recent development, the Red Sox went 87-75 this past season and were the second wild card team. They were swept by the rival Latest York Yankees in the Wild Card Series and scored only two runs in the two games.

    We're nearly a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while some people say it's too early to start talking about MVP, we are not among those people.

    Right now, it's a clear two-horse race: Luka Doncic or Victor Wembanyama? There is a real split on this. Here's where I stand as of Tuesday, Nov. 17.

    According to recent reports, the Luka Dončić we're watching right now isn't just the best offensive player in the world. He might be the best in history. Nobody has ever put up anything close to the numbers he is charting at the moment: 39 points per game with seven assists, seven boards, nearly two steals and a positively scorching 66.0 TS%, the latter being a number even the great Stephen Curry has only bested twice in his career.

    According to recent reports, it's early, sure. Dončić isn't likely to keep making 3s at this rate for an entire season, and indeed we've seen some slippage of late (35% over his last four, if you really want to split hairs), but his volume remains, with 4.5 makes a night over that stretch. Dončić remains on track to break Curry's single-season record of 402 3-pointers, and he's done more off-ball shooting than in the past.

    Recent findings suggest that throw in more transition production and a 53% midrange conversion rate, per Cleaning The Glass, and you're seeing a more diverse scorer, which is to say this isn't just a guy who has started off hot on his step-back 3s (though this is a major factor, too, of course), but a guy piercing defenses from more spots with different shots. If Dončić could actually be any harder to guard than he has been in the past, we're seeing it this season.

    He's also defending. His 23 steals rank sixth league-wide. Only two players have recovered more defensive loose balls than his eight. Only one has taken more charges than his four. With Dončić as the primary defender, shooters are converting just 36.7% of their shots against a 45.1 expected FG%; that minus-8.6 is the fourth-largest discrepancy among all players who've contested at least 150 shots.

    Most importantly, the Lakers are 12-2 and tied with the Spurs atop the Western Conference. The Lakers rank as the league's top offense with a rating that balloons to 129.2 points per 100 possessions (which would be an NBA record by a long shot) with Dončić on, and a net rating, as illustrated below, that falls off a cliff when he sits.

    Industry observers note that look, if you have Wembanyama ahead of Dončić in the MVP race a month into the season, nobody is going to argue much with you. The oddsmakers slightly favor Wembanyama (+110 at FanDuel; Dončić is +140), who, as you'll see below, has what would qualify as a potentially unanimous case in most years. But this isn't most years. We got a dude averaging nearly 40 points for a No. 1 seed that nobody expected to be a No. 1 seed. Until one of those things changes, it's hard for me to go against Dončić.

    If you think Dončić's plus-35.5 on/off split (it's actually plus-32.2 without filtering for garbage time) is crazy, have a look at Wembanyama's number.

    Victor Wembanyama's impact this season has been another level. Spurs are +42.6 points per 100 possessions with Wemby on the court than off it, according to @cleantheglass. Small sample but other-worldly. Lakers star Luka Dončić is at +35.5 pts/100 poss.Both numbers are better… pic.twitter.com/0GJCFFmZ5K.

    Yes, you're reading that right. The Spurs, for all their supportive talent, fall by 42.6 points per 100 possessions when Wembanyama leaves the court (plus-29.2 on vs. minus-13.3 off), per Cleaning the Glass. By comparison, the best on/off split that Nikola Jokić has ever recorded is plus-24.8. Curry's best is plus-21.3. LeBron James' is plus-17.8. Go down that list and look at the most impactful on-off splits those guys have ever posted. Wembanyama is in another galaxy.

    Sources indicate that and it's vital to note that Wembanyama plays on a great team, as all these guys in the graphic have. The fact that there is still so much difference between when Wembanyama is on the court and when he isn't, even in a small sample, is honestly difficult to comprehend. San Antonio's three-guard lineup was supposed to be an experiment, but it's hard to know if Dylan Harper, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle truly optimize one another or if Wembanyama is enough to make any lineup dominant in spite of traditional complications (like none of those three being a true shooter).

    Wembanyama is the best defensive player on the planet by an immeasurable amount. Even the stats don't do it justice. He's on pace for north of 350 blocks, a number only four players (Elmore Smith, Mark Eaton, Manute Bol and Hakeem Olajuwon) have eclipsed since blocks became an official stat in 1973, and still it's just as much, if not more, about the shots he deters scorers from even attempting.

    In a recent development, and why would they? Scorers are making just 33.6% of their shots when Wembanyama is the nearest defender, a 17% drop from their expected 50.4%. That also leads the league among all players who've defended at least 120 shots, and again, it fails to fully capture his defensive dominance.

    The fact that we've gotten this far without talking about Wembanyama's offense, as if it's a mere afterthought for a guy to be averaging 28.6 points and 11.6 rebounds in under 30 minutes a night. Wembanyama is figuring out his hot spots, prioritizing closer-to-the-basket positioning where he is a skyscraper among regular NBA buildings. He's taking two more paint shots per game than he did last season; 43% of his shots are coming from inside four feet, per Cleaning the Glass, up from 38% last season, and his 4.6 dunks per game (up from 2.7 last year) have him on pace to shatter Rudy Gobert's single-season record of 306.

    According to recent reports, if I had to guess, Wembanyama's production is more sustainable than Dončić's. It's hard to imagine Dončić not hitting a rough patch from 3, and he's almost certainly not going to keep scoring 39 points per game. He'll be over 35 points per game when everything is said and done because that's what the Lakers need from him, but there's a burnout factor while Wembanyama is kind of cruising to these numbers, and the defensive impact is as natural as breathing. My gut states Wembanyama will be a clearer MVP favorite by Christmas.

    Assuming Dončić and Wembanyama each get to the mandated 65 games, everyone else is playing for third place at the moment. Which is crazy given the seasons some of the following names are having.

    Industry observers note that one of two players averaging at least 22 points, nine rebounds and seven assists, and the only player to be leading his team in all three categories. The Rockets are 11-4 with the No. 2 offense and Sengun is the center of it all.

    Recent findings suggest that tatum is averaging his normal 26.5 points per game. The shooting efficiency still hasn't come around, but he is an absolute quarterback on this Celtics team. He draws the doubles, and his 35.1% assist rate, per CTG, is a career high by a mile. The Celtics, for my money, are the best team in the East.

    Sources indicate that here come the Heat, who have won five straight games, with the last three wins coming over the Cavaliers, Pistons and Rockets. Antetokounmpo is averaging 28.3/12.5/5.2 with 1.3 blocks per game on 60% shooting. He's on fire from the midrange as the Heat are exploiting the soft spots in all the drop coverage they're facing.

    It has been revealed that gilgeous-Alexander has so much on his plate that it actually creates a clearer path to a third straight MVP if he can somehow lift Oklahoma City above all these injuries. He's trying. The Thunder are 9-5 and he's getting his 30.9 points per game, but his 58.7 true-shooting is down considerably, which makes sense as he has to force tougher shots now with fewer weapons around him.

    Curry's value can perhaps be felt most in his absence. The Warriors have lost three straight since he went out with a torn oblique, the last two by 59 points. The Warriors have outscored opponents by 13.5 points per 100 possessions with Curry on the floor this season and have been outscored by 8.3 points per 100 possessions without him. Along with Yaxel Lendeborg, who's being asked as a rookie to carry an impossibly heavy weight without Curry, Curry remains the only real lifeblood of a team that is still shockingly lifeless without him.

    Industry News: Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

    📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4130 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.
    • Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.
    • The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

    Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

    The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

    “England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

    Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

    Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

    Leeds manager Daniel Farke noted: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

    “I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

    “He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

    Industry observers note that forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

    Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

    Recent findings suggest that forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a fresh right wing-back before the deadline.

    Industry observers note that newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

    In a recent development, glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

    “For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

    “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

    This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

    Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

    The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

    It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

    Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

    “Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

    Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

    Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

    In a recent development, ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

    You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

    Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

    Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

    The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

    Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a latest forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

    Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

    In a recent development, speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

    Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

    "There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2.

    "It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C.

    Recent findings suggest that and that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

    A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

    A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

    There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

    Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

    There will be six minutes of added time.

    It has been revealed that that just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

    It has been revealed that calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

    Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

    There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

    According to recent reports, the “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

    In a recent development, nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

    It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP.

    Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

    The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

    Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

    Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

    Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

    He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

    There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s fresh-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

    The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

    Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

    Okafor reveals off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

    Sources indicate that chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

    Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

    End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE.

    Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”.

    This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

    Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

    Sources indicate that dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm.

    According to recent reports, nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

    James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

    Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

    A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

    Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

    This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

    According to recent reports, both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

    James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

    Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

    What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ.

    James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

    According to recent reports, reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

    “I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

    “We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”.

    Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke noted: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game.     Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

    Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood.

    The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

    Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

    It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

    Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

    It has been revealed that our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj.

    Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s latest head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

    Recent findings suggest that the Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

    Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Resta la sua obiezione sulla possibilità di votare due volte; alle elezioni del 14 dicembre ci saranno due candidati.

    According to recent reports, adriano Galliani rinuncia al ricorso contro l’ammissione della sua candidatura e guarda al voto del 14 dicembre. A margine del Premio Galbiati, ai microfoni di Sky Sport, ha risposto a Giovanni Malagò, commissario straordinario della FIGC, che aveva definito signorile la sua scelta.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Galliani resta convinto della propria posizione: «Continuo ad essere convinto che non si possa dare un voto due volto. Altrimenti qualunque candidatura può essere tolta all'ultimo minuto. All'improvviso ti viene fatta una revoca e cade la candidatura». Spiega così la decisione di fermarsi: «Detto questo faccio calcio da 50 anni, ho pensato che il nostro mondo ha bisogno di serenità, tranquillità, abbiamo tanti problemi, allora ho pensato di non fare niente e andiamo al 14 dicembre».

    Alla domanda se la rinuncia renderà più serena la campagna elettorale, risponde: «Assolutamente sì, si vota fra 4 settimane, ci sono due candidati e vedremo cosa succede».

    Galliani racconta come ha cambiato idea sulla candidatura: «Avevo detto di no in precedenza. Mi hanno convinto le telefonate, oltre che di qualche club, dell'AssoCalciatori e dell'AssoAllenatori». Aggiunge: «Ulivieri mi ha detto che gli anni migliori per i rapporti con la Lega Calcio, di cui sono stato rappresentante, sono stati secondo lui quando c'ero io. Calcagno mi ha detto il suo maestro, l'avvocato Campana, gli aveva detto a sua volta che i rapporti migliori c'erano quando io ero presidente di Lega. Così mi hanno convinto».

    Sul programma dichiara: «È molto lungo, l'ho presentato e depositato. Ora sono qui per premiare la memoria del grande Baresi e vi rimando al programma, non vorrei parlare troppo tempo».

    Industry observers note that interpellato sulla Nazionale, Galliani risponde: «Non voglio parlare di Nazionale per evidenti motivi, quindi parliamo di Galbiati». Ricorda di averlo trovato al Milan al suo arrivo nel 1986 e di averlo poi voluto a Monza: «Ha insegnato a calciare a Ibrahimovic. Ibra era fortissimo, ma non sapeva calciare in porta, Italo glielo ha insegnato. Poi da talent scout scovava giocatori, ce ne sono pochi bravi come lui».

    Industry News: Yankees' David Bednar, Twins' Ryan Jeffers accept qualifying offer, six others reject $23.15 million QO

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that two players have accepted this year's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m.
    • Sources indicate that an eighth free agent, Jake Bauers, also received the QO.
    • Industry observers note that the five unsigned free agents who rejected the QO are now tied to draft pick compensation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that two players have accepted this year's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET. deadline, and six others have declined the QO. David Bednar (Yankees) and Ryan Jeffers (Twins) are returning to their teams, for the 2027 season, while Randy Arozarena (Mariners),  Brandon Lowe (Pirates), Adrian Morejon (Padres), Trevor Rogers (Orioles), and Seiya Suzuki (Cubs) are all hitting the market.

    Sources indicate that an eighth free agent, Jake Bauers, also received the QO. He agreed to a four-year, $58 million contract with the Red Sox this past weekend. Effectively, Bauers declined the QO. Because they paid CBT in 2026, the Red Sox will surrender their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign Bauers. The Brewers, as a revenue-sharing receiver, will receive a compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million.

    Industry observers note that the five unsigned free agents who rejected the QO are now tied to draft pick compensation. Their former teams will receive a draft pick if they sign elsewhere, and their new teams will be docked a draft pick and potentially international bonus pool money to sign them. The exact compensation depends on the team's revenue sharing and competitive balance tax (CBT) status.

    Here is draft pick compensation the former teams will receive if the seven qualified free agents change teams:.

    Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

    Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

    Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

    CBT payors, like the Red Sox, will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign a qualified free agent. Teams that receive revenue sharing will surrender their third-highest 2027 draft pick. All other teams will surrender their second-highest 2027 draft pick and $500,000 in 2027 international bonus pool money.

    It must be noted that declining the QO does not mean the free agent can not return to his former team. The two sides could still work out a contract of any size and any length, including one worth less than QO, though that is very unlikely. Zac Gallen, Michael King, and Kyle Schwarber rejected the QO last offseason and then later re-signed with their teams.

    Sources indicate that free agents must meet certain criteria to be eligible for the QO. Players cannot have received the QO previously and they must have spent the most recent season with one team, meaning anyone traded in-season is ineligible. The Dodgers could not give Tarik Skubal, far and away the offseason's best free agent, the QO following his midseason acquisition.

    Sources indicate that the QO is set at the average of the top 125 salaries in the most recent season and that is salaries only, not total compensation. For example, the Yankees paid Cody Bellinger a $20 million signing bonus and a $32.5 million salary in 2026. Only the $32.5 million counts toward the QO calculation. This QO was worth a record $23.15 million this winter.

    The current QO system replaced the old free-agent arbitration system in 2012 and will remain in effect this offseason. The upcoming collective bargaining agreement could change the QO system, if not eliminate it entirely. Entering the offseason, just 18 of the 157 free agents to receive the QO accepted it. That count is now at 20 of 165.

    Recent findings suggest that one of the more effective closers in baseball last season, Bednar closed down 35 of 39 save chances with a 2.47 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and 76 strikeouts in 69 ⅓ innings. Having him back on board means the Yankees don't need to find a fresh closer and can look instead to shore up the bridge to the ninth as needed.

    There had been talk that Jeffers wanted to stay with the Twins but that he'd decline the QO and then negotiate a long-term deal. There's still room to reach an extension, of course, but he now doesn't have any leverage from outside offers. It's a massive win for the Twins, with Jeffers resuming his role as the everyday catcher and Victor Caratini serving as the primary backup.

    According to recent reports, jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 (127 OPS+) with 14 homers and 56 RBI is only 92 games last season. He's been one of the most productive offensive catchers in baseball over the course of the last four seasons, when healthy.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that if you simply looked at his touchdown total, you'd think that Derrick Henry had himself a night in the Week 10 finale. The veteran back once again barreled into the end zone multiple times, and even tied LaDainian Tomlinson for the most seasons with at least 10 rushing touchdowns (9) in NFL history. Not too shabby, right?

    Recent findings suggest that well, when you zoom out of the mere touchdown total, you'll find Henry and the Baltimore Ravens ground attack managing just 16 total rushing yards amid a 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night. That led to Henry getting a bit testy in the locker room following the loss that dragged Baltimore to 4-6 on the season and its fifth straight defeat.

    Recent findings suggest that "What were they doing?" Henry asked when questioned about how L.A. was stopping them on the ground, via the Baltimore Banner. "Not letting us run the ball. We weren't efficient enough to run the ball. They were better on that side.".

    When asked whether it was more about the Ravens not executing or the Chargers doing a good job at stopping them, Henry noted, "Everything. Just not doing a good enough job to be efficient in the run game. 16 total yards is a clear explanation.".

    In a recent development, those 16 rushing yards are the third-fewest in a game in team history. They had zero rushing yards in the entire first half. As for Henry, he accounted for 10 of those 16 rushing yards on 10 attempts. When accounting for his five receptions in the loss, Henry averaged just 1.3 yards per touch, which is the fewest this season of any player (233 instances) that has had at least 15 touches in a game.

    This lackluster ground attack on Monday night isn't a one-off for Baltimore. The run game has been virtually nonexistent amid this losing streak, which coincides with Lamar Jackson missing time due to an ankle and right thumb injury. Over the past seven games, Henry has logged zero 20-plus-yard rushes and has failed to have a 10-yard rush in three of his last four games.

    Industry observers note that during this five-game losing skid without Jackson, Henry has logged 81 touches for 246 yards. That 3.0 yards-per-touch average is the fewest of any player in a five-game span in the past five seasons (min. 80 touches), according to CBS Sports Research.

    Again, this has a lot more to do with Lamar Jackson's absence than with Henry falling off. When you subtract Jackson from the equation, it takes the mystery out of Baltimore's running game. No defense fears the like of Tyler Huntley, Joe Fagnano or Jacoby Brissett pulling the ball from Henry and running it himself as they do with Jackson. That allows them to key in on Henry and the ground game even more, especially if they're struggling in the passing attack.

    Here's a look at Baltimore's remaining opponents and how they are against the run so far this season:.

    In a recent development, the Ravens are 4-6 on the season and situated as the No. 10 seed in the AFC playoff picture, looking up at the Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) and New England Patriots (5-5) in the wild card race. They are all looking to unseat either the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) or Cleveland Browns (6-4), who hold the No. 6 and No. 7 seeds entering Week 11.

    If Baltimore can't find a way to rekindle their ground attack, their season may go by the wayside with it and eliminate any reason for Lamar Jackson to return from IR once his broken right thumb heals.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph is on the verge of returning to the lineup. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said during a radio interview on Tuesday that "the plan would be to get [Joseph] going this week" against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, according to The Detroit Free Press.

    According to recent reports, joseph has been out the entire season with a knee injury sustained last year. He played in only the first six games of the 2025 season before being placed on injured reserve. Joseph dealt with the knee injury during the 2025 preseason and played through it early in the year, but he aggravated it and missed the remainder of the year.

    Recent findings suggest that the Lions' defense desperately needs the lift that Joseph can provide on the back end after losing star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the season to a torn ACL suffered in the team's victory over the Latest England Patriots in Munich, Germany. Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye on the first drive of the game and then injured his knee while celebrating the play.

    Detroit's defense has played better of late after beginning the season looking like one of the worst units in the league. The Lions allowed at least 24 points in each of their first four games and at least 30 points in three of them. They also allowed at least 335 yards in each of those games and at least 445 in three of them. Since that point, they have yet to allow more than 21 points or 327 yards, and they have won five straight games.

    In a recent development, it's probably no coincidence that they recently got defensive back Brian Branch back from his injury to solidify one of the spots in the secondary, which has helped limit opponents' ability to attack through the air. The Lions have been excellent against the run during that stretch, though, and their ability to wrangle opponents' run games may now take a hit with Hutchinson out. So, they need the lift that Joseph will provide on the back end to make up for it.

    According to recent reports, detroit's schedule for the rest of the season includes a few tough tests, such as the division rival Bears twice and the Packers in the regular-season finale. However, it also provides some easier games against the Buccaneers (possibly without Baker Mayfield), Falcons, Titans, Vikings and Giants. Joseph's return will surely help them navigate that slate, even if he has to ramp up to a full workload of snaps.

    #26816. Re-grading the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade: Why the Heat and Bucks both look much worse now

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2325 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Re-grading the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade: Why the Heat and Bucks both look much worse now

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2325 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Giannis Antetokounmpo will face the Milwaukee Bucks for the first time as an opponent on Wednesday, but it's a game that feels as though it's a half-decade or more in the making.
    • The Bucks kept kicking the can down the road.
    • Now, Antetokounmpo plays for the Heat while the Bucks are in no man's land.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Giannis Antetokounmpo will face the Milwaukee Bucks for the first time as an opponent on Wednesday, but it's a game that feels as though it's a half-decade or more in the making. The Miami Heat were a rumored suitor for Antetokounmpo, who played his first 13 NBA seasons in Milwaukee, as far back as the buildup to his possible 2021 free agency, which the Bucks averted by trading for Jrue Holiday and ultimately winning a championship.

    The Bucks kept kicking the can down the road. They secured another extension with Antetokounmpo in 2023 by trading for Damian Lillard. They stuck their fingers in their ears and pretended everything was fine when Lillard tore his Achilles in 2025, in the process bypassing the chance to trade Antetokounmpo with multiple years left on his contract when they could have maximized his trade value. In the end, though, Heat president Pat Riley did what he has done so many times before: he got his man.

    Now, Antetokounmpo plays for the Heat while the Bucks are in no man's land. We have around four weeks of data on how these teams are going to look after one of the bigger blockbusters in recent NBA history, so with their first head-to-head bout at hand, let's regrade the trade based on everything we now know.

    Let's start with the obvious positive: despite age- and injury-related fears, Antetokounmpo is still mostly himself. He is, by both the counting stats and the all-in-ones, playing either at the level of his Milwaukee peak or somewhere relatively close. He has at the very least been a top 10 player in the NBA this season, and you could argue him into the top five. Miami paid an All-NBA price and has gotten an All-NBA player.

    There are slight signs of slipping in his age-32 season that merit some examination, though they don't come close to triggering any real alarms. His free-throw rate is lower than it's been since 2018, for instance, but it's still near the top of the league. He's scoring 1.38 points per possession when shooting at the rim -- a very good figure that rates him in the 82nd percentile league-wide, per Synergy Sports. We just judge Antetokounmpo on a curve because he was in the 95th percentile last season and generally hovered around the mid-90s when he was winning MVPs and his 2021 championship.

    Industry observers note that this is, again, not a significant concern. He's still great, and he's supplementing his rim finishing with significant improvement from mid-range. After shooting below 39% from mid-range over the past five seasons combined, he's above 51% so far this season. We can say pretty safely at this point that the 3-point shot is never coming for Antetokounmpo, so this shot will be his pathway to both aging gracefully and combating the walls he'll see at the rim in the playoffs. If this is sustainable, it extends his prime another year or two and makes him close to unguardable while he remains near his physical peak. Thus far, last year's calf injuries have not recurred.

    He's slipped defensively. That's almost undeniable. He contested around nine shots per game when he won Defensive Player of the Year in 2020. He's down to around six this season, and opponents are shooting 6% worse within six feet of the basket against Antetokounmpo than they are otherwise, per NBA.com tracking data. That figure was 20.4% in 2020. The all-in-ones share this basic opinion: still good, no longer great. The tape reveals an older player who paces himself defensively. He can still summon greatness for stretches, but he's not in the All-Defense mix seriously anymore.

    Industry observers note that that brings us to the bigger picture. When you trade as much as Miami did, the question is never just whether the player is good enough to justify the cost, but whether the team is. Heat fans would point to the team's ongoing 8-2 stretch following its 0-4 start to suggest that it was. Count me as a remaining skeptic.

    Sources indicate that most of those victories came against either the bottom of the league -- the Kings, the Jazz, they needed overtime to beat the Clippers! -- or injured opponents. No Tyrese Haliburton in the Pacers win. No Jalen Duren against the Pistons. No Evan Mobley against the Cavaliers. No Amen Thompson against the Rockets, playing the second night of a back-to-back. They've faced only two true heavy hitters at full strength, the Lakers and Timberwolves, and they stood no chance against either.

    In a recent development, the theory of this team relies on a top-five defense. The offense is simply too reliant on shot creation out of its bigs -- Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo -- to be the leading unit for a champion. The early defensive returns have thus far been discouraging, though in fairness, no team has been unluckier on wide-open opponents' 3s. Even during the 8-2 stretch, they're allowing 48.4 points in the paint per game, a well-below-average figure. Their transition defense is nothing special and they're so-so rebounders. They've hung their hat on turnover-generation, but they're by no means elite on that front. The raw numbers are bad. The truth is closer to fine when you factor in luck. They haven't been great, which is what they need to be.

    Sources indicate that part of the problem is that they need to play defensively deficient players -- most notably Klay Thompson and, if he eventually re-earns his rotation spot, Tim Hardaway Jr. -- in order to survive offensively. You can get away with that if everyone else is great. Antetokounmpo has taken a step back. Andrew Wiggins has been a mess. Erik Spoelstra is a defensive miracle worker, but the players here just haven't lived up to expectations. Davion Mitchell has become so notable offensively that even he's slipped a bit on that end.

    Mitchell's playmaking has been a godsend, and a pretty surprising one in context. The Heat tried and failed to get the Bucks to take Mitchell instead of Kasparas Jakučionis in the trade. There's no telling how bad things would be without Mitchell at this stage, but we're still talking about a pretty limited scorer who nearly doubled his 3-point volume and free throw attempt rate in a single season. Miami probably can't expect him to carry this sort of burden forever. Pelle Larsson is more of a connector than a creator in his own right. Down the line, another guard who can create off of the dribble is probably needed here, especially without a strong Antetokounmpo-Adebayo two-man game forming thus far.

    According to recent reports, the paths to improvement here are narrow here. The Heat are pressed up against a first-apron hard cap, and they'd need Charlotte's cooperation to amend the protection on their 2027 selection if they wanted to trade even a single first-round pick at this deadline. It's going to take a little while to meaningfully upgrade the supporting talent here, and the rest of the Heat offseason reflected that.

    Recent findings suggest that they could have perhaps generated the cap flexibility to retain Norman Powell. They elected instead to let him walk, and when they extended Wiggins, they chose to front-load the deal by using his player option rather than spreading the money out to create more immediate hard cap room. Rather than signing a mid-level free agent to a multi-year deal, they added the older Hardaway on just a one-year contract, presumably to maintain optionality going into next summer.

    Sources indicate that if Antetokounmpo were 28, this patience might make sense. He turns 32 in less than a month. The time to go all-in around him is now. It's an ironic middle ground that the Heat have put themselves in. Miami could justify the cost it paid for Antetokounmpo only through immediate contention, yet they're slow-playing the roster build in what you would expect, just based on the standard aging curve, to be the best individual season left in his career. It really doesn't make sense to do this halfway.

    We're talking about the Heat here. They've made the Finals with less talent than they have now, and they are organizationally opposed to intentional rebuilds. There was never a conversation here about, say, trading Adebayo and starting over as opposed to pushing chips in for someone like Antetokounmpo. But if a few years pass and the Heat don't at least make the conference finals with this core, it's going to be worth wondering if that's the path they should have taken. The early returns here are mixed. The Heat bet their future on a single player. He may be good enough to warrant that investment, but the jury's still out on whether their team actually is.

    Recent findings suggest that the Bucks dug themselves an enormous hole by refusing to trade Antetokounmpo when the whole world knew they should have. It was over the moment Lillard tore his Achilles. At that point, Antetokounmpo had two years left on his contract, so hypothetical rental trades would have been feasible. He was younger and he hadn't yet lost a year to calf injuries, so his value was higher. Asset-rich teams like the Spurs and Rockets might have been interested. Had the Bucks moved Antetokounmpo in 2025, they would have gotten substantially more than they wound up getting. Instead, they made the disastrous decision not only to keep him but also to waive and stretch Lillard to sign Myles Turner. Yikes.

    When the Bucks finally realized they'd reached the point of no return, Antetokounmpo, as an expiring contract, had complete control of the situation. At least four teams with strong offers were turned away because Antetokounmpo simply wasn't interested in extending with them, according to ESPN. He only wanted the Heat or Celtics. Given those circumstances, the Bucks still managed the negotiations as well as they reasonably could have. They used the Celtics as an effective scare tactic to compel Miami to give up pretty much all of its available draft capital, plus Jakučionis instead of Mitchell.

    You can win a negotiation and still lose a trade, though, when most of the things the other team had to give in a trade just weren't that valuable. The big swing piece here was Kel'El Ware, an extremely high-risk, high-reward young big man with star-level raw talent and a pretty iffy reputation when it comes to his motor and commitment. The Bucks, thus far, have gotten the worst version of him. He's playing less in his third season with the Bucks than he did in two years with the Heat despite being on the worst roster of his career. He's missing shots everywhere, his defense has been miserable, and if he's ever going to reach that sky-high ceiling, it's probably going to have to come on his third team.

    It has been revealed that that, in a nutshell, is the problem here. The Bucks traded the greatest player in franchise history, one of the 25 or so best players the league has ever seen, and got no one who could credibly be considered a cornerstone moving forward. Ware looks like a swing and a miss. It's too early to say much on Nate Ament, but he's a No. 13 overall draft pick, so odds are, he's going to be fine and not much better. Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez Jr. are both about what they expected, but both will need to be paid next summer. Herro's presence exacerbates a preexisting glut of guards. His presence has forced last year's breakout guard, Ryan Rollins, to the bench. Maybe that makes him a bit cheaper as a free agent next summer. It also probably sours him on a future in Milwaukee.

    Speaking of the guard glut, the Gary Trent Jr. investigation looms large over this trade. The NBA set a notable precedent in the Kawhi Leonard case that it is willing to strip teams of draft picks acquired through trade. This is notable because the Bucks have so little control over their own first-round picks moving forward. The picks they got from the Heat in 2031 and 2033, at least for now, are the crown jewels of this trade. Both of them are theoretically vulnerable if the NBA finds that the Bucks circumvented the salary cap.

    It's even worth wondering if the Bucks should or could have used the Antetokounmpo situation as an escape hatch on any preexisting agreements with Trent, if one actually existed. If the Bucks felt an obligation to pay Trent more than the market suggested he was worth, and if they knew they had so many guards that he was unlikely to factor into their rotation (he played less than 40 total minutes before bizarrely leading the Bucks in playing time in Sunday's loss to the Hawks despite coming off the bench), then why not use the leverage Antetokounmpo's availability granted them to foist Trent on Miami through a sign-and-trade? Of course, if the Bucks had the foresight to do this, they probably wouldn't be in this situation in the first place. For now, the investigation is ongoing and we know little beyond the sheer ridiculousness of the contract itself.

    It has been revealed that the Bucks are 1-13 as of this writing. That, roughly, was to be expected. This was a bad team with Antetokounmpo, so inevitably, removing an MVP candidate was going to make it far worse. But to leave a trade involving a player of that caliber without a single blue-chip player or draft pick is frankly embarrassing.

    The Bucks bungled this Antetokounmpo saga for a year, and even if they managed its end stages properly, they'd dug themselves so deep a hole that there was just no obvious way out of it. Now, it seems they may well have made the situation worse with Trent after the fact. This was an organization-wide debacle.
